More about the role:

As Director, Intelligence & Insight, UK, you will help lead the growth of Burson’s Intelligence & Insights business across a portfolio of priority clients. Reporting to the Head of Intelligence & Insights, UK, you will act as senior counsel to clients and help the team continue to evolve in delivering outstanding value; identifying where intelligence can answer real business and reputation questions, shaping those opportunities into clear briefs, and turning data-led outputs into recommendations that senior stakeholders act on.

You will also play a leading role in how our intelligence offer evolves. Working with the regional Intelligence & Insight hub, product and technology teams, you will identify where our methodologies need to develop to meet changing client needs, and make sure every new approach is clearly tied to the value it delivers. The role requires a strong understanding of the UK communications market, emerging technologies and the commercial potential of data, AI and intelligence in client work.

What you'll do:

  • Growth: Own the growth agenda for intelligence across priority UK clients. Work with client leads to build, shape and convert pipeline, using Burson’s AI suite, wider tech stack and WPP Open platform to address live client challenges. Hold accountability for the revenue and commercial performance of your portfolio.
  • Senior Counsel: Act as a trusted adviser to senior client stakeholders across communications, marketing and corporate affairs. Frame business and reputation challenges, guide decisions with evidence, and lead senior presentations and workshops that demonstrate the value of intelligence.
  • Opportunity Identification: Spot where intelligence can add value across existing accounts and new business. Lead intelligence input to pitches and work with market leadership to position intelligence as a differentiator in winning and growing client relationships.
  • Methodology Development: Identify opportunities to enhance and evolve our intelligence methodologies so they keep pace with client needs. Work with the regional hub and product teams to test, refine and scale new approaches, ensuring each one delivers measurable client value.
  • Team Leadership: Lead, mentor and develop members of the Intelligence & Insight team, and equip account teams to use data and intelligence confidently and commercially. Set clear briefs for the regional hub and hold quality sign-off on outputs.
  • Thought Leadership: Shape Burson’s point of view on data, AI and their application in communications. Contribute to industry publications, speak at conferences and represent Burson as a leading voice in the data and intelligence space.
  • Collaboration: Work closely with the I&I leadership team, account leadership and regional Intelligence & Insight teams to ensure clients benefit from the best of Burson’s data, AI and advisory capabilities.
  • Data Ethics: Ensure all data projects adhere to Burson's data ethics standards and comply with relevant regulations. Promote responsible data practices within the agency and among clients.

Experience that contributes to success:

  • Proven experience in data, intelligence, research or measurement, including senior client-facing roles in a communications agency or consultancy.
  • A proven track record of driving commercial growth, including building pipeline, winning new business and expanding client relationships.
  • Experience counselling senior client stakeholders, with the credibility to challenge thinking and guide decisions.
  • Strong methodological grounding across social, press, search and web analytics, research and measurement, with a record of developing approaches that meet evolving client needs.
  • Deep understanding of the communications market, emerging technologies and the application of data and AI in communications.
  • Ability to translate complex data into clear, actionable recommendations.
  • Experience leading, developing and inspiring teams.
  • Passion for innovation and a commitment to data ethics.

job.title: Senior Account Executive, Digital Media/Content Strategy
job.description:
Who we are:

Burson, part of WPP, is the global communications leader built to create value for clients through reputation. With highly specialized teams, industry-leading technologies and breakthrough creative, we help brands and businesses redefine reputation as a competitive advantage so they can lead today and into the future. When you work at Burson, you are part of a global community of lifelong learners who thrive at the edge of innovation.

WPP (LSE/NYSE: WPP) is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. For more information, visit WPP.com 

For more information visit bursonglobal.com and follow us on LinkedIn and Instagram.

More about the role:

Join Burson’s Digital Experience and Content Strategy team as a storyteller and content strategist who turns complex topics into useful, engaging content for audiences across the digital experience spectrum. In this role, you’ll bring a journalist’s mindset to brand storytelling to support corporate newsroom and owned content creation for major global brands.  

As a Senior Account Executive, you’ll have meaningful ownership of stories from idea through publication. You’ll help write and edit content, coordinate publishing across channels, pitch timely story ideas, and work closely with clients and internal teams to keep projects moving. 

You’ll also use audience insights, search trends, and content performance data to understand what readers care about and identify opportunities to make content more discoverable across traditional search and emerging generative AI and AI-powered search experiences. 

This is an opportunity for someone who loves storytelling but also wants to shape the strategy behind it. You’ll support clients on both ends of the digital editorial strategy process, from maintaining editorial operations and tracking content performance to writing stories and social content, with room to deepen your editorial expertise or grow further into digital strategy and analytics. 

What you'll do:

  • Research, pitch, and write digital newsroom stories that make corporate, business, technology, product, and industry topics clear, relevant, and useful to readers. 
  • Develop compelling story ideas based on company priorities, industry and cultural trends, audience interests, and search behavior.
  • Own stories from initial concept through publication, including research, outlining, drafting, sourcing, factchecking, coordinating through editorial, client, legal, and other review processes, and finalizing for publication. 
  • Apply strong editorial judgment to determine the right angle, structure, level of detail, and tone for each story, including the best images to use from available libraries. 
  • Maintain editorial calendars, story pipelines, and project trackers, ensuring deadlines, responsibilities, and approval stages remain clear and on track.
  • Interview and gather information from client stakeholders, subject matter experts, and other sources to create credible, authoritative content.
  • Serve as a trusted day-to-day client contact for assigned projects, providing timely updates around drafts, deadlines, approvals, potential roadblocks, and next steps.
  • Collaborate with colleagues across content strategy, account management, creative, social, analytics, GEO, and other digital disciplines. 
  • Review content performance through metrics such as traffic, engagement, referral sources, search visibility, and reader behavior to identify what is resonating with audiences. 
  • Turn audience and performance data into actionable editorial recommendations, including new story opportunities and ways to improve existing content. 
  • Help evolve content for an increasingly AI-driven search environment by applying GEO fundamentals including search intent, keyword strategy, headlines, metadata, internal linking, and content structure. 
  • Adapt long-form editorial stories for other digital channels, including LinkedIn and social platforms, tailoring the format and message to each audience. 
  • Contribute additional digital content such as blog posts, executive content, social copy, landing pages, and other brand storytelling as needed. 
  • Stay current on developments in digital publishing, social media, search, generative AI, and corporate storytelling, bringing new ideas and opportunities to the team. 
  • Proactively contribute ideas during editorial planning and brainstorms. 

Experience that contributes to success:

  • At least 3 years of experience writing and editing clear, accurate, audience-focused digital content through journalism, communications, digital media, brand publishing, content marketing, or a related field. 
  • Client-facing or agency experience is strongly preferred. 
  • Strong research and reporting skills, including the ability to quickly understand unfamiliar or technical subjects, identify credible sources, verify information, and explain complex ideas in plain language. 
  • A strong sense of what makes a story interesting and relevant, with the ability to uncover the human, business, cultural, or consumer angle within a corporate topic. 
  • Excellent writing, editing, proofreading, and organizational skills with exceptional attention to detail. 
  • Experience balancing multiple assignments at different stages while keeping deadlines and stakeholders on track. 
  • Comfort receiving and incorporating feedback from multiple reviewers while maintaining the clarity and integrity of the final content. 
  • Strong professional communication skills and the confidence to interact directly with clients and internal partners. 
  • An understanding of how content performs across digital channels and an interest in using audience data and analytics to inform editorial decisions. 
  • Familiarity with GEO fundamentals and curiosity about how search and content discovery are evolving through generative AI and AI-powered search. 
  • Familiarity with basic image editing and selection principles, such as resizing, cropping, selecting the best visuals from libraries, and drafting captions. 
  • Intellectual curiosity and the ability to quickly become knowledgeable about industries, products, technologies, and topics that may be new to you. 
  • Sound judgment around factual accuracy, sourcing, claims, brand reputation, and sensitive corporate topics. 
  • A collaborative mindset and an interest in working across editorial, strategy, analytics, creative, social, and account teams. 
  • The initiative to identify opportunities, pitch ideas, solve problems, and independently move work forward.

  • Drive the team to deliver ahead of time: assign with clarity, follow through relentlessly, and resolve risks before they reach the client.

  • Take on additional responsibilities in support of the practice and its clients as the business evolves.
  • Champion the strategic use of Generative AI tools across all communication programs to enhance planning, ideation, content creation, and operational efficiency.

job.title: Senior Vice President, Corporate Affairs, Health Policy - Burson
job.description:
Who we are:

Burson, part of WPP, is the global communications leader built to create value for clients through reputation. With highly specialized teams, industry-leading technologies and breakthrough creative, we help brands and businesses redefine reputation as a competitive advantage so they can lead today and into the future. When you work at Burson, you are part of a global community of lifelong learners who thrive at the edge of innovation.

WPP (LSE/NYSE: WPP) is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. For more information, visit WPP.com 

For more information visit bursonglobal.com and follow us on LinkedIn and Instagram.

More about the role:

Burson is seeking a Senior Vice President, Health Policy and Public Affairs, to lead one of the agency's most strategically important global healthcare accounts.

This role serves as the senior strategic counselor to client leadership across a portfolio of marketed and pipeline therapies in neurology and rare disease. The EVP will lead multidisciplinary teams responsible for patient advocacy engagement, access and reimbursement policy, stakeholder mobilization, executive visibility, corporate reputation and issues management.

The successful candidate will possess deep healthcare public affairs expertise, exceptional stakeholder engagement experience, and a strong understanding of the evolving policy, regulatory, reimbursement and market access environment impacting innovative medicines globally.

This leader will work at the intersection of science, policy, patient need and reputation, helping shape conversations among patient organizations, professional societies, policymakers, healthcare providers, caregivers and advocacy stakeholders while ensuring communications and engagement strategies support both long-term corporate reputation objectives and product-related priorities.

The ideal candidate combines the strategic instincts of a public affairs leader, the stakeholder expertise of a patient advocacy professional, and the business acumen of a senior agency executive. They are equally comfortable discussing healthcare policy with government stakeholders, scientific innovation with medical leaders, reputation strategy with the C-suite and patient priorities with advocacy organizations.

Most importantly, they understand how policy, science, access, patient advocacy and reputation intersect, and can help global healthcare organizations navigate that complexity to create meaningful impact for patients, caregivers and society.

This Hybrid role is ideally based in New York and Washington DC. 

What you'll do:

Strategic Client Leadership

  • Serve as senior strategic counselor to global and regional client leadership teams.
  • Lead integrated public affairs, corporate reputation and stakeholder engagement programs across neurology and rare disease portfolios.
  • Shape strategic communications approaches that connect policy, patient advocacy, access and reputation objectives into a cohesive narrative.
  • Develop executive-level recommendations informed by evolving healthcare, political, reimbursement and regulatory environments.
  • Act as the primary escalation point for complex business, reputation and policy challenges.

Public Affairs, Policy & Access Leadership

  • Lead policy and advocacy strategies addressing market access, affordability, reimbursement and healthcare system priorities.
  • Counsel clients on emerging U.S., European and global policy developments affecting innovative medicines.
  • Monitor and advise on pricing, reimbursement and trade-related policy developments, including initiatives such as Most Favored Nation (MFN) pricing models, international reference pricing and healthcare cost-containment efforts.
  • Translate complex policy developments into impactful engagement and communications strategies.
  • Partner with policy experts, economists and scientific leaders to develop evidence-based advocacy initiatives.

Patient Advocacy & Stakeholder Relations

  • Build and strengthen relationships with patient organizations, advocacy coalitions, caregivers, healthcare professional associations and disease community leaders.
  • Design and implement engagement strategies that elevate patient perspectives throughout the disease lifecycle.
  • Identify opportunities for trusted partnerships that advance awareness, access, education and health outcomes.
  • Guide stakeholder mapping and influence strategies across advocacy, policy and medical communities.
  • Ensure patient-centered engagement approaches are integrated across all programs.

Neurology & Rare Disease Expertise

  • Provide strategic counsel across brain health, neuroscience and rare disease areas.
  • Help clients advance a more integrated and holistic view of brain health that addresses patient outcomes, access, caregiver needs, public awareness and policy considerations.
  • Develop reputation and thought leadership platforms supporting both established therapies and future innovation.
  • Counsel clients on scientific milestones, breakthrough therapies, disease awareness efforts and emerging healthcare trends.
  • Support launch readiness and lifecycle communications for pipeline and marketed assets.

Issues & Reputation Management

  • Lead proactive reputation management and complex issues preparedness initiatives.
  • Develop risk assessments, scenario planning exercises and stakeholder response frameworks.
  • Counsel executives during periods of heightened scrutiny involving pricing, access, clinical development, regulatory matters or public policy debates.
  • Ensure consistency of corporate and product-related narratives across stakeholder groups and geographies.
  • Protect and strengthen organizational reputation during critical moments.

Regulatory & Commercialization Strategy

  • Advise clients throughout the therapy development lifecycle, including:
    • Clinical development and trial communications
    • Regulatory milestones
    • FDA and global regulatory approval processes
    • Launch readiness
    • Market access preparation
    • Lifecycle management
  • Partner with scientific, medical and market access teams to connect innovation stories with stakeholder priorities and policy realities.

Business Leadership & Team Development

  • Lead and inspire cross-functional account teams across multiple markets.
  • Drive account growth through expansion opportunities and strategic advisory services.
  • Contribute to new business efforts across the health and public affairs sectors.
  • Mentor and develop senior talent while fostering a collaborative and inclusive culture.
  • Strengthen Burson's intellectual capital across healthcare public affairs, patient advocacy and reputation management.

Experience that contributes to success:

  • 15+ years of experience in healthcare public affairs, policy, corporate communications, government affairs, market access, advocacy or related disciplines.
  • Significant experience counseling pharmaceutical, biotechnology or healthcare clients on complex public affairs and reputation issues.
  • Demonstrated expertise in neurology, neuroscience, rare disease, specialty pharmaceutical or adjacent therapeutic areas.
  • Deep understanding of healthcare policy, pricing, reimbursement and access environments in the United States and internationally.
  • Experience developing and executing stakeholder engagement strategies involving patient advocacy organizations, healthcare professional associations, policymakers and caregiver communities.
  • Strong familiarity with FDA approval pathways, clinical trial communications and pharmaceutical commercialization strategies.
  • Proven experience supporting both marketed products and clinical-stage pipeline assets.
  • Knowledge of European and/or global healthcare policy environments and stakeholder ecosystems.
  • Exceptional executive presence and ability to counsel C-suite and senior healthcare leaders.
  • Experience leading large, multi-market client engagements and cross-functional teams.
  • Demonstrated success managing complex reputation and issues management situations.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working within global pharmaceutical companies, healthcare trade associations, public affairs consultancies or communications agencies.
  • Understanding of rare disease and neurological policy frameworks within key international markets.
  • Familiarity with health technology assessment (HTA), reimbursement decision-making and payer environments.
  • Experience engaging with organizations such as patient advocacy coalitions, specialty medical societies, health policy organizations and caregiver networks.
  • Exposure to global market access, international pricing policy and cross-border regulatory considerations.

Burson is an equal opportunity employer and considers applicants for all positions without discrimination or regard to particular characteristics. We are committed to fostering a culture of respect in which everyone feels they belong and has the same opportunities to progress in their careers.

job.description:

For more information, visit WPP.com 

For more information visit bursonglobal.com and follow us on LinkedIn and Instagram.

Qui sommes-nous:

Burson, leader mondial de la communication, a pour mission de créer de la valeur pour ses clients par la gestion de leur réputation. Grâce à notre expertise, nos technologies de pointe, nos solutions d'intelligence artificielle et notre créativité, nous anticipons les risques en temps réel, identifions les insights générateurs de préférence et d'engagement, et accompagnons la transformation et la réussite de nos clients. Nous réinventons la réputation pour en faire un véritable atout concurrentiel. Burson est le gardien de votre réputation, le partenaire qui vous guide dans un environnement complexe.

En rejoignant Burson, vous intégrez une communauté mondiale d'experts à la pointe de l'innovation.

Burson fait partie du groupe WPP (LSE/NYSE : WPP), spécialiste de la transformation créative. Pour en savoir plus, rendez-vous sur bursonglobal.com et suivez-nous sur LinkedIn et Instagram.

En savoir plus sur le rôle:

Stage conventionné à pourvoir à partir de février 2027.

Missions :

Au sein de l’équipe Lab IA & Data de Burson France, vous contribuerez à des missions variées pour des clients de divers secteurs d’activité, en exploitant notamment des outils et des méthodologies propriétaires basés sur l'intelligence artificielle ou intégrant des composants IA :

  • Veille réputationnelle et reporting quotidien
  • Analyse des conversations en ligne (tendances, produits, marques, entreprises, etc.)
  • Benchmark de communication (concurrentiels, tendances, social media, etc.)
  • Conduite d’études et analyses (analyse quantitative et qualitative, recherche d’insights, élaboration de pistes stratégiques)
  • Décryptage et cartographie de débats/sujets (arguments, acteurs en présence, évaluation de la sensibilité, etc.)
  • En new bizz, analyse qualitative sur un marché, une marque ou une problématique

Vous serez formés aux outils et méthodologies de l’agence, incluant nos plateformes basées sur l'IA.

Profil recherché :

  • Étudiant(e) en communication, sociologie, sciences humaines, lettres, sciences politiques – Master 1 ou 2. Les candidats au profil purement data analyst ne correspondent malheureusement pas à nos attentes pour ce poste.
  • Curiosité pour les réseaux sociaux et les enjeux d’opinion
  • Forte appétence pour la recherche, l'analyse de données et l’IA
  • Bonne culture générale
  • Qualités rédactionnelles, esprit de synthèse et rigueur
  • Français courant et bon niveau en anglais

Notre engagement :

  • Stage professionnalisant avec encadrement personnalisé, vous permettant de travailler avec des outils de pointe intégrant l'IA
  • Suivi régulier avec votre tuteur/tutrice
  • Retours constructifs sur vos missions
  • Découverte des différentes facettes du métier d'insights analyst, enrichies par les dernières innovations en IA.

  • Gratification : 750€/mois
  • Télétravail possible et éligibilité à la prime de télétravail (10€/mois)

  • Prise en charge des repas au restaurant d’entreprise (reste à charge de 3,70€)

Ces talents sont essentiels pour concevoir des idées audacieuses, favoriser un dialogue constructif, créer des expériences enrichissantes et stimuler l'innovation pour nos clients. More about the role:

Burson is seeking a highly organised, proactive and detail-oriented Team Coordinator to join our team in South Africa, primarily supporting the JLR EMEA account. The role will focus on managing end-to-end travel and logistics across the region, including travel arrangements, accommodation, itineraries and event coordination, alongside broader account administration and operational support.

Working closely with JLR stakeholders, regional teams and travel partners, you will take ownership of travel and logistics requests from start to finish, ensuring arrangements are seamless, timely and well-coordinated. You will also support wider account operations by proactively managing follow-ups and keeping stakeholders informed. Strong organisational skills, attention to detail and responsiveness during core European working hours will be essential to success in this role.

What you'll do:

  • Act as a key point of contact for travel and logistics requirements across the JLR EMEA account, supporting employees and stakeholders with travel-related queries and requests.
  • Manage & coordinate end-to-end business travel across EMEA, including flights, accommodation, ground transportation, visas where applicable and travel itineraries, working closely with travel agencies and partners.
  • Take ownership of travel and logistics requests from initial enquiry through to completion, managing bookings, amendments, cancellations, approvals and resolving issues while keeping stakeholders informed.
  • Coordinate logistics for team meetings, events, conferences and regional activities, including venues, catering, transportation and other practical arrangements.
  • Support wider JLR account operations by maintaining trackers, coordinating meetings, monitoring actions and following up on key deliverables and deadlines.
  • Work closely with regional market and brand teams to support day-to-day coordination, facilitate communication and ensure the smooth running of account activities across EMEA.
  • Provide general team coordination and administrative support, including diary assistance, meeting coordination, document preparation and ad-hoc operational requirements.
  • Maintain a proactive and responsive approach during core European working hours, particularly when managing time-sensitive travel arrangements, event requirements and live operational issues

Experience that contributes to success:

  • Excellent organisational and planning capabilities, with the ability to manage competing priorities, multiple requests and tight deadlines effectively.
  • Proven experience in travel management and coordination, administration or operations, ideally supporting regional teams across multiple countries and markets.
  • Demonstrated experience liaising with travel agencies, suppliers and external service providers to manage travel arrangements and resolve issues.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy when coordinating complex travel itineraries, bookings, schedules and documentation.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to proactively manage requests, drive follow-ups and take ownership through to completion.
  • Ability to work effectively across different countries, cultures and time zones, demonstrating flexibility and responsiveness during core European working hours.

job.title: Health Reporter and Multimedia Journalist
job.description:
OVERVIEW:

WRAL News is seeking a Health Reporter and Multimedia Journalist (MMJ) to lead coverage of the health stories that matter to families in the Triangle and across North Carolina. The role focuses primarily on health journalism, from breaking news and public health emergencies to original reporting on medical research and access to care. This full-time position works across WRAL-TV, WRAL.com, mobile apps, WRAL News+, YouTube and social media. The reporter also supports grant-funded coverage, including recurring health explainers and audience growth reporting.

KEY RESPONSIBLITY AREAS: 

  • Own breaking health news, including outbreaks, exposure alerts and public health emergencies. Monitor alerts, official sources and tips, coordinate with the assignment desk, and deliver verified live reports and updates as stories develop.
  • Develop sources among public health officials, clinicians, researchers, patients, caregivers and community organizations. Use public records, data and independent experts to verify claims, put findings in context and pursue accountability stories.
  • Pitch and produce daily and enterprise stories on emerging research, prevention, treatment and access to care. Answer timely audience questions and explain what developments mean for patients and families.
  • Help launch recurring, in-depth health explainers within the first six months of the grant agreement. Produce them for WRAL.com, YouTube and other WRAL platforms.
  • Independently shoot, write, edit and file stories for WRAL-TV, WRAL.com, mobile apps, WRAL News+, YouTube and social media. Report live from the field and studio, conduct interviews and use graphics to clarify data, findings and timelines.
  • Adapt reporting to each platform, including clear TV scripts, digital articles, longer YouTube explainers and short social video. Follow AP style and WRAL editorial and production standards.
  • Work with producers, photographers, editors and digital teams to publish stories in the WRAL.com Health section, give major breaking health stories prominent homepage and social placement based on news value, and showcase coverage in WRAL’s most-watched newscasts.
  • Maintain a record of grant-supported coverage across platforms, including recurring explainers. Log story links, topics, platform placement, available audience and engagement metrics, and time spent on assignments outside the health beat.
  • Work with newsroom leadership to prepare quarterly updates for grant funders using the coverage log. Establish an audience baseline from initial results and report progress on pageviews, video views, watch time and engagement.
  • Pitch and produce original digital health stories that give audiences more depth and practical context. Use audience data to guide follow-up coverage and grow reach across WRAL platforms.
  • Performs other duties as required or assigned, provided they are reasonably related to the responsibilities outlined in this job description.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in journalism, communications or a related field, and at least two years of TV newsroom experience as a reporter, MMJ or in an equivalent role.
  • Ability to independently shoot, write, edit and publish accurate, visually clear stories on deadline.
  • Proficiency with ENPS, Edius, FTP and mobile live transmission tools, along with digital publishing and social video tools.
  • Strong news judgment, interviewing and source development skills.
  • Familiarity with media law, journalistic ethics and public records, and the ability to explain complex health information clearly and accurately.
  • A valid driver’s license and clean driving record.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Live reporting experience is strongly preferred.


Work Conditions: 

  • This field-based role includes studio work as needed, irregular hours, nights, weekends, holidays and on-call breaking news response. Occasional assignments outside the health beat may include major breaking news or weather coverage, major station projects or events, and holiday or vacation relief. A valid driver’s license and clean driving record are required.

    Other duties as assigned.

Benefits:

  • Competitive salary based on experience.
  • Benefits package including:
    • Comprehensive health insurance plan options
    • Vision and Dental Insurance
    • Company sponsored life insurance
    • Numerous voluntary benefit options – legal plans, pet insurance, discounted home and auto and more!
    • 401K with company match
    • Generous paid time off
    • 9 paid company holidays
  • Opportunities for professional development and career growth.
  • Dynamic and inclusive work environment with a supportive team culture.
  • Exciting projects and growth opportunities within a leading organization.
  • Opportunities to attend free local events, such as sporting events, concerts, shows, and more.

Pre-Employment Information:

  • A pre-employment drug screening is required.
  • Capitol Broadcasting Company participates in E-Verify.
  • Capitol Broadcasting Company participates in the Work Opportunity Tax Credit (WOTC) program. However, completing the WOTC questionnaire is completely voluntary. Your decision will have absolutely no impact on your hiring chances, and your application WILL be accepted regardless of whether you choose to provide this information or not.

EEO Statement:

Capitol Broadcasting Company is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and applicants. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

CBC Statement:

Capitol Broadcasting Company, Inc. is a diversified communications leader which owns and/or operates WRAL-TV, WRAZ-TV, WRAL News+ (WNGT-CD), WRAL-FM, WRAL-HD2, WCMC-FM, WCMC-HD1, WDNC-AM, WCMC-HD2, WCMC-HD3, WCMC-HD4, Microspace Communications, and Capitol B Creative in Raleigh, NC; WILM-TV, WILT-LD and Sunrise Broadcasting in Wilmington, NC; The Durham Bulls Baseball Club, Bull City Hospitality, and the Coastal Plain League in Durham, NC; The Holly Springs Salamanders in Holly Springs, NC; the Zebulon Devil Dogz in Zebulon, NC; the American Underground startup hub and workspace in Durham, NC; and real estate interests including the American Tobacco Historic District in Durham, NC, and Rocky Mount Mills in Rocky Mount, NC.

You love coming up with creative treatments for all platforms, including digital and social.  And you are experienced in gathering sound and images in the field, and weaving those elements into a compelling story arc.

Behind the scenes, but ahead of the curve: help us develop the next-generation public service media organization.

 

Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. Our purpose is to constantly innovate to evolve and maintain the Corporation’s technology and infrastructure. We are the people that make stuff work. We make connections between media content, systems, people and places. We are the space in between.

 

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology — not just in Canada but around the world. Today, we are transforming ourselves into a modern and agile public service media organization. Technology is the driving force, and we are the team making it happen.

 

This role requires full-time on-site presence.

 

Role

 

You are responsible for coordinating the use and ensuring the continuity of acquisition, feed and communication resources for CBC/Radio-Canada networks and external clients. You distribute the signals of programs or program segments, ensuring quality control.

 

Description of Duties

  • Check audio, video, captioning and communication signals for programs or program elements across the entire Radio-Canada distribution system, including those from outside distribution companies (e.g., cable operators, satellite signal providers), along with all technical equipment (e.g., VTRs, servers, external links, internet); make corrections if they are not compliant with standards.
  • Draft reports on irregularities and inform the relevant people.
  • Adjust, test, set up and operate technical equipment (e.g., VTRs, servers, broadcast graphics, digital delay), ensuring everything is clean, secure and in good working order.
  • Contact telecommunications companies to resolve transmission and reception problems.
  • Apply solutions in case of technical failures; coordinate operations necessary to maintain service quality and continuity, and report on your work.
  • Perform tasks involved in operating equipment and making connections as required by schedules or network programming.
  • Adjust Control Centre activities to provide required signals and feeds, reporting any changes or errors and implementing corrections.
  • Receive requests for terrestrial circuits or satellite channels, obtain pricing and place orders with providers.
  • Coordinate and determine the necessary connections for terrestrial circuits, mobile microwave links and satellite channels, and manage the assignment of distribution channels (RF) and common station elements.
  • Ensure the proper operation of satellite dishes, receivers/decoders and transmitters, and communicate any changes to satellite channel assignments.
  • Establish communication links for signal transmission and reception, conduct technical tests and maintain the necessary contacts.
  • Ensure that the return signal for each network broadcast by Radio-Canada is recorded for CRTC purposes.
  • Authorize and initialize Radio-Canada decoders/receivers based on regional and management requests.
  • Record programs, commercials and promos; check their accuracy and technical quality; and take corrective action in case of non-compliance.
  • Route and feed news exchange content from servers, VTRs or other sources to regional stations.
  • Import elements and perform conversions to various file formats for incorporation into edited sequences.
  • Manage disk space by deleting or archiving content associated with your work.
  • Advise technical and production staff on how to resolve issues and/or achieve desired results.
  • Review and apply technical plans and diagrams.
  • Assist in reviewing or developing operating methods and technical standards.
  • Note all relevant information in a log to ensure the required follow-up actions and continuity; consult the log daily.
  • Complete the appropriate forms and documents; share information to ensure proper follow-up and to keep others informed.
  • Familiarize other employees with their duties and the work environment.
  • Carry out, as needed, the duties of another job classification within an equivalent or lower salary group, as well as other related duties.

 

Job Requirements

  • Education or equivalent knowledge: College diploma (DEC) in television production and/or post-production techniques, or any other relevant diploma.
  • Prior experience: Three years’ experience required to perform duties satisfactorily.

  • Interview.

The Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) team is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. Our purpose is to constantly innovate to evolve and maintain the Corporation’s technologies and infrastructure. We are the people that make stuff work. A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology — not just in Canada, but around the world. Today, we are transforming ourselves into a modern and agile public service media organization. Technology is the driving force, and we are the team making it happen.

 

This is a hybrid role with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

 

Role Overview

 

This role serves as a strategic bridge, functional reference, and provides advanced analysis for our corporate tools portfolio. Its primary focus is on maximizing user adoption, understanding, and safe usage of our core productivity tools, including the Google Workspace ecosystem, and its rapidly evolving AI capabilities.

 

Moving dynamically between business strategy and technical evaluation, you will be responsible for demystifying AI, scoping business needs, and participating in pilot projects primarily within Google Workspace, but also across the full suite of productivity tools. Furthermore, you will collaborate with other Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) support teams for enterprise platforms such as Workday or Oracle as needed to ensure strategic alignment in the use of AI.

 

You will act as a technology scout and functional tester, ensuring teams understand how to use new tools effectively. With a strong technical background and a focus on increasing organizational productivity, you will evaluate new AI capabilities, deliver engaging training, and participate in cross-functional risk mitigation procedures to ensure secure and compliant rollouts.

 

Key Responsibilities

 

  • Tech Watch, Testing & Functional Configuration
    • Feature Evaluation & Tech Watch: Track the fast-moving AI market, acting as a technology scout for upcoming generative and agentic AI capabilities embedded primarily within the Google ecosystem, assessing other systems like Workday and Oracle as needed.
    • Functional Testing & Test Documentation: Actively test new AI features (such as Workspace Studio, NotebookLM, and Gemini) within sandbox or Alpha environments as soon as they are announced, evaluating user experience, functional limitations, and integration risks. Meticulously document all test plans, execution steps, and outcomes to maintain a clear and reliable functional knowledge base.
    • Technical Configuration & Issue Tracking: Build master templates and configure advanced operational setups (such as automated project structures or intelligent workflows) to support business pilots. Provide specialized guidance for advanced Google products, utilizing scripting where necessary to automate simple workflows. Create, manage, and escalate technical tickets effectively to track bugs, vendor issues, and user feature requests.

 

  • User Adoption, Training & Enablement
    • Driving Adoption & Productivity: Develop and execute strategies to champion the active user adoption of AI tools across the business. Build awareness around enterprise-approved tools while guiding and migrating users away from unapproved tools toward Google Workspace and other supported solutions. Identify opportunities to leverage technology to streamline daily tasks, eliminate bottlenecks, and significantly increase overall workforce productivity.
    • Documentation & Translation: Translate complex vendor release notes and technical evaluations into clear, easy-to-understand functional impact analyses and plain-language user guides.
    • Training & Upskilling: Design and deliver engaging training sessions and workshops to raise the overall AI literacy of employees, acting as an expert to help productivity teams understand how various corporate AI tools intersect.
    • Best Practices Watch: Observe how peer media organizations or similar enterprises use AI in their daily operations.

 

  • Cross-Functional Support & Risk Mitigation
    • Governance Participation: Assist in partnering with internal compliance teams (Legal, Privacy, InfoSec, Accessibility) to ensure corporate AI tools meet enterprise standards. Help prepare functional impact analyses for governance committees, shaping corporate policies without leading the committees.
    • Risk Mitigation: Support the ongoing monitoring of automated vendor updates and the execution of deployment strategies designed to protect sensitive organizational and personal data.

 

  • AI Pilots, Accelerators & Special Projects
    • Business Analysis & Scoping: Partner directly with diverse business units to identify practical AI opportunities, translate complex user requirements into actionable functional use cases, and scope corporate special projects.
    • Pilot Deployment & Value Tracking: Support the analysis and deployment of "AI Accelerator" pilot projects. Define, monitor, and measure business success metrics (such as workflow simplification or time saved) to assess the real-world return on investment for corporate tool AI initiatives, ensuring pilots directly contribute to increased business productivity.

 

Qualifications & Ideal Profile

  • Minimum of 10 years of experience as a Business Analyst, Functional Analyst, Product Owner, or in a similar role.
  • Highly organized and detail-oriented, with a rigorous approach to documenting processes, managing tickets, and maintaining project structures.
  • Demonstrated passion for driving user adoption, change management, and leveraging technology to increase organizational productivity and efficiency.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Communications, Information Technology, or a related field (or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience).
  • Strong technical knowledge of Google Workspace and its core applications, combined with AI literacy and a sharp ability to rapidly leverage AI tools.
  • Fluency in both French and English, with exceptional written and verbal communication skills in both official languages.
  • Comfortable speaking in front of groups, delivering interactive training sessions, and producing clear, high-impact reporting for executive stakeholders.
  • Proven track record of conducting thorough business process analysis, testing tools, and mapping complex workflows.
  • Demonstrated experience collaborating with legal, privacy, security, or accessibility partners, with the diplomacy needed to balance user innovation against corporate risk frameworks.

This is a hybrid role with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

Your Role


CBC/Radio-Canada is seeking a Lead Analyst, Data Protection Specialist, to design, lead and evolve the Corporation’s data security program. 

In this role, you will provide technical and operational leadership to safeguard sensitive data and personal information throughout the data life cycle (collection, processing, storage, transmission, archiving and destruction). You will collaborate closely with Legal Services, privacy officers, enterprise architects and IT Operations to align data security with regulatory requirements and industry standards.

This position can be based in Montreal or Toronto.

What’s in It for You

Challenges. We spend our days solving problems of all kinds. Media files are highly nuanced and incredibly complicated; updating, installing and supporting technologies that are organization-wide and that impact broadcasting content is a time-sensitive, complex technical feat. And that’s just the beginning. You’ll be working with leading-edge data management, cloud, IP broadcasting, AI, security and reliability technologies.

As Lead Analyst, you will:

  • Define data security strategy: Develop and refine the road map for the Corporation’s data protection program.
  • Implement data classification: Establish and deploy data classification policies and frameworks.
  • Administer data protection technologies: Select, deploy and optimize data loss prevention (DLP) tools.
  • Protect cloud and hybrid environments: Design security controls tailored to cloud-hosted data and hybrid architectures.
  • Partner on compliance and policy frameworks: Work closely with the policy, compliance and legal affairs lead to align security controls with statutory requirements.
  • Manage the data security risk register: Document, maintain and map risks related to confidentiality, potential data breaches and approved exceptions.
  • Adjudicate and govern exception requests: Evaluate, document and follow up on exception requests when standard security controls cannot be immediately applied, ensuring appropriate compensating controls are established.
  • Lead data breach response: Actively participate in investigations of suspected or confirmed data breaches in co-ordination with the Information Security, Legal Services and Incident Response teams.
  • Develop metrics and dashboards: Define and track key performance indicators (KPIs) and key risk indicators (KRIs) to monitor program effectiveness.
  • Assess program maturity: Plan and conduct periodic evaluations, performance reviews and audits of data protection controls to identify gaps, measure maturity progress and formulate recommendations for continuous improvement.
  • Maintain industry expertise: Stay current on information security best practices and industry trends.

What You Bring

  • University degree in computer science, IT or information security.
  • Minimum five years’ experience in data protection, privacy security, DLP or data governance, including at least three years in an information security role.
  • Proven track record of implementing and evaluating technical data protection programs within large, complex organizations.
  • Deep technical expertise in data protection, including cryptography (encryption at rest and in transit, PKI), DLP tools (network, endpoint, cloud), CASB technologies and SQL/NoSQL databases.
  • Extensive knowledge of security technology and risk assessment methodologies, policies and processes.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to translate complex technical concepts for non-technical decision-makers (e.g., governance committees, business units, legal teams).
  • Excellent analytical, evaluative and problem-solving abilities.
  • Experience with compliance programs as well as their technical and security requirements.
  • Technical expertise across key domains:
    • Standards and Frameworks: Strong command of industry standards such as ISO/IEC 27001, 27002, 27005, NIST SP 800-53 / 800-161, COBIT and ITIL.
    • Cloud and Web Architecture Security: Solid understanding of web infrastructure and cloud environment security.
    • Network and Security Technologies: Thorough understanding of network architectures (LAN/WAN, routers), network security technologies (firewalls, IDS/IPS, DNS, web filtering) and cryptographic principles (encryption at rest and in transit).
    • Architecture and Data Security: Working knowledge of database architecture concepts and secure software development best practices.
    • Operational Resilience and Physical Security: Solid understanding of business continuity and disaster recovery planning (BCP/DRP), operational resilience and physical security controls.
  • Relevant professional security certifications a definite asset (e.g., CISSP, CRISC, CBCP, CISA, CISM or equivalent).
  • Bilingualism (English and French) essential.

Candidates may be subject to skills and knowledge testing.

About the Opportunity


Radio-Canada is proud to launch an internship program specifically designed to increase the representation of members of Indigenous communities in Canada within the audio and radio industry. This internship aims to foster inclusion, professional development and the growth of Indigenous talent within our teams, aligning with CBC/Radio-Canada’s National Indigenous Strategy and building on the First Peoples – Tell Your Story training initiative for Indigenous storytellers. We are seeking passionate, aspiring professionals from all walks of life who are eager to unlock their potential and pursue a rewarding career in media.


The internship will be from January 11 to April 2, 2027 (12 weeks).


This role requires full-time on-site presence.


Who We’re Looking For:


This internship is open exclusively to First Nations, Inuit and Métis individuals in Canada. We encourage applications from motivated candidates at various stages of their professional journey:

  • Early Career Professionals: Ready to broaden your horizons, diversify your skills and take on fresh challenges? This internship is a perfect opportunity to expand your expertise in the media sector.
  • Recent Graduates: Are you a recent graduate with a passion for media and looking to gain foundational hands-on experience? This internship offers the chance to fully immerse yourself within our production teams.
  • Professionals in Career Transition: Do you have solid experience in another field but dream of a dynamic, creative career in media? This internship will help you acquire essential skills and leverage your transferable expertise.

Skills and Qualities We Value:

  • Adaptability and Eagerness to Learn: You can easily fit into new work environments and quickly pick up new technical and professional skills.
  • A Passion for Audio: You have a keen interest in radio broadcasting, sound production and all forms of audio content.
  • Interest in the Radio-Canada Environment: You are driven to elevate Indigenous programming on our airwaves and platforms, and excited to showcase Indigenous talent at Radio-Canada.
  • Interpersonal and Professional Qualities: You bring leadership, creativity, strong organizational, communication and teamwork skills, and a collaborative mindset.
  • Critical Thinking and Open-Mindedness: You possess strong analytical skills and sound judgment, allowing you to navigate complex information and diverse situations with ease.

Tailored to your background and career goals, this immersive, hands-on internship provides the opportunity to gain experience across multiple areas, including content development, interview preparation and program design. It will allow you to build a versatile skill set while working alongside our teams at Radio-Canada OHdio, ICI PREMIÈRE or ICI MUSIQUE.

About the First Peoples Program


The First Peoples: Tell Us a Story initiative is a specialized professional development program designed to build bridges between First Peoples and Radio-Canada. It aims to amplify Indigenous voices in the media while nurturing lasting, reciprocal relationships with Indigenous communities.


Building on the success of its 2025 pilot, the initiative returns this year with a redesigned format. This paid training opportunity has been expanded to eight (8) weeks and will focus on the craft of storytelling. Throughout the program, you will hone your skills through hands-on workshops led by both Indigenous and non-Indigenous media professionals. You will also have a dedicated platform to share your stories, showcase your culture, language and lived experiences, and highlight your community's achievements.


We are looking for four (4) individuals from First Nations, Inuit or Métis communities ready to take the next step in their media careers.


The program runs full time for eight (8) weeks, from February 1st to March 26, 2027. Full-time availability, Monday to Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. (ET) for the entire eight-week program is mandatory.


This program is in hybrid mode (remote work with required travel to Montreal and a regional station).


Candidates must meet the following eligibility requirements:

  • Be 18 years of age or older.
  • Self-identify as First Nations, Inuit or Métis.
  • Be available full time for the duration of the program (February 1st to March 26, 2027).
  • Be willing and able to travel for three (3) separate five-day sessions during the eight (8) weeks (travel and accommodation expenses are fully covered by Radio-Canada).
  • Be able to work and communicate in French (reading, writing and speaking). 

Who You Are:

  • You have a working proficiency in French across speaking, reading and writing. 
  • You have a genuine curiosity about news and current affairs, paired with a passion for storytelling.
  • You have an open, collaborative attitude.
  • You are eager to learn new things.
  • Familiarity with Google Workspace tools is an asset.

Program Overview:

As part of this second cohort, you will complete an eight-week learning curriculum running from February 1st to March 26, 2027.


The program includes the following:

  • Orientation and Onboarding: Settle into the cohort and preview your training plan through a combination of virtual sessions and in-person activities in Montreal. 
  • Theory Instruction (Three (3) weeks, Virtual): Build foundational journalism skills across digital writing, audio/radio storytelling and video production, culminating in one (1) to three (3) portfolio-ready pieces. 
  • Regional Station Placement: Shadow and work alongside Radio-Canada journalists at a regional station to experience the day-to-day rhythm of an active newsroom.
  • Professional Development (Virtual): Take part in sessions designed to support your learning and development. 
  • Closing Week (Montreal): Wrap up the program alongside your peers with a final week of hands-on activities. 

Workplace and Technical Requirements :

The theory instruction will take place primarily online; however, you must be available to travel to Montreal and to a regional station during designated periods. All required travel and accommodation expenses are fully covered by Radio-Canada.


Please note:

  • You must have access to a reliable, high-speed internet connection.
  • You must have access to a desktop computer, laptop or iPad Pro. 
  • Any specialized production gear required for your training modules will be provided by Radio-Canada for the duration of the program. 

Full-time availability for the entire eight-week program is mandatory.

Candidates may be subject to skills and knowledge testing.

  • A mandatory Criminal record check. 

  • Other background checks may be conducted based on the operational requirements of the position.

Your role


The Regional Media team is looking for a Producer to support regional teams and contribute to content development.


Your role will be to support regional teams in developing distinctive content and deploying it to maximize its impact across our digital ecosystem.


You will work within the Regional Media tactical team and help ensure that production efforts are prioritized in alignment with our strategic objectives of local relevance and digital agility, while contributing to strengthening audience trust in Radio-Canada.


Your role will contribute to implementing a story-driven approach designed to strengthen our ability to showcase the distinctive journalism of Regional Media by supporting local teams and leveraging the collective expertise of Regional Media.


You will have considerable autonomy to exercise your leadership, judgment and initiative in fostering a culture of local relevance and digital agility among regional teams.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Maintain an overall view of high-impact projects to prioritize the sector's digital needs and facilitate requests to partners.
  • Support teams in selecting the most appropriate formats, telling stories using the latest digital storytelling techniques, and implementing content distribution best practices in alignment with the sector's strategic directions.
  • Develop expertise in Radio-Canada's conversational tools within Regional Media and act as a subject matter expert and advisor to regional teams.
  • Coordinate the work of resources located across the country who can support local teams on various projects.
  • Build connections between digital experts at different regional stations and promote best practices in keeping with strategic directions.
  • Prepare and support regional teams in adopting new digital production approaches and tools, particularly by actively participating in the Regional Media Innovation Collaborative Space.


This role requires full-time on-site presence.


Your profile:

  • University degree or equivalent.
  • Five (5) years of relevant experience in the media or communications field.
  • Experience coordinating the work of a multidisciplinary team.
  • Excellent understanding of journalistic standards and practices, and how to apply them.
  • Advanced knowledge and understanding of digital production tools, storytelling best practices, and digital conventions.
  • Curiosity and a strong interest in new editorial approaches.
  • Strong collaborative leadership skills and the ability to influence others without direct authority.
  • Ability to work under tight deadlines.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple files simultaneously and independently establish priorities.
  • Strong initiative.
  • Excellent adaptability
  • Advanced French, and English-language proficiency in speaking, writing and reading (CCC).

CBC News is seeking two creative and video-savvy producers to create short-form video for multiple platforms including CBCNews.ca, TikTok and YouTube Shorts. 


You must be an expert in short-form video storytelling and open to experimenting with new social-first formats to reach younger and diverse audiences. You know how to pitch, script, film and produce breaking news content and hosted explainers to help our audience make sense of the news. You think visually and creatively, and can unpack complex topics into clean, simple writing. 


You work with reporters and producers across Canada and in our World bureaus to turn their stories into digital(vertical)videos, including coaching them on scripting and on-camera delivery. You are comfortable hosting these videos, as required. You also collaborate within other social producers and story development producers, including vetting your peers. 


You’re on top of daily news, current affairs and trending stories that younger audiences are talking about on social platforms. You are able to take your understanding of stories that matter and present them in a way digital audiences expect.


You’re an independent, communicative producer who can successfully juggle daily tasks and long-term projects under deadline. Your work is governed by and adheres to CBC journalistic and programming policies, standards and practices. 


You care about the people you work with and have a deep appreciation for different perspectives, opinions and experiences. You live and promote the values of diversity and an inclusive and respectful work culture. 


Reporting is to the executive producer of Story Development.


Please provide examples of 3-5 digital news videos you have produced and/or hosted with your application.


Tasks:

  • Pitch, script, film and host video for CBCNews.ca, TikTok and YouTube Shorts. 
  • Produce digital videos with reporters and producers in bureaus and units across the country and abroad.
  • Produce and host on social platforms, including live events and Q&As with the Ask CBC News team.
  • Identify platform trends and experiment with new digital video storytelling formats.
  • Vet titles, banners, descriptions and scripts for social posts on TikTok, YouTube, and CBCNews.ca, ensuring best practices and journalistic standards apply.
  • Train, coach and provide feedback to collaborators across the network and new staff members. 

Relevant qualifications:

  • Minimum five years of journalism experience, including minimum of three years in social or video production.
  • Proven experience producing innovative short-form digital video on news topics.  
  • Excellent writing and editing skills. 
  • Demonstrated hosting skills and ability to coach reporters on social on-camera performance. 
  • Ability to understand and interpret analytics on digital platforms.
  • Experience packaging and publishing videos on digital platforms. 
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a high-pressure, tight-deadline environment.
  • Knowledge of CBC editorial policies, including CBC's Journalistic Standards and Practices.
  • University degree or equivalent experience.
  • Ability to work independently and source material through archives, Media Central, units/bureaus, audio teams, photo desk and more.
  • Ability to work flexible hours as required, including evenings and weekend shifts.

Your role


CBC/Radio-Canada is currently seeking a Resource Specialist to work in the newsroom on planning the human and technical resources required for all our radio, television and web productions. This posting is for a full time one (1) year contract.


You will be responsible to plan, organize and provide staff, schedules, facilities, and equipment needed for content production, in keeping with program constraints and requirements. You will also oversee schedule coordination and team assignment, aiming for efficient and cost-effective use of human/physical resources.


More specifically, you will plan for, select, organize, acquire or provide staff, facilities, and materials needed to produce programs or program segments. Planning responsibilities include pre-production, production, and post-production, following through to format and telecast requirements. General direction is provided but there is latitude for and an expectation of independent judgment and initiative. You will work on multiple projects at once with constant interruption, and you must meet critical deadlines within a live and recorded TV-radio-web segment. Tact and diplomacy are essential, as decisions must satisfy the needs of several stakeholders with varying priorities.


Key Tasks:

  • With senior managers, producers, unit managers and technical directors, contribute to long- and short-term planning for productions by attending meetings or receiving specific requests. 
  • Provide advice on cost saving and other possible advantages to clients. 
  • Resolve conflicting resource requests.
  • Identify and obtain the appropriate staff, facilities, materials and services for any given production. In so doing, ensure that resources are available when required. 
  • Provide an overview of all production activities and recommend corrective action to accommodate timeline changes or the needs of new and additional productions.
  • Maintain up-to-date knowledge of all collective agreements and corporate policies.

This role requires full-time on-site presence.


We are looking for a candidate with the following: 

  • College graduate from a broadcasting program or equivalent TV broadcasting experience.
  • Minimum of five (5) years relevant experience demonstrating a solid understanding of the television-radio-web production processes is an asset.
  • Knowledge of ScheduAll and iNews software is an asset.
  • Mastery of the functionalities of the Google suite.
  • Strong leadership skills; able to work without supervision; highly tactful, well organized; very motivated self-starter.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills.
  • Able to come up with creative solutions and assist in developing innovative procedures to ensure collaborative and responsive service.
  • Able to work alone as part of a team, under pressure and with tight deadlines.
  • Able to efficiently collaborate and develop synergy with various partners and clients, with a view to providing service adapted to production needs and expectations, while also aiming for cost savings and efficient use of human and material resources.
  • Able to manage multiple projects and priorities at once, while reacting and responding to the needs of clients, colleagues, employees, etc., in a timely and efficient manner.
  • Able to create accurate database records and update existing records.

Your role:


You execute efficient digital advertising and search engine marketing (SEM) campaigns across a variety of platforms. You have a strategic vision for search: you know how to capture intent, structure accounts effectively, and drive engagement. You excel in Google Ads and know how to build efficient campaign structures. You are ready to adapt quickly to emerging trends, new content, and other digital advertising channels as business priorities evolve. You understand how to set objectives, choose the right tactics, make data-driven decisions, and measure your success. You have sound judgment, attention to detail, and value giving and receiving feedback to improve our shared outcomes. You treat others with empathy, respect, and enthusiasm.


As a Senior Communications Officer, you are a cross-functional leader that helps shape the future of CBC. In collaboration with our marketing, creative, content, and product teams, you use your passion for digital marketing and public good to help deliver on CBC’s business objectives.


Some of the duties for this role will include:


  • Plan and execute search-based campaigns in Google Ads promoting key programming and products across CBC and CBC News.
  • Contribute to integrated marketing plans including recommending search strategies, keyword targeting, bidding tactics, and measurement to support specific business objectives.
  • Create, optimize, and maintain efficient search campaign structures, seamlessly integrating new sites, shows, and content into the overarching search strategy.
  • Use attribution-based tracking methods like tags, pixels,  UTMs and Mobile Measurement Partners (MMP) to measure full funnel performance and identify opportunities for optimization.
  • Work closely with in-house creative and content teams to create and test highly relevant ad copy and assets that are grounded in best practices and emerging search trends.
  • Collect, analyze, and socialize campaign insights through written reports and compelling presentations.
  • Track and assign budgets across multiple projects and verticals, making strategic decisions to maximize return on ad spend.
  • Work cross-functionally with teams across the organization from Marketing, Creative, Digital Products, Events, Finance, and others.
  • Other related tasks as required.

Qualifications

Education Required:


  • Diploma or certificate in Communications or Marketing or an equivalent combination of education, training and experience.

Experience and Skills Required:


  • Five years of direct experience that demonstrates superior writing, editing, and proofreading skills, a working knowledge of a wide range of communications and marketing strategies, excellent interpersonal and organizational skills and the ability to work under the pressure of deadlines and multiple priorities.
  • A proven ability to craft and execute campaigns on digital platforms, with deep, hands-on expertise managing and structuring Google Ads (Search, Display, Performance Max, etc.) and a curiosity to adapt to other paid media platforms.
  • Genuine interest in evolving search marketing, SEM, and general advertising trends.
  • Solid understanding of digital marketing and consumption metrics and ability to analyze data to identify opportunities, optimize account architectures, and clearly demonstrate successes.
  • Championing diverse perspectives and ideas, and differing points of view is critical.
  • Demonstrated creative and problem-solving abilities, particularly in campaign restructuring and strategic bidding.
  • Proven ability to work effectively as a member of a team with shared responsibilities and outputs.
  • Flexibility in work hours as operations demand, including the ability to work shifts, including evenings, weekends and holidays, is required.
  • Basic understanding of CBC programming and brand.
  • Bilingualism is a preferred asset.
  • Proven ability to effectively maximize available resources.
  • Successful at managing multiple projects simultaneously while working with tight deadlines.

This is a one year position based in Edmonton, Calgary, Regina or Winnipeg.


The Role

CBC News is looking for an ambitious, creative journalistic leader to serve as the pulse of our Prairies newsrooms. Based in Alberta, Saskatchewan, or Manitoba, you will guide our national reporting teams across all three provinces—setting the news agenda, driving innovative storytelling, and ensuring our coverage reflects the communities we serve.


As Senior Producer, you are a natural leader and self-starter who thrives in fast-paced environments. Operating independently under the direction of an Executive Producer, you will lead, assign, and coach teams across the prairies to respond to daily and breaking news while pursuing high-impact original journalism. 


You will juggle multiple projects, shifting priorities, and competing deadlines across digital, radio, and television platforms, always planning ahead for future coverage and special events while coordinating staff and travel within an assigned budget.


A collaborative mindset is essential to this role. You will break down silos by working closely with local CBC stations across the Prairies and colleagues across CBC to seamlessly share information, content and resources. As a keen observer of the changing media landscape, you embrace experimentation and constantly look for fresh story ideas and formats that reach new, younger, and underserved audiences.


To succeed, you must bring a solid understanding of news across the region, paired with a strong grasp of national and international stories. 

You are skilled at navigating change and conflict, providing constructive feedback, and bringing out your colleagues' creative best.

Above all, you live and promote the values of an inclusive, respectful, and representative work culture.


This role requires a thorough understanding of CBC Journalistic Standards and Practices. This is a permanent, full-time, on-site position that involves regional travel and can be based in Alberta, Saskatchewan, or Manitoba.


Key Tasks:

  • Lead a team of multi-platform journalists located in Calgary, Edmonton, Regina and Winnipeg to file news stories of national interest to CBC’s TV, radio, and digital programs and platforms
  • Work closely with the journalists and leaders in the local CBC stations in each location to ensure news and events from Saskatchewan, Manitoba and Alberta are properly reflected on national programs and that coverage reflects the geographic, racial, cultural and socio-economic diversity of the region
  • Participate in daily meetings with national assignment and story development leaders and other regional assignment producers
  • Pitch Prairies stories for cross-platform rollouts with a focus on shaping these stories to resonate with national audiences
  • Be able to guide reporters, producers and videographers when their help is needed on assignments, whether based in their province or beyond
  • Propose and plan coverage for news events, collaborating with local teams and other CBC teams across the province.
  • Be a leader on major breaking news events, able to quickly build coverage plans, do risk assessments, dispatch field teams and collaborate with local and CBC counterparts to ensure we’re on the story and fast.
  • Ensure storytelling for radio, television and digital platforms has high production values.
  • Have a strong understanding of regional news and knowledge of how to make local stories meaningful to wider audiences
  • Support journalists pursuing enterprise stories, balancing daily demands with original journalism.
  • Work with the Executive Producer of Newsgathering and the Domestic Newsgathering Managing Editor to monitor and support team well-being/mental health, including planning for and recovery from coverage of potentially stressful and traumatic events.
  • Develop and maintain contacts with a wide variety of sources.


Qualifications

  • University degree or equivalent required.
  • Must have 7 years of relevant experience and recognized journalistic and leadership credentials.
  • Exceptional leadership skills and organizational ability.
  • Strong understanding of Manitoba, Saskatchewan and Alberta news.
  • Cultural sensitivity and awareness, with strong connections to diverse communities.
  • Lived experience that broadens journalistic perspectives.
  • Experience pursuing stories in under represented communities.
  • Ability to recognize issues of importance quickly and take effective action to ensure appropriate coverage.
  • Skill in generating ideas for original stories and overseeing original journalism.
  • Outstanding communication and collaboration skills; ability to work cooperatively with team members and supervisors in
  • high pressure situations. Ability to lead with empathy through stressful situations.
  • Solid technical grasp of broadcast and online production tools and methods.
  • Ability to work long hours and travel as required.
