We help our clients navigate today’s fast-moving and interconnected world to win support from the people who are interested in them. The knowledge, creativity, and passion our people bring to this work is why we are a leader in our field.

Do you want to join a world-leading strategic communications consultancy?

We’re now welcoming applications for our 2027 Asia Graduate Programme

With five offices across the Asia region, you will be applying to join our brilliant team in one of the following locations: Beijing, Hong Kong, Shanghai or Singapore.

During the graduate programme you will get the opportunity to work on high-stakes, business-critical projects that span some of the world’s largest companies and most complex situations faced by organisations. You’ll encounter issues that make up the global news agenda of the time.

If you are interested in other opportunities, please visit our Join Us page. Candidates who are interested in applying to our graduate programme in the UK or Middle East must submit a separate application for these markets and adhere to the respective application processes.

What the programme will involve

Successful applicants will be enrolled on in a 2-year structured programme, learning both on-the-job and through formal trainings to help develop your knowledge and skillset across key areas of strategic communications and capital markets advisory. You will have the chance to put these skills to use across a variety of exciting and impactful client mandates.

You will be based in one of our Asia offices but working in close collaboration with clients and colleagues across the Asia region and our international offices. We are a global business, and we work collaboratively across time zones.

Our people love the work they do, and the people they do it with, so you’ll have plenty of opportunities to get to know your local and global colleagues both socially and professionally.

Through the application process, we select individuals for this programme who we believe will pioneer the future of FGS Global. The intention is for us to invest in your development, and you to receive a truly immersive learning experience that challenges you and allows you to demonstrate your own entrepreneurial flare, growing with the firm. The expectation is that you will continue with us after the programme ends as a full-time Senior Associate.

Who are we looking for?

  • We are looking for motivated and proactive graduates who welcome a steep learning curve and the chance to collaborate with a wide range of people.
  • The role requires individuals who are interested and engaged in how different stakeholders communicate – be it through news outlets, investor presentations, social media, keynote events, or face-to-face conversations.
  • We want applicants who are interested in the news agenda, and track emerging issues and current challenges facing society today.
  • In doing so we want people who will bring their own dynamism and knowledge of how companies and organisations communicate, for example the changing world of digital and social media communications.
  • Successful candidates will be able to demonstrate that they embody the values our people live by: being ambitious together, working hard while keeping energy levels high, striving for excellence and taking responsibility in all they do.
  • We care for and uplift those around us, and expect anyone who joins our team to do their part.

What we offer you in return

  • We are a diverse, dynamic and caring group of people. We motivate each other, strive to deliver to a brilliant standard and we take the time to celebrate together and learn lessons to improve.
  • You will have the opportunity to work with leading communications professionals, learning from the brightest minds in the industry who come from a diverse background.
  • You will be working on a diverse mix of clients, across industries, sectors and geographies.
  • You will have continuous training and development throughout the programme, with dedicated mentors.
  • You will be given the platform to innovate and trusted to demonstrate your entrepreneurial flare.
  • You will have access to a range of office perks, location-dependent, including regular team socials, flexible and remote working policies, gym and wellness allowances, and private health and dental care.
  • A competitive salary benchmarked against others in the industry and reviewed regularly, on an annual basis.
  • Candidates applying from abroad will receive relocation support, including flights and assistance with accommodation and visa applications.
  • At the beginning of the programme, we require you to be in the office full time. After this, we expect all colleagues to be in the office the majority of the working week, however we do offer flexibility to work from home at least one day a week.

Visa, language and relocation requirements

Asia

  • Exceptional English language skills (written and verbal) are essential and proficiency in a relevant Asian language is preferable.
  • For candidates looking to join our Hong Kong, Shanghai or Beijing offices, it is necessary to have a high-level of proficiency in Chinese (written and verbal)
  • We will support candidates with their visa application; for those candidates looking to join our offices in Beijing, Shanghai and Singapore, it is important that you have the right to work in these markets.
  • Candidates must be able to relocate by start of August 2027 to begin work by the middle of August

How the application process works

Step 1. We will ask you to fill out a short form and send us your CV and we will also ask you to address an FGS Global-specific case study analysis task that is designed to highlight the brightest, most creative graduates. This task is an opportunity for you to demonstrate your research skills, creative thinking and ability to communicate complex ideas in a simple way.

For the instructions for the task please click here.

Your completed case study analysis should be structured as a 1–2-page summary in English, providing a focused, well-organized overview of your findings.

We appreciate that this task takes a lot of work, but it gives us the opportunity to assess in a completely objective way based on your abilities and talents.

Your case study analysis and CV must be submitted in PDF format. This application must be completed by Friday 19th March 2027 at 23:59 HKT – late applications will not be accepted.

Step 2. Shortlisted candidates will be sent an online written assessment, and if you are applying for a position in one of our locations where Asian language skills are required, we will ask you to complete an assessment in this language

Step 3. We will host a series of assessments including group tasks, problem solving exercises and interviews the week of 19th April 2027. Further details of the final assessment phase will be announced in due course.

Successful applicants will start full-time on 9th August 2027.

 

For more in depth information please refer to our Grad Programme Website.

job.title: Account Payable Accountant
job.description:
Account Payable Accountant 

 

Overview of the Firm   

FGS Global helps the world's most influential leaders move minds and markets. Working where business, government, and public opinion intersect, we advise CEOs, boards, and leadership teams at the most consequential moments.  

We work as one team across geographies and disciplines - bringing together specialists with backgrounds in communications, finance, law, government, journalism, data science, and digital. Whatever the moment demands, we combine multidimensional perspectives to help leaders anticipate what's next, engage the stakeholders who matter, and drive meaningful outcomes. 

Across 31 global offices, we draw on the full depth of the firm so clients can operate with clarity, act with confidence, and lead with trust. This collaborative approach has established FGS as a market leader: we are consistently ranked Band 1 for Crisis & Risk Management and Litigation Support by Chambers and Partners, and were ranked the #1 Global M&A PR firm by deal value and deal count for four consecutive years (Mergermarket, 2025). 

 

The Role  

You will play a pivotal role in facilitating daily accounting and payment operations across the firm in Hong Kong. 

You will collaborate closely with consultants, client teams, and finance colleagues to ensure the seamless and accurate processing of financial transactions. 

 

Responsibilities 

  • Process accounts payable transactions, including office expenses, client project payments, staff reimbursements, corporate card expenses, and travel-related invoices 
  • Handle banking activities, including cheque deposits and collections, telegraphic transfers, and other payment arrangements 
  • Perform daily bank reconciliations and ensure the accuracy of financial records 
  • Assist in preparing accounting schedules, reconciliations, and ad hoc finance reports 
  • Support month-end closing activities and maintain proper documentation for audit and compliance purposes 
  • Liaise with internal stakeholders regarding payment requests, invoice enquiries, and expense claims 
  • Assist with administrative duties and contribute to ongoing process improvement initiatives within the finance team 
  • Provide cross-functional support to team members when required 

Desired Skills & Qualities 

  • Minimum 5 years of accounting experience gained from a professional services firm or multinational corporate environment 
  • Exposure to accounts payable, expense processing, and bank reconciliations 
  • Experience using NetSuite is an advantage 
  • Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Excel and other Microsoft Office applications to run reports and do analysis 
  • Strong attention to detail with good organisational and analytical skills 
  • Effective communication skills in English and Cantonese 
  • A proactive team player with a positive and professional attitude

job.title: Accounting Manager / Senior Accounting Manager
job.description:
Overview of the Firm 

FGS Global helps the world's most influential leaders move minds and markets. Working where business, government, and public opinion intersect, we advise CEOs, boards, and leadership teams at the most consequential moments.

We work as one team across geographies and disciplines - bringing together specialists with backgrounds in communications, finance, law, government, journalism, data science, and digital. Whatever the moment demands, we combine multidimensional perspectives to help leaders anticipate what's next, engage the stakeholders who matter, and drive meaningful outcomes.

Across 31 global offices, we draw on the full depth of the firm so clients can operate with clarity, act with confidence, and lead with trust. This collaborative approach has established FGS as a market leader: we are consistently ranked Band 1 for Crisis & Risk Management and Litigation Support by Chambers and Partners, and were ranked the #1 Global M&A PR firm by deal value and deal count for four consecutive years (Mergermarket, 2025).

 

The Role

We are seeking an experienced and hands-on Accounting Manager to join our Asia finance team in Hong Kong. Reporting to the Head of Finance, Asia, and working closely with the Finance Operations Senior Manager, this role plays a key part in the accounting operations of the firm across the Hong Kong, Singapore, and China entities, with key responsibility for the month-end close, financial reporting, and tax compliance, as well as supporting the statutory and group audits. The role places a strong focus on income statement analysis to provide insight into revenue and cost performance.

The ideal candidate will be a qualified accountant who combines strong technical knowledge with a hands-on approach, takes accountability for their deliverables, and communicates clearly with senior internal and external stakeholders. They will be comfortable operating in a fast-paced professional services environment and contributing to continuous improvement in processes and controls. Experience with VAT/GST filing across Singapore and China jurisdictions will be highly regarded.

 

Responsibilities

  • Reporting to Head of Finance, this role is a key Act as a key member to perform the month-end closing, including revenue recognition, accruals, balance sheet reconciliations and variance analysis.
  • Work closely with Global Accounting Team to drive alignment and compliance with Group Policy and Accounting Standards and to support audits and tax filings.
  • Perform detailed monthly income statement analysis, explaining revenue and cost movements against prior periods, budget and forecast, and identifying trends, anomalies and risks.
  • Ensure departmental costs are accurately recorded, coded, and allocated to the correct cost centres, reviewing cost reports and resolving variances with budget holders on a timely basis.
  • Review and deliver monthly, quarterly, and annual financial and management reports, providing analysis and commentary on key variances to the Head of Finance and regional leadership.
  • Support the statutory and group audit processes together with Finance Operations Senior Manager.
  • Manage tax filing obligations across Hong Kong, Singapore, and China, including GST/VAT compliance, corporate income tax, and withholding tax matters, and liaise with external tax advisers.
  • Partner with operational teams on cost budgeting and reforecasting to support business to drive cost control.
  • Proactively identify opportunities to drive cost optimisation, analysing spending trends and recommending practical cost-saving initiatives to the Head of Finance and business leaders.
  • Partner with global finance teams and external service providers on group reporting, intercompany, and consolidation matters.
  • Maintain and strengthen internal controls and accounting policies, and drive process and system improvements to enhance efficiency in the Asia finance function.
  • Support ad hoc finance projects as required.

 

Desired Skills & Qualities

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting or a related discipline from a recognised university.
  • A recognised professional accounting qualification (e.g. HKICPA, ACCA, CPA) is required.
  • 10-15 years of relevant accounting experience, preferably in a professional services or multinational environment. Audit firm experience is an advantage.
  • Solid technical accounting knowledge, with experience applying US GAAP and/or IFRS/HKFRS.
  • Strong analytical skills with a proven track record in income statement analysis, able to translate financial results into clear, actionable insights for business leaders.
  • Proven experience supporting statutory audits and managing tax filings across multiple jurisdictions; familiarity with Singapore GST and China VAT filing will be highly considered.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel; experience with ERP or accounting systems such as NetSuite is strongly preferred.
  • Strong team player, with the ability to guide and support junior team members.
  • Hands-on, highly organised, and able to manage competing priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced and dynamic working environment.
  • Treasury experience is a plus but it is NOT a must.
  • Proactive, with excellent interpersonal and communication skills and the confidence to engage senior stakeholders, auditors, and advisers.
  • Fluency in written and spoken English and Cantonese is preferred and be ready to join global calls

District of Columbia Salary Range$130,000—$170,000 USD

Join our team in Amsterdam as Intern Strategic Corporate & Transaction Communication starting February 1st 2027.

 

What tasks can you look forward to?

  • As an intern, you will be part of the team from day one and experience everyday life as a communications consultant at first hand.
  • You will support the project teams in the development and implementation of communication strategies for national and international clients in matters of strategic corporate communication and positioning.
  • The topics range from M&A transactions, IPOs and strategic realignments to the communication of digitalization and transformation strategies.
  • Together with our team, you will design compelling communications materials for internal and external stakeholders (e.g., communications plans, press releases, corporate presentations).
  • You follow, monitor and understand Dutch and European media.
  • You help with ad-hoc requests and questions from other offices about the media, economy, and society in the Netherlands.
  • For research and analysis, you will dig deep into relevant topics, exciting companies, media coverage and trends.
  • You bring in fresh, inspiring ideas and innovative communications formats.

 

What should you bring along?

  • You are at the end of your undergraduate or master's degree - the subject is less important than your enthusiasm for communication.
  • Ideally, you have already gained practical experience during your studies, for example in communications, finance, journalism, politics and/or strategy consulting.
  • You are a quick learner and it is recommended that you communicate fluently in Dutch and very well in English.
  • You have a good understanding of the Dutch media landscape.
  • You love variety and new challenges and really thrive when working in a team.

 

What we can offer you

  • The opportunity to get to know strategic communications consulting
  • Insights into the activities of a leading strategic communications consultancy as well as into various industries and areas of expertise as part of our integrated project teams
  • Exciting and varied tasks in an international and inspiring working environment
  • The opportunity to benefit from training & development opportunities
  • Induction and individual support as well as detailed feedback from an experienced consultant
  • A committed, collegial and constantly growing team in which mutual appreciation and team spirit are paramount
  • A company culture that combines excellence with team spirit
  • The opportunity to work flexibly both in our offices and from home
  • Our beautiful office in the heart of Amsterdam- Zuid

 

Don’t meet every single requirement? Please don’t worry! Studies have shown that some groups like women or people of color are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single requirement. At FGS Global, we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace. So, if you’re excited about this role and our company but your previous professional experience doesn’t match perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we would like to encourage you to apply anyway. You may just be the right candidate for this or another role.

We look forward to your complete application (incl. all relevant academic and professional certificates and/or reference letters). Feel free to contact us by email via careers-eu@fgsglobal.com.

 More information: FGS Global

job.title: Application Security Engineer
job.description:
About Us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide. At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world. In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing. Your future at the FT will be filled with opportunities that challenge and inspire you. Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

We believe in the power of unique perspectives and want all voices in our organisation to be heard, respected and valued. A supportive workplace is one where employees feel they can be themselves and operate to their full potential. We are committed to removing barriers for everyone, with a focus on addressing those faced by underrepresented groups.

The Role Overview

We’re looking for a Cyber Security Engineer to help improve application security across the FT’s cloud-native technology estate. This is a hands-on role focused on making secure engineering easier for product, platform and software engineering teams.

Application security experience is essential for this role. You’ll help improve developer-friendly security guardrails across GitHub-based CI/CD pipelines, application repositories and engineering workflows. This includes working with SAST, software composition analysis, secret scanning, vulnerability management and secure coding guidance so that security findings are clear, actionable and owned by the right teams.

You’ll work closely with engineers to support practical threat modelling, triage application vulnerabilities, improve security playbooks and help teams remediate issues in a pragmatic way. You do not need to be a deep AWS or cloud security specialist, but some exposure to AWS, cloud security or infrastructure-as-code security would be useful.

We’re looking for someone with practical AppSec experience who wants to grow their impact - someone who enjoys working with engineers, improving tooling and helping security become part of normal delivery rather than a last-minute checkpoint.

What you’ll bring to the role

Application security experience: practical experience identifying, explaining and helping remediate application security risks in modern engineering environments.

Developer-friendly security mindset: you enjoy working with engineers, explaining risks clearly and helping teams adopt secure practices without unnecessary friction.

Vulnerability management experience: experience triaging and tracking application vulnerabilities from sources such as SAST, dependency scanning, secret scanning, penetration tests, bug bounty reports or third-party advisories.

CI/CD and code security awareness: familiarity with security tooling in development workflows, such as SAST, software composition analysis, secret scanning or repository security controls.

Threat modelling awareness: experience participating in, supporting or facilitating lightweight threat-modelling sessions for applications, services or new features.

Automation mindset: ability to write scripts or small tools, ideally in Python, to reduce manual effort, improve visibility or make security workflows easier.

Cloud security awareness: Some exposure to AWS, cloud security or infrastructure-as-code security would be useful, but is not essential.

Growth mindset: willingness to keep developing across application security, cloud security, secure development and modern engineering practices.

Required Experience, Essential

  • Practical experience in application security.
  • Experience working with software engineers to explain and remediate security issues.
  • Familiarity with common web application security risks and secure coding practices.
  • Experience with vulnerability triage, prioritisation and remediation tracking.
  • Experience using or interpreting findings from tools such as SAST, software composition analysis, secret scanning or similar.
  • Experience participating in or supporting threat-modelling activities.
  • Ability to write scripts or small tools, ideally in Python, to automate tasks or improve visibility.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills.
  • Familiarity with Agile or Scrum ways of working.

Desirable

  • Exposure to AWS security, cloud security or infrastructure-as-code security.
  • Experience with Terraform or CloudFormation.
  • Experience with container or Kubernetes security.
  • Experience with bug bounty, penetration testing or security testing programmes.
  • Experience with Splunk or similar logging/SIEM platforms.
  • Exposure to AI security, such as LLM-enabled applications, AI-assisted development workflows or prompt/data leakage risks.
  • Experience building dashboards, metrics or reports to support vulnerability management.
  • Relevant security certifications or training, such as AWS security training, secure coding training, GIAC, ISC2, CREST or equivalent practical experience.

 

What’s in it for you? Our benefits

Our benefits vary by location but we are committed to providing best-in-class perks across all our offices. These include generous annual leave, medical cover, inclusive parental leave packages, subsidised gym memberships and opportunities to give back to the community. Full details of our benefits are available here.

The role

We are looking for a dedicated and versatile Copywriter to join the Financial Times' Brand and Partnerships team, creating compelling, creative and persuasive marketing copy that brings the FT brand to life across a wide range of channels and audiences.

Reporting to the Senior Marketing Copywriter, you will work closely with colleagues across global communications, commercial marketing, design, creative and editorial teams to deliver impactful campaigns and messaging that strengthen the FT's reputation and encourage audiences to engage with our journalism.

From conceptual advertising campaigns, podcast and video scripts to digital ads, direct response emails, event marketing, speeches, white papers and social media, you'll have the opportunity to work on a diverse range of creative projects. You'll also help promote the FT's brand platform to both internal and external audiences, ensuring our distinctive tone of voice is reflected consistently in everything we do.

This is an opportunity to join a fast-paced, collaborative and ambitious team at the heart of a global news organisation. We're looking for someone who combines exceptional writing skills with critical thinking, creative flair and a genuine passion for news, brands and digital media.

Key responsibilities

  • Create high-quality, engaging and persuasive copy for a wide range of marketing campaigns, channels and audiences, including both B2B and B2C communications.

  • Work collaboratively with the Senior Marketing Copywriter, brand and creative teams, external agencies and internal collaborators to develop compelling creative concepts and messaging.

  • Champion and protect the FT's brand identity and tone of voice, ensuring consistent and impactful communications that strengthen our reputation as a trusted source of global journalism.

  • Write and adapt copy across multiple formats, including conceptual advertising, digital campaigns, emails, social media, podcast and video scripts, speeches, events and longer-form content.

  • Manage copywriting briefs from across the business, identifying the right approach for each audience and channel while balancing multiple projects and deadlines.

  • Review, edit and refine AI-generated copy, applying creative judgement to ensure accuracy, quality, originality and alignment with the FT's brand standards.

  • Ensure messaging is consistent, complementary and aligned with FT brand guidelines across all marketing activities.

  • Support the wider brand, marketing and business teams in developing communications that build awareness, encourage engagement and attract new subscribers.

Required skills and experience

  • A qualification in English, marketing, advertising, journalism or a related field.

  • At least two years' professional copywriting experience in advertising, marketing, media or a related field.

  • Exceptional writing skills, with demonstrable experience creating engaging and effective copy across a variety of channels, including print, digital, audio and speeches.

The role

We're looking for a Marketing Automation Journey Lead to join our Reader Revenue Group and play a key role in shaping how we engage with customers across their lifecycle.

As our Consumer and B2B subscription businesses evolve towards a more sophisticated, customer-led approach to growth, engagement and retention, Marketing Automation plays a critical role in delivering relevant, connected and effective customer experiences.

Our Marketing Automation teams operate as a Centre of Excellence, bringing together journey expertise, platform capabilities, experimentation, personalisation and measurement to drive customer and commercial value.

Reporting to the Head of Marketing Automation (Consumer or B2B), you'll be responsible for ensuring we're automating and improving the right customer experiences.

Sitting between lifecycle strategy and execution, this is a journey architecture, orchestration and optimisation role. You'll partner closely with Lifecycle Marketing and other collaborators to understand customer needs and commercial objectives, translating these into effective automated experiences.

You'll take a comprehensive view of the automated journey portfolio, finding opportunities to improve how journeys, campaigns, triggers and customer or account states work together. You'll assess existing activity, identify gaps or overlaps, and recommend whether journeys should be optimised, extended, redesigned, consolidated or retired.

Rather than focusing primarily on building individual campaigns, you'll lead the thinking behind journey design and optimisation, developing actionable recommendations and coordinating delivery through Marketing Automation Specialists and Executives.

You'll also work closely with your counterpart in the Consumer or B2B Marketing Automation team, sharing expertise and helping establish consistent standards, experimentation approaches and guidelines across the Centre of Excellence.

This is an opportunity to have a meaningful impact on the FT's customer experience, ensuring automated journeys are connected, measurable and continuously improving.

Key responsibilities

Journey architecture and orchestration

  • Partner with Lifecycle Marketing and other collaborators to understand business objectives, customer needs, target audiences and lifecycle challenges.

  • Translate strategic briefs into effective automation opportunities, challenging proposed solutions where necessary to address the underlying customer or commercial problem.

  • Maintain a comprehensive view of the automated journey portfolio, ensuring journeys, campaigns, triggers and customer or account states work together coherently.

  • Map and visualise customer journeys, identifying gaps, overlaps, friction and opportunities to improve reach, relevance and effectiveness.

  • Determine whether objectives are best achieved by optimising existing journeys, introducing new pathways, adjusting triggers, content or sequencing, or retiring existing activity.

  • Design automated experiences using appropriate audiences, channels, behavioural signals, personalisation, decisioning and timing.

  • Define journey sequencing, eligibility, hierarchy and suppression rules to handle interactions between customer experiences.

  • Work with Data, Technology, Creative and Marketing Automation colleagues to translate journey designs into delivered experiences.

Portfolio optimisation and prioritisation

  • Own and maintain the journey opportunity and optimisation roadmap, prioritising activity according to customer and commercial impact, reach, effort and strategic importance.

  • Regularly audit automated journeys to find opportunities for improvement, redesign, consolidation or retirement.

  • Investigate underlying audience, data, design and execution issues to understand journey performance.

  • Find opportunities to improve customer experiences through behavioural triggers, segmentation, personalisation and multichannel orchestration.

  • Ensure journeys are continuously reviewed and optimised rather than treated as one-off launches.

  • Work with the Head of Marketing Automation to align optimisation priorities with the wider strategy and available capacity.

Measurement, testing and learning

  • Establish clear objectives, KPIs and measurement approaches for significant journey interventions.

  • Incorporate testing and experimentation into journey design, including hypotheses, control groups and learning objectives where appropriate.

  • Use customer, account, behavioural and commercial data to assess journey effectiveness and find opportunities.

  • Evaluate broader journey outcomes alongside individual campaign performance, focusing on measurable customer and commercial impact.

  • Translate analysis and experimentation into actionable recommendations and future improvements.

  • Contribute to shared learning, measurement frameworks and procedures across the Centre of Excellence.

Delivery leadership and collaboration

  • Translate journey recommendations into clear, actionable briefs for Marketing Automation Specialists and Executives.

  • Work with delivery teams to define audience requirements, triggers, branching logic, personalisation, sequencing, testing and data dependencies.

  • Provide architectural direction, reviewing implementation proposals and identifying risks or opportunities for improvement.

  • Coach and support colleagues in journey design, optimisation and effective use of automation capabilities.

  • Collaborate with Consumer and B2B counterparts to share expertise, find opportunities and develop consistent approaches.

  • Contribute to Centre of Excellence playbooks and standards for journey design, testing, personalisation and orchestration.

Platform and capability development

  • Apply a strong understanding of marketing automation and customer data platforms to design effective journeys.

  • Find opportunities to make better use of existing automation capabilities and work with technical colleagues where further development may be required.

  • Combine customer and account data, behavioural signals, segmentation and decisioning to improve relevance and effectiveness.

  • Support the development and adoption of scalable, reusable Marketing Automation standards and ways of working.

Required skills and experience

  • Significant experience in marketing automation, CRM, lifecycle marketing or a closely related field.

  • Strong expertise in customer journey architecture, design and orchestration, with the ability to think across interconnected customer experiences rather than individual campaigns.

  • Experience handling or optimising a portfolio of automated journeys, identifying gaps, dependencies and opportunities for improvement.

  • Ability to translate customer and commercial challenges into clear journey strategies and practical automation solutions.

  • Strong understanding of automation principles, including triggers, segmentation, personalisation, decisioning, channel selection, frequency and journey sequencing.

  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with experience using customer, behavioural and commercial data to improve outcomes.

  • Experience developing testing and experimentation approaches and applying insights to journey optimisation.

  • Commercial awareness and an understanding of how automated journeys contribute to acquisition, conversion, onboarding, engagement, retention and customer value.

  • Ability to map, visualise and explain sophisticated customer journeys to collaborators with varying levels of technical expertise.

  • Strong relationship management, collaboration and influencing skills, including confidence challenging briefs and recommending alternative approaches.

  • Experience coaching or mentoring colleagues and supporting the development of others.

  • Excellent organisational skills, with the ability to prioritise contending opportunities and make evidence-based recommendations.

  • Sufficient technical and platform knowledge to understand implementation requirements, identify dependencies and challenge proposed solutions.

Desirable

  • Experience in subscription, digital media, recurring revenue or other customer lifecycle businesses.

  • Familiarity with sophisticated marketing automation or customer data platforms such as Bloomreach, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Marketo or equivalent.

  • Experience with behavioural decisioning, next-best-action, dynamic content or advanced personalisation.

  • Experience designing or optimising multichannel journeys across email, onsite and other digital channels.

  • Knowledge of account-based marketing, multi-contact buying journeys or complex B2B customer relationships.

  • Experience developing reusable journey frameworks, playbooks or operating standards.

  • Experience working across B2C and B2B audiences or within a Centre of Excellence.

What's in it for you? Our benefits

Our benefits vary by location but we are committed to providing best-in-class perks across all our offices. These include generous annual leave, medical cover, inclusive parental leave packages, subsidised gym memberships and opportunities to give back to the community. job.description:

Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

Our commitment is to be an employer role model, grounded in inclusion and fairness for all.

We want every application to receive fair and thoughtful consideration; therefore, all applications are reviewed by a member of our recruitment team, not by AI.

 

The Roles

Newsletters are key to the FT’s strategy, engaging our subscribers and expanding the reach of our journalism. We are looking for two editors to join our newsletter team in London. In this role you’ll be editing, writing and developing newsletters across multiple topics, in collaboration with our global team of reporters, columnists and editors.

You will be confident editing, writing and curating top-quality global journalism, as well as building relationships across a newsroom spanning multiple countries. You have excellent digital and analytical skills, understanding of the newsletter medium and ideas for innovation. You will be aware of media and audience developments. You will be skilled at writing strong subject lines, calls to action, and accurate, concise, engaging summaries of complex stories across many topics.

One newsletter editor role is a permanent position. One is a 12 month fixed term contract. You can apply for either or both opportunities through this listing. Please indicate in your application form whether you are interested in both opportunities or only one.

 

Key Responsibilities

  • Writing, editing and curating a variety of newsletters
  • Using strong editorial judgment, alongside audience data, to inform your decisions
  • Continuously identifying opportunities for improving our newsletters, conducting smart experiments to test ideas and giving recommendations on potential changes
  • Contributing to the development and piloting of potential newsletter launches
  • Helping us to grow our newsletter audience and working with the audience engagement team to promote newsletters
  • Working collaboratively with other members of the newsletter team and cross-functionally with other departments to execute the FT’s newsletter strategy 

 

Your Skills

  • Excellent editing, writing and organisational abilities
  • Ability to work under pressure to tight deadlines
  • Experience working with data to inform editorial decisions
  • A passion for and experience with newsletters
  • Understanding of unique product and design challenges in newsletters and ability to develop innovative ideas to improve the audience experience
  • Excellent communication skills and experience working collaboratively with a variety of stakeholders

 

Your Expertise

  • Knowledge of business, markets, economics, finance, politics, international affairs, arts and culture
  • Knowledge of professional services–including management consulting and accounting–is of special interest
  • Knowledge of the Gulf is of special interest
  • Our newsletters cover a broad range of topics, and we don’t expect candidates to have expertise on all of them. So the ability to learn quickly about areas where you have less experience editing is essential

 

Please submit your application by the end of the day, Tuesday 1st December 2026.

 

The use of AI

Original reporting, great writing and intelligent commentary lie at the heart of FT journalism. Our readers trust us to produce quality journalism that is accurate, fair and insightful. This is why FT editorial staff do not by default use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to write articles or create other reader-facing content. For specific and pre-approved cases, AI can be harnessed for certain tasks, such as assisting data research for investigations.  

We expect applicants to the FT newsroom to refrain from using AI in their test submissions, and any written materials should be a genuine reflection of their own knowledge, skills and experiences. We encourage candidates only to employ AI as a tool to help with research and interview readiness for a role. 

Candidates should be aware that the use of AI throughout the application process is monitored to ensure a fair and transparent hiring process for all.

 

What’s in it for you? Our benefits

Our benefits vary by location but we are committed to providing best-in-class perks across all our offices. These include generous annual leave, medical cover, inclusive parental leave packages, subsidised gym memberships and opportunities to give back to the community. Full details of our benefits are available here.

FT Newsroom staff are expected to work onsite a minimum of three days per week, subject to role requirements and regular review. While flexible working requests will be considered, not all patterns are suitable for Editorial roles.

 

Accessibility

We are a disability confident employer and Valuable 500 signatory.

Please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments/personalisation as part of the application process or to enable you to attend an interview. If you would like to discuss your requirements or have any questions, email talent@ft.com and a member of our team will be happy to help.

The FT is looking for a sharp, sure-footed editor to help run its London night news operation. This is a demanding role at the heart of the newsroom, requiring the judgement to make big editorial calls and the skills to commission, edit and present high-profile FT’s journalism.

The London evening is often when the big stories of the day can take a decisive turn. From wars and geopolitical crises to market-moving corporate deals, the night editor needs to respond quickly to breaking developments and decide what matters most to FT readers.

The editor will be responsible for running the FT's UK homepage during the shift, making calls on news priorities and ensuring stories are presented with strong headlines, images and graphics.

Night news commissions breaking news that can cut across all the main newsdesks. The team also plays an important role revising stories for publication, upholding the FT's high standards for accuracy and quality.

The night news operation must work closely with the New York desk, co-ordinating coverage so important stories are handled smoothly between time zones.

We are open to appointing an experienced editor to lead the London night news team, or a strong candidate to join it in a senior editing role. The person taking on leadership responsibility would be expected to set priorities, support colleagues and manage the team.

 

Working arrangements

The role is based in London and involves evening shifts and regular Sunday working. The existing pattern is four night shifts a week, but we are open to discussing different working arrangements with candidates that would ensure the needs of the news operation are met.

job.title: Senior Cyber Security Engineer
job.description:
About Us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide. At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world. In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing Your future at the FT will be filled with opportunities that challenge and inspire you. With no fixed path, you’ll discover new skills and forge a career that can take you anywhere. Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

We believe in the power of unique perspectives and want all voices in our organisation to be heard, respected and valued. A supportive workplace is one where employees feel they can be themselves and operate to their full potential. We are committed to removing barriers for everyone, with a focus on addressing those faced by underrepresented groups.

The Role Overview

We’re looking for a Senior Cyber Security Engineer to help mature application and cloud security across the FT’s cloud-native, AWS-hosted technology estate. This role has an approximate 50/50 focus across application security and cloud security, working closely with product, platform and engineering teams to make secure delivery easier by default.

You’ll shape and improve developer-friendly guardrails across GitHub-based CI/CD pipelines, AWS environments and infrastructure-as-code workflows. This includes improving SAST, software composition analysis, secret scanning, IaC scanning, vulnerability management and AWS misconfiguration management so that findings are actionable, low-noise and owned by the right teams.

Day to day, you’ll run practical threat-modelling sessions, review application and cloud designs, improve security playbooks, support vulnerability and misconfiguration remediation, and build automation that reduces toil. We’re looking for someone who has demonstrably improved security outcomes in real engineering environments, not just someone with theoretical knowledge of tools or frameworks.

Depending on team structure, you may also mentor or line-manage one or two security engineers, while remaining hands-on and close to the technical work.

What you’ll bring to the role

Application and cloud security experience: practical experience across both application security and cloud security, ideally in AWS-hosted, cloud-native environments.

Developer-friendly security mindset: you know how to work with engineers, explain risk clearly and design controls that help teams move securely without unnecessary friction.

Vulnerability management at scale: experience improving how application vulnerabilities, dependency risks, bug bounty findings, penetration test findings and advisories are identified, prioritised, owned and remediated across engineering teams.

Cloud misconfiguration & vulnerability management: experience identifying and reducing infrastructure-as-code and AWS vulnerabilities & misconfigurations at scale through pragmatic guardrails, tooling and clear remediation paths.

Threat modelling: confidence running lightweight, practical threat-modelling sessions that lead to useful engineering decisions and risk reduction.

CI/CD and code security: hands-on experience with security tooling such as SAST, software composition analysis, secret scanning and IaC scanning.

Automation mindset: ability to write scripts or small tools, ideally in Python, to reduce toil, improve visibility and surface meaningful risk.

Security leadership: ability to mentor other security engineers and influence engineers across the wider organisation. Depending on team structure, this may include line management.

AI security awareness: experience of leveraging AI to improve and scale appsec and cloud sec controls would be useful, but is not essential.

Key Responsibilities

Improve application security guardrails
 Tune and evolve SAST, software composition analysis, secret scanning and related controls so they are actionable, low-noise and useful to engineering teams.

Improve cloud and IaC security guardrails
 Help identify, prioritise and reduce AWS and infrastructure-as-code misconfigurations and vulnerabilities at scale.

Drive vulnerability management
 Improve how application vulnerabilities, dependency risks, bug bounty findings, penetration test findings and third-party advisories are triaged, prioritised and remediated.

Drive cloud misconfiguration management
 Help teams understand, own and remediate cloud security issues using pragmatic, developer-friendly workflows.

Run practical threat modelling
 Facilitate lightweight threat-modelling sessions for new products, features, services and architectural changes.

Build automation and tooling
 Create or improve scripts, integrations, dashboards and workflows that reduce manual effort and make risk easier to understand.

Support secure architecture decisions
 Provide application and cloud security input into design reviews, AWS architecture decisions and larger technical changes.

Partner with engineering teams
 Work closely with product, platform and software engineering teams to embed security into design, delivery and operational practices.

Support incidents and lessons learned
 Provide application and cloud security expertise during incidents and feed lessons learned back into patterns, tooling and guidance.

Mentor others
 Coach security engineers and engineering teams on practical security approaches. Depending on team structure, this may include line management of one or two security engineers.

Required Experience, Essential: 

  • Strong practical experience in application security and cloud security, ideally with a balanced focus across both.
  • Hands-on AWS security experience, including common misconfiguration patterns and practical remediation approaches.
  • Experience improving vulnerability management across engineering teams, including prioritisation, ownership, remediation tracking and noise reduction.
  • Experience in improving cloud or IaC misconfiguration management at scale in a developer-friendly way.
  • Experience integrating, tuning or improving security tooling in CI/CD workflows, such as SAST, software composition analysis, secret scanning or IaC scanning.
  • Experience running practical threat-modelling sessions that influence design, delivery or remediation decisions.
  • Ability to write scripts or small tools, ideally in Python, to automate security workflows or improve visibility.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to influence engineers and technical leaders without relying on gatekeeping.
  • Evidence of improving application security, cloud security or vulnerability management practices in a real engineering environment.
  • Familiarity with Agile or Scrum ways of working.

Desirable

  • Experience with leveraging AI for AppSec and CloudSec.
  • AWS Certified Security – Speciality or equivalent practical AWS security experience.
  • Terraform or CloudFormation expertise.
  • Incident-management or incident-response experience.
  • Experience with Splunk or similar logging/SIEM platforms.
  • Experience with security metrics, dashboards or reporting that helped drive measurable risk reduction.
  • Experience mentoring or line-managing security engineers.

 

What’s in it for You?

Our benefits vary by location but we are committed to providing best-in-class perks across all our offices. These include generous annual leave, medical cover, inclusive parental leave packages, subsidised gym memberships and opportunities to give back to the community. Full details of our benefits are available here.

While flexible working requests will be considered, not all patterns are suitable for all roles. We believe this balanced approach supports flexibility and protects our culture, making collaboration and communication easier, building stronger relationships and team cohesion, and supporting peer learning.  We reserve discretion on reasonable notice to change this approach either generally or for specific individuals or teams.

You will also manage two junior lawyers, providing guidance and supporting their professional development.

  • Lead the drafting, review and negotiation of complex commercial agreements, particularly technology contracts, including SaaS, cloud services, software licensing, development agreements and data processing agreements.

  • Advise on major business initiatives, technology transformation programmes, strategic procurement projects and complex supplier relationships.

  • Provide legal support for the development and enhancement of the FT's digital products, technology infrastructure, data and analytics initiatives, and adoption of emerging technologies.

  • Advise on Ad Tech and Payment Processing matters, including legal and regulatory requirements relating to digital advertising, cookies and similar technologies.

  • Represent the Legal team on the FT's AI Panel, advising on legal and regulatory risks associated with artificial intelligence and supporting the development and implementation of the FT's AI governance framework.

  • Provide legal guidance on data protection and cybersecurity incidents, advising on regulatory obligations, risk mitigation and incident response.

  • Support FT People on commercial and contractual matters relating to HR systems, employee benefits, recruitment and other People-related activities, excluding specialist employment law advice.

  • Build trusted relationships with senior stakeholders, including executive leadership and Board members, providing clear, commercially balanced advice on complex issues.

  • Line manage two junior lawyers specialising in technology and general commercial matters, providing supervision, workload management and professional development support.

Required Skills and Experience

Essential

  • Qualified to practise in English law, with at least eight years' post-qualification experience (PQE).

  • Available to start from 1 February 2027.

  • Extensive experience drafting and negotiating complex commercial contracts, particularly technology agreements.

  • Strong knowledge of data protection legislation, including GDPR and CCPA, with experience advising on privacy, information security, cookies and similar technologies.

  • Experience advising on the legal and regulatory implications of AI and emerging technologies.

  • Strong commercial judgement, with the ability to assess complex legal risks and provide practical, solutions-focused advice.

  • Excellent communication, negotiation and relationship management skills, with the confidence to engage and influence at executive and Board level.

  • Ability to quickly understand ongoing matters, establish effective stakeholder relationships and operate independently from the outset.

  • Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and exercise sound judgement in a fast-paced environment.

  • Experience supervising or managing junior lawyers.

  • A genuine interest in working for a leading business news and information organisation.

Desirable

  • Experience advising on major technology transformation projects.

job.description:
About us

The Financial Times ranks among the world’s foremost news organisations. It is known globally for its authority, integrity, and accuracy. Its mission is to provide quality information and services across the globe.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, build work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world.

In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing.

Your future at the FT will be filled with opportunities that challenge and encourage you. With no fixed path, you’ll discover new skills and forge a career that can take you anywhere.

Develop a newsworthy career at the FT.

Our dedication to inclusion and fairness

We believe everyone should have a fair opportunity to contribute, succeed, and reach their full potential. That means ensuring everyone is heard, respected, and valued, while identifying and removing barriers that may get in the way. Our dedication is to be an employer role model, grounded in inclusion and fairness for all.

The role

We’re looking for a Senior Product Designer to join our Editorial Technology team, helping build the tools journalists and editors use to compose, manage, and publish world-class journalism.

You’ll build experiences across Spark, our newsroom content management system (CMS), and related editorial tools supporting written stories, video and audio.

This role involves working on intricate products that directly aid journalism production at the FT. Work often starts without a clear brief or defined project. You will need to be comfortable investigating problems, grasping detailed workflows, and helping decide the appropriate course.

Collaborating with product managers, engineers, and newsroom colleagues, you'll merge user research, systems thinking, and strong design skills to develop intuitive, accessible tools for expert users.

You'll also consider how editorial tools interact with the reader experiences they facilitate across our website and apps, partnering with our Customer Products teams as needed.

AI is increasingly crafting editorial workflows, and you'll have chances to explore how new technologies can assist journalists and editors. These include tools that improve editorial quality and accuracy.

Key responsibilities

  • Lead the end-to-end build process, from early problem framing and discovery through information architecture, exploration, prototyping, testing and delivery.
  • Develop a deep understanding of how journalists and editors work, using research, workflow mapping and direct engagement to find opportunities for improvement.
  • Partner with product managers and engineers to build product direction, define problems and establish clear priorities, particularly where requirements are ambiguous.
  • Build intuitive, accessible experiences for complex editorial workflows, including the creation and management of written and multimedia content.
  • Work closely with engineering teams to understand technical architecture, data, systems and constraints, ensuring built solutions are practical and achievable.
  • Build positive relationships with newsroom collaborators, bringing their expertise into the development process while applying sound design judgement.
  • Consider how editorial tools connect with customer-facing experiences, collaborating with Customer Products teams to support consistency and shared development patterns.
  • Communicate build decisions, recommendations and trade-offs clearly, helping teams navigate complexity and make informed decisions.
  • Investigate ways AI can assist editorial workflows, such as quality and accuracy checks, while collaborating closely with editorial, product, and engineering colleagues.
  • Use AI-enabled tools such as Codex or Figma Make, where appropriate, to prototype, test ideas and communicate technical assumptions.
  • Stay informed about developments in AI-assisted build and prototyping, bringing relevant approaches and ideas into the team.

  • Experience crafting and delivering complex digital products, including internal tools and workflows for expert users.

  • Strong product and systems thinking, with an ability to understand how interconnected tools, workflows and technologies work together.
  • A thoughtful and analytical approach to problem-solving, with the confidence to challenge assumptions and explore alternative solutions.
  • Experience planning and conducting proportionate user research, combining qualitative and quantitative insights to inform development decisions.
  • Sufficient technical understanding to collaborate effectively with engineers and navigate complex systems, data and technical constraints.
  • Strong Figma and prototyping skills, with practical experience applying accessibility principles.
  • Experience using AI-assisted prototyping or development tools, with the judgement to assess their opportunities and limitations.
  • Excellent communication and collaborator management skills, with the ability to build positive relationships across multidisciplinary teams.
  • Confidence working through ambiguity, crafting requirements and helping teams move towards clear, considered solutions.

Desirable

  • Experience crafting content management systems, editorial platforms or newsroom tools.
  • A grasp of digital publishing workflows, including the creation and management of multimedia content.
  • Experience working on products that connect complex internal systems with customer-facing digital experiences.

job.description:
About us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.

Our commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion

We believe everyone should have a fair opportunity to contribute, succeed, and reach their full potential. That means ensuring everyone is heard, respected, and valued, while identifying and removing barriers that may get in the way. Our commitment is to be an employer role model, grounded in inclusion and fairness for all.We want every application to receive fair and thoughtful consideration; therefore, all applications are reviewed by a member of our recruitment team, not by AI.

 

About the Role

The Financial Times is globally renowned for premium business and financial journalism. Behind our world-class reporting is a highly sophisticated technological ecosystem that ensures our journalism is structured, discoverable, and rapidly delivered to support a global subscriber base.

We are looking for a highly technical Senior Product Manager to join FT Core and help shape the product strategy for our Content & Metadata (C&M) Platform. The C&M platform acts as the central nervous system between our content creation (Spark CMS) and our downstream consumers—powering FT.com, our mobile apps, Specialist publications, B2B syndication, and new AI-driven experiences.

This is a senior Individual Contributor (IC) role that requires deep technical curiosity and domain expertise. You will not have direct reports; instead, you will partner closely with a Principal Engineer and three Tech Leads, collectively guiding the product vision for an execution team of 12-13 engineers. You will also collaborate extensively across FT Core (specifically Access & Identity), Editorial Tech, Data Science, Commercial (B2B), Editorial, and Legal to ensure our metadata and content pipelines serve diverse and complex needs.

 

What You Will Do

  • Drive Platform Strategy: Co-create and champion the product roadmap for the Content & Metadata platform in partnership with engineering leadership, ensuring FT journalism is treated as a highly structured, reusable, and discoverable asset.
  • Deep Technical Partnership: Work daily with a Principal Engineer and Tech Leads. Your deep understanding of content platforms, API-driven architectures, document stores (MongoDB), and graph databases (Neo4j) will be critical in making collaborative architectural tradeoffs and earning the team's trust.
  • Shape Knowledge Management & Ontologies: Collaborate to guide the evolution of the FT’s Knowledge Graph, helping ensure content is semantically segmented, enriched with accurate metadata, and connected to power advanced search and AI use cases.
  • Stakeholder Alignment: Act as the bridge between highly technical engineering teams and cross-functional business stakeholders, translating B2B commercial goals, editorial requirements, and legal compliance into actionable, shared technical goals.

 

Key Focus Areas & Challenges We're Tackling Next

You will be joining a team working on some of the most complex and exciting content architecture challenges in the industry. Over the next 6-12 months, you will help us tackle:

  • The Shift to "Knowledge Component" APIs: We are transitioning from delivering "whole articles" to exposing discrete, machine-readable components. You will help us solve the challenge of achieving near 100% representation of all journalism components (including custom code and graphics) downstream so that AI models, search algorithms, and B2B partners can consume granular data without losing context.
  • Building an In-House AI "Knowledge Layer": You will collaborate with the team to develop in-house, AI-powered natural language processing capabilities that enhance content understanding, metadata enrichment, and knowledge discovery. This involves navigating the complexities of low-latency, real-time tagging.
  • Leveraging the "Abstract Syntax Tree" Foundation: We recently implemented a unified "Abstract Syntax Tree" foundation across our publishing stack. You will get to capitalize on this architecture to collaboratively phase out legacy capabilities (like the Internal Content API) and rapidly introduce new, universally supported content formats.
  • Enabling Production AI Access: You will partner closely with the Access & Identity platform to figure out how best to supply the structured schema and Knowledge Component APIs required to build a production-grade Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, paving the way for secure LLM integrations.

 

What We Are Looking For

  • Domain Expertise: Extensive product management experience within a media company's content platform, or deeply relevant experience working for a vendor of content/metadata management solutions.
  • Technical Depth: You aren't just comfortable around engineers; you are excited by the technical details. You must have practical experience with document databases (e.g., MongoDB), graph databases (e.g., Neo4j), API design, and content distribution technologies like RSS feeds.
  • Taxonomy & Ontology Fluency: A strong, proven background in taxonomies, ontologies, and semantic content structuring.
  • Search & Content Discovery: A good understanding of modern search technologies, information retrieval, and content discovery, including how metadata, semantic search, and AI-powered capabilities improve content accessibility.
  • Senior IC Capabilities: Exceptional ability to lead by influence. You can confidently debate technical details with Principal Engineers while effectively communicating strategic value to commercial and editorial leadership.
  • Systems Thinker: A natural ability to navigate complex, multi-domain environments and understand how a change in the upstream CMS impacts downstream AI models, B2B feeds, and consumer apps.

 

Benefits

  • Annual bonus scheme
  • 25 days paid leave
  • 24/7 Employee Assistance Program
  • Life Insurance
  • Enhanced Parental Leave policy
  • Food Allowance
  • Multisport Card
  • Both in house and external training programs
  • Your own training dedicated budget (for conferences, courses etc.)

job.title: Singapore Correspondent
job.description:
About us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world.

In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing.

Your future at the FT will be filled with opportunities that challenge and inspire you. With no fixed path, you’ll discover new skills and forge a career that can take you anywhere.

Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

 

Our commitment to inclusion and fairness

We believe everyone should have a fair opportunity to contribute, succeed, and reach their full potential. That means ensuring everyone is heard, respected, and valued, while identifying and removing barriers that may get in the way. Our commitment is to be an employer role model, grounded in inclusion and fairness for all.

We want every application to receive fair and thoughtful consideration; therefore, all applications are reviewed by a member of our recruitment team, not by AI. 

 

The Role

The Financial Times is seeking a Singapore Correspondent to cover one of the world’s most important financial centres. Normally operating solo - although in close cooperation with the SE Asia correspondent and the finance team around the world - the role covers everything from investment banks to oil trading and local politics. For an enterprising reporter, the scope is considerable.

Singapore has evolved into one of Asia’s main financial hubs and a global centre for commodity trading. All the dealmaking is of core interest to the FT, as are the numerous entrepreneurs and family offices - most especially from China - that have set up shop. The city-state attracts its share of colourful characters and dubious behaviour: from the collapse of Barings to the Wirecard scandal, significant parts of the action were in Singapore.

The city is not just a centre for making deals; it is an important player itself. Temasek and GIC are role models for many of the world’s sovereign wealth funds and their activity is another important source of stories. Singapore’s much-admired social model, and the tensions that exist in Singaporean society nonetheless, often interest the outside world.

The Singapore correspondent also has responsibility for Malaysia, which is enjoying a resurgence in the semiconductor industry, and charting an independent course in regional geopolitics. There may also be opportunities to cover stories elsewhere in SE Asia, especially when following supply chains and deals that pass through Singapore.

News is the heart of the job - and you will find strong demand from FT editors - but we want and expect the correspondent to write across a range of formats, from sharp analysis to magazine features. There will be opportunities for travel. Singapore is an important venue for FT Live and you will be asked to represent the FT at events. 

Your Skills

The core of the job is writing and reporting. You will have solid experience as a journalist, most likely in financial reporting or as a foreign correspondent, with a demonstrated ability to cultivate sources and break news. You should be able to write for all parts of the website and newspaper, from strong spot news to deft analysis on a range of subjects.

You will be motivated and full of ideas for stories, not just waiting for the news to arrive. Good communication skills are important. You should regularly pitch ideas to editors in Hong Kong and deliver copy when promised. You should also be collegiate: forging a close relationship with FT correspondents across the region will be crucial to your success.

Singapore is one of the world’s wealthiest cities and a comfortable place to live. The reporting environment, however, requires a degree of resilience and diplomacy. The state maintains tight control over the local media. Some information may not be publicly announced or readily available, requiring a correspondent to work hard and keep up their sources in order to stay in the game.

 

Please submit your application by the end of the day, Thursday 3rd December 2026.

 

The use of AI

Original reporting, great writing and intelligent commentary lie at the heart of FT journalism. Our readers trust us to produce quality journalism that is accurate, fair and insightful. This is why FT editorial staff do not by default use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to write articles or create other reader-facing content. For specific and pre-approved cases, AI can be harnessed for certain tasks, such as assisting data research for investigations.  

We expect applicants to the FT newsroom to refrain from using AI in their test submissions, and any written materials should be a genuine reflection of their own knowledge, skills and experiences. We encourage candidates only to employ AI as a tool to help with research and interview readiness for a role. 

Candidates should be aware that the use of AI throughout the application process is monitored to ensure a fair and transparent hiring process for all.

 

What’s in it for you? Our benefits

Our benefits vary by location but we are committed to providing best-in-class perks across all our offices. These include generous annual leave, medical cover, inclusive parental leave packages, subsidised gym memberships and opportunities to give back to the community. Full details of our benefits are available here.

FT Newsroom staff are expected to work onsite a minimum of three days per week, subject to role requirements and regular review. While flexible working requests will be considered, not all patterns are suitable for Editorial roles.

 

Accessibility

We are a disability confident employer and Valuable 500 signatory. Please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments/personalisation as part of the application process or to enable you to attend an interview. If you would like to discuss your requirements or have any questions, email talent@ft.com and a member of our team will be happy to help.

job.description:
About the Role

Fox Tech runs one of the most complex 24/7 streaming and broadcast operations in the industry. Our overnight and weekend coverage depends on people who can move smoothly between disciplines, so we're hiring a Floating Operations Specialist who can cover wherever the business needs them most.

This is not a single-desk job. On one shift you might be monitoring live event streams for FOX One, FOX Sports, and FOX Nation. On the next, you might be running master control playlists or watching SCTE ad markers and CDN dashboards in the Media Control Center. You'll learn each area, build the skills to work in it independently, and help the team respond quickly when priorities change mid-shift.

If you get energy from switching gears, learning new systems, and adapting to whatever the night brings, this role was built for you.(add in get to expand technical stack)

What You'll Do

  • Digital Operations: Monitor live events, app clients, and video performance across FOX One, FOX Sports, FOX Nation, and Tubi. Run pre-flight checks, encoder validations, entitlement sweeps, and post-event validation (DVR, highlights, short-form), and complete regular app sweeps for functionality and parity.
  • Master Control: Support media ingest, quality control, assembly, playout, and distribution for pre-programmed and live content. Perform on-air switching and run automation playlists in multicast and live sports environments.
  • Media Control Center: Monitor SCTE markers, CDN performance, and transmission dashboards for signal health and delivery quality. Support inbound contribution and outbound distribution across linear and OTT platforms.
  • Incident & Handoff Support: Log incidents accurately in JIRA, PagerDuty, and ServiceNow, escalate issues to the right team, and write clear shift handoff notes for the morning team.
  • Documentation: Help create and update runbooks, checklists, and playbooks as processes evolve.
  • Cross-Team Coverage: Step in to support Business Continuity, Disaster Recovery, and Live Media teams when needed.

What You Need

  • Strong attention to detail, checklists, and ticket documentation/ escalation
  • Demonstrated ability to learn new tools and workflows quickly and apply them under time pressure
  • Clear written and verbal communication, especially for handoffs and incident updates
  • Availability for overnight, weekend, and holiday shifts

Nice to Have, not a Dealbreaker

  • Bachelor's degree in a technical or related field
  • Experience in a 24/7 environment such as master control, broadcast operations, a network operations center, or digital streaming operations
  • Bilingual Spanish/English
  • Prior experience leading or documenting incidents

What Success Looks Like

  • You can move from one area to another without losing focus or accuracy.
  • You stay calm when priorities change in the middle of a shift and adjust the plan without being asked.
  • You notice small details, such as a missing ad marker or a slow app load, and act on them.
  • You learn a new system quickly, ask good questions, and document what you learn for the next person.
  • Teammates count on you to cover gaps, and you pick up the work that needs doing.

job.title: Broadcast Maintenance Engineer
job.description:
The Broadcast Maintenance Engineer will perform tasks associated with the installation, operation, repair, and maintenance of various media technologies for three FOX owned and operated multi-platform television stations. Examples include master control and production automation systems, encoding/decoding and various streaming technologies, video switchers, audio mixers, cameras, robotics, character generators, playback servers, transmitters, satellite distribution systems, desktop computers, networking equipment, and various facility needs as assigned. System examples include Bitcentral, Evertz, Sony, Panasonic, Calrec, Vizrt Tricaster, Adobe, RTS, LiveU, Arista, Cisco, Rohde & Schwarz, and IHSE. The engineer will play an important role in maintaining and operating these systems to support live programming. Highlights include NFL, NCAA football and basketball, MLB, FIFA, NASCAR, and many more.

A SNAPSHOT OF YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Maintenance of broadcast equipment including routing and switching systems, control room and studio equipment, receivers and links, edit systems, live vehicles, RF and ENG equipment
  • Maintain RF sites and equipment including transmitters, translators, TVROs, STL/TSLs, ICRs, RPUs, 2-way, remote controls and fiber paths
  • Maintain inventory of spare and replacement parts
  • Maintain building, grounds and support systems at RF sites

WHAT YOU WILL NEED

  • Previous experience within a television station or similar industry supporting and installing broadcast equipment, production systems, video streaming technologies, and/or IT-related components
  • Skilled with both SDI and IP video standards, such as SMPTE 2110, NDI, and Dante
  • Strong troubleshooting skills and willingness to learn new technologies
  • Ability to communicate effectively with management, vendors, and co-workers; work efficiently and meet deadlines
  • Able to work independently and as a member of a team
  • Ability to sit and stand for extended periods of time
