job.description:
About Gray Media:

Today, we are a growing multimedia company headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. We are the nation's largest owner of top-rated local television stations and digital assets serving 117 full-power television markets that collectively reach approximately 37% of US television households. The portfolio includes 80 markets with the top-rated television station and 100 markets with the first and/or second-highest-rated television station in average all-day ratings across 116 of such markets that were measured by Nielsen in 2025. We also own the largest Telemundo Affiliate group with 46 markets and Gray Digital Media, a full-service digital agency offering national and local clients digital marketing strategies with the most advanced digital products and services. Our additional media properties include video production companies Raycom Sports, Tupelo Media Group, and PowerNation Studios, and studio production facilities Assembly Atlanta and Third Rail Studios.

About KSLA:

KSLA News 12 is the aggressive, National Edward R. Murrow Award-winning CBS affiliate serving the region known as the ArkLaTex. The station is the market’s leader in timely and accurate reporting of breaking news, investigative journalism, award-winning storytelling, and First Alert Weather. KSLA News 12 serves its community on all on-air, digital, and mobile platforms, embracing the innovation of the industry. In the center of the ArkLaTex is the Shreveport/Bossier City metroplex where the best of Louisiana, Texas and Arkansas culture is combined to create a vibrant and comfortable lifestyle.

Job Summary/Description:

Are you a relentless seeker of facts who refuses to take "no comment" for an answer? KSLA News 12 is looking for an Investigative Reporter/MMJ who doesn't just report the news but uncovers it. We need a storyteller who can turn complex data into high-impact, urgent narratives that demand attention—whether someone is watching on their big screen or scrolling through their feed. If you have the grit to dig deep and the digital savvy with a reach beyond measure, we have just the place for you on our award-winning team. 

Duties/Responsibilities include (but are not limited to):

What You'll Do:
• Lead the investigation: Research, develop, and produce groundbreaking investigative content that holds the powerful accountable and serves our community.
• Own the data: Dive deep into spreadsheets, public records, and databases to find the "smoking gun" that others miss.
• Tell unforgettable stories: Use creative, outstanding storytelling techniques to make complex investigations relatable, urgent, and visually compelling.
• Drive digital impact: Craft digital-first investigative pieces, social media reels, and interactive content that engages our audience across all platforms.
• Balance the beat: Manage a pipeline of longer-term projects while remaining agile enough to apply investigative techniques to daily coverage and breaking news.

Qualifications/Requirements:

What You Bring:
• The "Investigative Itch": At least 2 years of dedicated investigative and general assignment reporting experience with a proven track record of digging.
• Technical Toolkit: Proficiency in computer-assisted reporting (CAR) and proficiency with databases.
• Digital Fluency: You know how to optimize a story for search, engage a social audience, and use digital tools to enhance your reporting.
• Relentless Urgency: A "get it first, get it right" mentality that thrives under deadline pressure.
• Human Connection: The ability to build trust with sources and tell the human stories behind the data.
• Sharp Judgment: Strong news ethics and the legal knowledge to navigate complex public records requests and sensitive interviews.

job.title: INVESTIGATIVE REPORTER/ANCHOR - KWCH
job.description:
About Gray Media:

Today, we are a growing multimedia company headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. We are the nation's largest owner of top-rated local television stations and digital assets serving 117 full-power television markets that collectively reach approximately 37% of US television households. Our additional media properties include video production companies Raycom Sports, Tupelo Media Group, and PowerNation Studios, and studio production facilities Assembly Atlanta and Third Rail Studios.

About KWCH:

KWCH (12 News) is a CBS television affiliate serving Wichita as well as central and western Kansas. KWCH is the market leader, providing viewers with local news, weather, and breaking news coverage. The news team is a 2026 National Murrow Award winner. Wichita is ranked as one of the best cities for young professionals - where you can enjoy a high quality of life, a low cost of living, and a vibrant community.

Job Summary/Description:

Do you have a relentless curiosity that won't let a story go until you've uncovered the truth? Are you the kind of journalist who thrives on the "big story" of the day—not just reporting what happened, but explaining why it matters and providing the deep context our audience craves? 12 News is looking for a dynamic Investigative Reporter/Anchor to join our team. We need someone who can pivot from a months-long deep dive to a high-stakes breaking news situation without missing a beat. Whether you’re behind the anchor desk or out in the field, you’ll be the voice of authority and the face of accountability for our community across every screen.

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: 

• Uncover the truth: Lead our investigative efforts by producing high-impact, long-form content that holds the powerful accountable and sparks real change.
• Provide instant context: Own the "big story" of the day by digging into the background, records, and data to give our audience a deeper understanding of breaking news as it happens.
• Own the anchor desk: Deliver newscasts with authority, energy, and a conversational style that connects with viewers on TV and streaming platforms.
• Drive digital engagement: Craft compelling investigative stories specifically for digital and social media—because our audience shouldn't have to wait for the 6 PM news to see your best work.
• Master the craft: Shoot, edit, and write your own stories with a sharp eye for visual storytelling and a commitment to journalism ethics.
• Lead in the clutch: Handle breaking news situations on-air with calm, confidence, and the ability to ad-lib when the teleprompter goes dark.
• Connect with the community: Represent 12 News professionally in the field and on social media, building the trust necessary to land the next big tip.

Qualifications/Requirements:

• The right foundation: You have a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Journalism (or a related field) and at least 2-3 years of on-air television reporting experience—though we’re always willing to train the right person with the right fire.
• Investigative grit: You have a proven track record of digging deep, filing FOIAs, and finding the stories others miss.
• Versatility: You’re just as comfortable anchoring a daily newscast as you are tracking down a lead in the rain.
• Digital-first mindset: You understand that "the story" lives on social media, our app, and our website just as much as it does on broadcast.
• Killer news judgment: You know what matters to our community and can quickly identify the investigative angle in a daily news cycle.
• Technical savvy: You can operate a field camera, light a scene, and edit your own masterpieces (ENPS and AP Style are your second languages).
• Urgency and empathy: You care about the people behind the stories and feel the fire to get the facts right—and get them first.
• A desire to win: You’re a team player who welcomes feedback and is always looking for ways to sharpen your skills.
• Flexibility: News doesn't follow a 9-to-5 schedule, and neither do you. You're ready to work when and where the story takes you.

About WFSB:

WFSB Channel 3, a Gray Media station, is the undisputed market leader in Connecticut and Southern New England. We dominate on-air, online, and on the stream. 

WFSB is the market’s #1 news brand across traditional broadcast ratings, digital reach, and social metrics. 

We are not just keeping pace with modern journalism; we are leading the way. WFSB produces more live streaming content than any other television station in New England. Located in a scenic region, along the coast between New York City and Boston, WFSB offers the ideal balance of top-tier, fast-paced journalism and the best of New England living.

Job Summary/Description:

WFSB / Gray Media is seeking a forward-thinking, hands-on IT Manager / Assistant Chief Engineer to bridge broadcast operations and modern IT infrastructure. This dual-focus role leads day-to-day station IT operations and systems administration while serving as the primary backup to the Chief Engineer on core television technologies and broadcast facilities.

The ideal candidate possesses deep, fluent expertise in enterprise IT (networking, virtualization, cybersecurity, directory services, and storage) combined with a solid working knowledge of broadcast television systems (SDI/SMPTE ST 2110 signal flow, production switchers, master control automation, newsroom computer systems, and RF transmission basics). You will ensure uninterrupted on-air operations, maintain IT compliance with corporate standards, and serve as technical operations lead when the Chief Engineer is off-site.

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: 

Information Technology & Systems Administration:
● Manage, configure, and maintain all local station IT infrastructure: Windows Server environments, Active Directory/Azure AD, group policies, and enterprise endpoint workstations (Windows/Mac).
● Oversee on-premises and hybrid virtualization clusters (VMware vSphere/ESXi, Hyper-V), SAN/NAS high-speed shared storage, and robust disaster recovery/backup platforms.
● Manage local network topology, including Cisco/Arista/Dell L2/L3 enterprise switches, VLAN segmentation (separating broadcast production, corporate IT, Dante/AES67, and guest traffic), routing, firewalls, and VPN access.
● Champion station cybersecurity posture in alignment with Gray Media corporate IT: endpoint protection, patch management, access control, multi-factor authentication, and rapid security incident remediation.
● Provide direct IT escalation support for newsroom computer systems (ENPS/iNEWS), non-linear editing workflows (Adobe Creative Cloud, Avid, Edius), and field contribution units (LiveU, Dejero).
● Partner with Regional IT leadership and corporate engineering to plan, deploy, and document technology rollouts and software lifecycle upgrades.

Broadcast Engineering & Operational Backup:
● Act as the designated technical backup to the Chief Engineer, maintaining operational continuity across studio, control room, master control, and transmission facilities during absences or on-call emergencies.
● Support and troubleshoot broadcast production equipment, including production switchers (Grass Valley, Ross), Crispin master control automation, Chyron graphics engines, audio consoles (Wheatstone, Calrec), and multi-viewer/routing infrastructure.
● Understand SDI, HDMI, and IP-based media transport (SMPTE ST 2110, NDI, SRT, Dante/AES67) signal flow, conversion gear, and video monitoring systems.
● Assist in monitoring and basic first-line troubleshooting of transmission systems, microwave studio-to-transmitter links (STL), satellite downlinks, EAS decoders, and transmitter facility infrastructure (HVAC, liquid cooling systems, generators, and UPS units).
● Coordinate with production, news, and operations crews to resolve live on-air technical discrepancies quickly and calmly.
● Maintain accurate, up-to-date station wiring diagrams, network schematics, rack elevations, and standard operating procedures (SOPs).

Leadership & Project Management:
● Lead and execute technology implementation projects from scoping and rack installation to commissioning and user training.
● Manage technical vendor relationships, RMA processes, warranties, and software support agreements.
● Promote a culture of proactive maintenance, cleanliness, security, and continuous improvement across all equipment racks and technical spaces.
● Participate in an engineering on-call rotation to support 24/7/365 news and broadcast operations.

Qualifications/Requirements:

Required Qualifications:
● 5+ years of combined hands-on experience in enterprise Information Technology systems administration and broadcast/media production environments.
● Proven expertise in Windows Server administration, Active Directory, DNS/DHCP, VMware/virtualized environments, and enterprise backup solutions.
● Solid understanding of TCP/IP networking, managed switches, VLAN configurations, subnets, QoS, and network troubleshooting tools (Wireshark, traceroute, etc.).
● Working knowledge of basic television broadcast workflows and equipment (SDI signal paths, video routing switchers, audio distribution, sync/timing, and studio cameras).
● Familiarity with newsroom production systems (e.g., ENPS, iNEWS) and digital media encoding/transcoding formats.
● Ability to diagnose and resolve complex technical problems rapidly under live broadcast deadlines.
● Strong organizational, documentation, communication, and interpersonal skills.
● Valid driver’s license with an acceptable driving record.
● Availability to work flexible hours, including on-call response for breaking news, severe weather, off-hours maintenance windows, and emergencies.

Preferred Qualifications:
● Associate or Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Broadcast Engineering, or equivalent military/technical training.
● Relevant industry IT certifications (CompTIA Network+/Security+, CCNA, Microsoft Certified, or VMware VCP).
● Broadcast engineering certifications such as SBE Certified Broadcast Technologist (CBT) or Certified Broadcast Networking Technologist (CBNT).
● Familiarity with modern broadcast IP technologies (SMPTE ST 2110, ST 2022-6, Dante, Ravenna, NDI).
● Exposure to transmitter site fundamentals, RF systems, ATSC 1.0/3.0 exciters, or backup power generators.

Application Instructions:

Hawaii News Now is looking for a highly organized, creative, and experienced Lifestyle Producer to join our Emmy Award-winning team. The Lifestyle Producer will help produce some of Hawaii News Now’s most dynamic lifestyle programming, including HI Now Daily, Kitchen Scraps, station specials, and

Duties/Responsibilities will include (but are not limited to) the following:

Core Responsibilities:

troubleshooting or supporting teammates
• Contribute ideas and look for creative ways to make our shows and specials better

Our ideal candidate is a strong producer and natural organizer who works well with a team, communicates clearly, stays calm under pressure, and takes ownership from planning through execution. Just as important, we are looking for a true team player who is willing to jump in and play whatever role is needed to get the show on the air and make the product great.

• Previous television or video producing experience
• Exceptional organizational and time management skills
• Strong writing, storytelling, and production skills
• Ability to juggle multiple priorities and deadlines without losing attention to detail
• Strong communication and collaboration skills
• Someone who takes initiative, follows through, and can be counted on
• Excellent judgment and problem-solving skills
• Ability to perform well under pressure in a deadline-driven environment
• A positive, team-focused approach and a willingness to pitch in wherever needed

• You are equally comfortable developing a great segment, building a rundown, coordinating a complicated shoot, floor directing a show, or jumping in to solve a last-minute production challenge.

About KSFY/KDLT:

Sioux Falls and the surrounding area remain one of the fastest-growing regions in the Upper Midwest and are home to 300,000 people, constituting more than 30% of the state's population. Healthcare and finance make up much of a diverse and broad workforce. The business climate in South Dakota continues to be one of the top in the nation, fueled by no state income tax and a diverse workforce.

There is never a shortage of activities or events, with summers packed with outdoor festivals and concerts, including free concerts at the Levitt at the Falls outdoor music venue.

Still, many also enjoy the city’s nearly 30 miles of bike trails and parks, including the namesake of the city, the beautiful waterfalls of the Big Sioux River! Yes, winters can be challenging, but it does not mean people hibernate. Colder temperatures provide plenty of outdoor and indoor activities all winter long. From parades like the annual Parade of Lights down Phillips Avenue to outdoor ice skating parks, life does not slow down in the winter in Sioux Falls.

The city is home to a 12,000-seat arena that is continually hosting major events and entertainment acts, ranging from the Professional Bull Riders, college and semi-professional hockey, indoor football, to concerts with names like Paul McCartney, Garth Brooks, and Elton John.

The city is also home to a new indoor aquatic center, an indoor ice-skating facility, a basketball arena, and an indoor tennis complex. Multiple award-winning golf courses, both public and private, surround the city, offering a relaxing and challenging day on the links

Culinary appetites never need to look far from being satiated, as there is no shortage of places to eat. Not only is Sioux Falls home to many familiar restaurant chains, but it’s also known for many great locally owned, nationally recognized restaurants and restaurateurs. For those looking for a quick weekend getaway, nothing to fear. You can drive to Omaha in three hours, Minneapolis in four, and the Black Hills in five. Since Sioux Falls is centrally located in the Midwest, direct and connecting flights to almost anywhere in the United States are often less than a few hours in length.

Dakota News Now is an award-winning television operation serving viewers in the eastern half of South Dakota as well as portions of southwest Minnesota and northwest Iowa. The stations operate from a relatively new studio in downtown Sioux Falls, branding all stations under the Dakota News Now umbrella. The facilities put Dakota News Now on the cutting edge of television and news gathering technology, making it one of the most state-of-the-art television stations in the market and the region. The Dakota News Now team produces 36 hours of news each week.

Some of our employees have been here for more than 25 years. For others, this is their first job out of college. It’s a great mix that gives us different perspectives while covering the news and assisting local clientele in achieving their marketing goals.

Learn more about Dakota News Now & Sioux Falls here: https://www.dakotanewsnow.com/page/ksfykdlt-careers/

Monday - Friday

Full-Time

Job Summary/Description:

Do you live for the science of weather but also love the art of digital storytelling? We're looking for a Meteorologist who can forecast with precision, deliver clear, concise weather segments in linear newscasts, create a high-energy, daily weather show on our primary streaming channel, and engage viewers on web and social media. This isn't just about reading a map; it's about owning the screen—whether it's a 65-inch TV in a living room or a 6-inch phone in someone's hand. If you're ready to lead the charge in how Vermont, New York, and New Hampshire experience the weather across every platform, we want to talk to you.

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Forecast with precision: Deliver accurate, high-stakes forecasts for a topographically complex three-state region (Vermont, New York's North Country, and New Hampshire) where the weather changes as fast as the headlines.
- Create compelling visuals: Use The Weather Company Max systems to build creative, data-driven graphics that tell a visual story, not just show the current temperature.
- Step into the spotlight: Provide high-quality on-air delivery for our weekday noon newscast, and fill-in for our weekday morning meteorologist, maintaining a professional and authoritative presence that our viewers trust.
- Go live in the field: Take the weather story to the streets, covering community and weather events live from the elements and from our StreetView3 weather vehicle.
- Own the stream: Produce and host a daily, interactive weather show on our primary streaming channel, making complex science accessible and engaging for a digital audience.
- Craft digital content: Create "must-click" weather stories and social media updates that stop the scroll and keep our community informed on hard deadlines.
- Collaborate across platforms: Work seamlessly with the news and digital teams to ensure our weather coverage is cohesive, urgent, and first.

Qualifications/Requirements:

- The Credentials: A four-year degree in meteorology or a related field.
- On-Air Presence: Proven experience presenting weather on-camera with confidence, clarity, and a bit of personality.
- Tech Savvy: Deep understanding of The Weather Company Max products and the ability to navigate CMS and ENPS like a pro.
- Audience-First Mindset: A genuine passion for social media and a knack for creating content that resonates on TikTok, Instagram, and beyond.
- Urgency and Accuracy: The ability to stay calm and deliver life-saving information during high-stakes flooding, severe weather and winter storms.
- Communication Skills: You're a skilled writer and a speaker who can translate complex science into "human speak" effortlessly.
- A Clean Record: A valid driver's license and a clean driving record are required.

About KCTV:

KCTV5 is the CBS affiliate serving the Kansas City metropolitan area.

Job Summary/Description:

KCTV5 is seeking a forward-thinking Morning Multi-Media Journalist (MMJ) who knows how to connect with Kansas City viewers wherever they start their day—on broadcast, streaming, or mobile platforms. This journalist will deliver energetic live reports throughout our 4:30–9:00 a.m. newscasts, provide live field updates for our streaming channel, develop focused coverage for our noon show, and create audience-first digital and vertical video content. If you are passionate about reach, engagement, community trust, and turning one story into multiple dynamic outputs, we want you on our team.

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

* Broadcast Impact: Report live with urgency, clarity, and personality across our 4:30–9:00 a.m. morning newscasts; write, shoot, and edit a compelling package or report tailored for the Noon broadcast.
* Streaming Coverage: Periodically join our continuous streaming channel live from the field to give viewers real-time updates, deeper context, and "what we know right now" coverage.
* Platform-First Storytelling: Craft vertical short-form explainers (Reels/TikTok/Shorts) and clear digital web stories that prioritize utility ("what this means to you"), community engagement, and verified facts.
* Audience Engagement & Trust: Foster two-way communication by monitoring morning comments, answering audience questions on digital channels, and clearly distinguishing between confirmed facts and developing details.
* Collaborative Daily Pitching: Pitch original, audience-focused story ideas daily that matter to local families, commuters, and workers starting their day across the Kansas City metro.
* Efficient Field Workflow: Shoot, write, and edit high-quality horizontal and vertical assets with reuse in mind, maximizing field time and newsroom collaboration.

Qualifications/Requirements:

* Proven Experience: 2–5 years of professional reporting experience as an MMJ or live reporter in a commercial newsroom.
* Live Broadcast Presence: Demonstrated ability to deliver compelling, active, and unscripted live field reports across a fast-paced multi-hour morning block (4:30–9:00 a.m.) and turn a polished story for the midday/noon show.
* Platform Literacy & Mobile Video: Hands-on experience creating audience-first vertical videos (Reels, TikTok, YouTube Shorts) utilizing strong hooks, clear on-screen graphics/captions, and authentic mobile delivery (not just cutdowns of broadcast packages).
* Streaming Agility: Comfort jumping on camera for live, conversational streaming updates from the field, explaining breaking developments and answering "what's next" for digital viewers.
* Technical Proficiency: Demonstrated skill operating field cameras, lighting, mobile gear, cellular transmitters (e.g., LiveU), and desktop/mobile editing software (e.g., Edius, Edits).
* Editorial Judgment & Trust: Uncompromising commitment to accuracy, AP style, sourcing, and transparency, with the ability to clearly label what is confirmed versus developing during fast-moving morning breaking news.
* Fantastic Newsroom Citizenship: Strong collaborative spirit, excellent communication with morning producers and digital desks, and a positive attitude during early-morning hours.
* Valid Driver's License: A clean driving record and willingness to work non-traditional early morning hours.

About KSLA:

KSLA News 12 is the aggressive, National Edward R. Murrow Award-winning CBS affiliate serving the region known as the ArkLaTex. The station is the market’s leader in timely and accurate reporting of breaking news, investigative journalism, award-winning storytelling, and First Alert Weather. KSLA News 12 serves its community on all on-air, digital, and mobile platforms, embracing the innovation of the industry. In the center of the ArkLaTex is the Shreveport/Bossier City metroplex where the best of Louisiana, Texas, and Arkansas culture is combined to create a vibrant and comfortable lifestyle.

Job Summary/Description:

Are you a relentless newsgatherer who lives for the thrill of a breaking story? Do you believe that great storytelling isn’t just about what happens on a TV screen, but how it connects with people on their phones, social feeds, and streaming devices? We’re looking for a Multimedia Journalist (MMJ) at KSLA News 12 who can do it all—find the story, shoot the video, and deliver a confident live report that stops the scroll. If you’re ready to be a community-centered storyteller who prioritizes the audience over the newscast clock, we want to talk to you.

Duties/Responsibilities include (but are not limited to):

What You'll Do:
• Own the story: Develop deep community roots and pitch original, enterprise stories daily that explore the real impact on local lives.
• Master the craft: Schedule interviews, shoot high-quality video, and edit compelling content that you tailor to a 65-inch TV and a smartphone.
• Lead with digital: Share verified updates, photos, and video from the field immediately—because our audience doesn't expect information on a scheduled timer.
• Deliver dynamic live reports: Bring energy and authority to your live hits, whether you’re standing on a street corner during breaking news or walking through a feature story.
• Write for every platform: Craft "web-native" stories with search-friendly headlines and local context that drive engagement across all digital channels.
• Engage your audience: Create platform-specific content like vertical video for social media and standalone clips for YouTube to meet our viewers where they are.
• Collaborate and innovate: Work closely with producers and digital teams to tailor content for different audiences while using analytics to help guide your storytelling.

Qualifications/Requirements:

What You Bring:
• A storyteller’s soul: You have a knack for finding the "human" element in every story and the technical skills to bring it to life visually.
• Multi-platform experience: You’ve spent at least two years (preferred) reporting, shooting, and editing in a fast-paced environment.
• Digital-first mindset: You understand that "news" happens 24/7 and you’re comfortable going live on social or streaming platforms at a moment’s notice.
• Confident communication: You’re a strong writer and an even stronger live reporter who remains calm and clear under pressure.
• Resourcefulness: You’re a "scrappy" newsgatherer who knows how to develop sources and verify information independently.
• Adaptability: You can pivot quickly when a story changes, manage your time like a pro, and you’re ready to work the shifts the news cycle demands (including weekends and holidays).
• Bilingual skills (Bonus!): If you can communicate effectively in both English and Spanish, that’s a huge plus for our community.
• The right foundation: A college degree in journalism or a related field is what we’re looking for.

Job Summary/Description:

Are you the kind of person who is naturally curious about the world around you? KTTC in Rochester, MN, is looking for a high-energy Multimedia Journalist (MMJ) who is ready to start their career by making a real impact. We’re not just looking for an employee; we’re looking for a storyteller who is eager to share facts, seek the truth, and own the news cycle across every screen—from the TV in the living room to the phone in the palm of a viewer's hand.

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:  

What You'll Do:

• Own the news cycle: Gather, shoot, and edit high-impact content for multiple platforms, ensuring our audience stays informed.
• Pitch with purpose: Come ready to the editorial meeting with researched ideas pitched through Microsoft Teams. You’ll have already made the calls and prearranged interviews to hit the ground running.
• Master the multi-platform: Write and adapt stories for different screens—from the morning news to quick social updates and deep-dive web articles.
• Report live from the scene: Be the first on the ground when news breaks, delivering authoritative and calm live reports that keep our viewers connected.
• Verify and validate: Gather and verify factual information through interviews, observation, and deep research—because accuracy is our foundation.
• Manage your time: Take charge of your daily workflow—from getting out the door for fresh video to editing your final masterpiece before the deadline hits.
• Stay agile: Update stories as they evolve and be ready to fill in on different shifts when the news demands it.

Why You'll Love It Here:

• A launchpad for your career: Join a young, energetic newsroom led by anchors with decades of experience who are eager to mentor the next generation of journalists.
• Growth every day: We believe feedback should happen in real time, not just during a yearly review. You’ll grow faster here than anywhere else.
• Innovation focus: KTTC is evolving on purpose—we’re serious about the future of media and want you to help shape it.
• Community impact: Tell stories that actually matter to the people of Rochester and the surrounding area.
• Supportive culture: We value scrappiness and digital innovation, but we also value our people. You’ll have the tools and the team to do your best work.

Qualifications/Requirements:

What You Bring:

• The mindset: Above all else, a relentless desire to learn, seek the truth, and share stories that matter.
• Strong writing chops: You craft scripts and articles that are tight, clear, and compelling (AP style is your best friend).
• Technical potential: While we can teach you to shoot and edit video, a familiarity with camera equipment and systems like ENPS or Edius is a great head start.
• Self-motivated hustle: The ability to work independently in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment without breaking a sweat.
• Versatility: You can manage multiple projects at once and pivot quickly when breaking news hits.
• A valid driver’s license: You’re ready to hit the road and go where the story takes you.
• Human qualities: Empathy for the stories you tell, urgency in how you tell them, and the flexibility to roll with the punches of a dayside shift.

Ready to start your journey and own the news cycle in Rochester? Let’s create something amazing together.

  • The "Gray" Factor: A relentless sense of urgency, a collaborative spirit, and a passion for helping local businesses thrive in a digital-first world.

Why You'll Love It Here:

About KBTX:

KBTX Media operates the CBS and CW affiliates in Bryan-College Station, Texas, serving an 18-county area known as the Brazos Valley. For nearly 70 years, we’ve been the dominant choice for local news and entertainment. Our team produces nearly 40 hours of broadcast content each week, along with a constant presence online at KBTX.com.

KBTX is routinely recognized among the best in the state by organizations including the Associated Press, RTDNA, and the Lone Star EMMY Chapter of the National Academy of Television Arts and Sciences. The station has won four consecutive Texas Association of Broadcasters’ Bonner McLane Public Service awards, and in 2023 won a National Edward R. Murrow Award for Digital content. KBTX is also a recent Texas AP Broadcasters/Freedom of Information Foundation of Texas Station of the Year and Texas Associated Press Broadcasters Station of the Year.

The station has launched the careers of many well-known journalists, meteorologists, and network executives, and takes pride in helping talent grow quickly into the nation’s largest television markets. The work family of KBTX is made up of a group of dedicated, professional, and passionate individuals who are the backbone of our daily mission.

Bryan-College Station, Texas, is a community of more than 250,000 people and the largest single metro in the Waco-Temple-Bryan DMA. The twin cities have a unique small-town feeling, but offer big city amenities, including a vibrant arts community, a city-wide, all-terrain trail system, and world-class dining and nightlife. Bryan and College Station are routinely recognized as a leader in quality of life and as one of the fastest-growing communities in the country.
College Station is home to Texas A&M University, the nation’s largest university. Aggie home football games attract more than 100,000 in the stands, with tens of thousands more camped outside celebrating at tailgates during football weekends.

Learn more about KBTX at www.kbtx.com.

At KSNB Local4, we are building the next generation of local television journalism, and we need a dynamic, forward-thinking leader to anchor our morning and midday broadcasts while driving our OTT streaming coverage. job.title: NEWS DIRECTOR - WIS
job.description:
About Gray Media:

Today, we are a growing multimedia company headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. We are the nation's largest owner of top-rated local television stations and digital assets serving 117 full-power television markets that collectively reach approximately 37% of US television households. Our additional media properties include video production companies Raycom Sports, Tupelo Media Group, and PowerNation Studios, and studio production facilities Assembly Atlanta and Third Rail Studios.

About WIS:

WIS is the #1 local media organization in the capital city market of Columbia, South Carolina. As the top-rated broadcast television station serving South Carolina's Midlands since 1953, WIS offers the opportunity to join an award-winning culture built upon decades of market leadership.

WIS is currently recognized as the South Carolina Broadcasters Association's Station of the Year and has won the award a record 17 times. WIS has earned the Edward R. Murrow Award for Journalism Excellence, the National Association of Broadcasters' Service to America Award, the George Foster Peabody Award, and has more than 70 Emmy nominations in the last 5 years. Among the many notable former journalists who helped set our standard, NBC Today Show co-host Craig Melvin began his career with WIS as an intern, photographer, reporter, then anchor.

WIS produces more than 60 hours of live, local broadcast programming per week, as well as original content for multiple digital platforms. The station offers a unique variety of multiplatform advertising solutions, sponsored content, and professional creative services for businesses of any size.

Columbia, South Carolina, is a vibrant and growing capital city with a diverse population. It is home to the U.S. Army's largest installation for Basic Combat Training, Fort Jackson, along with the University of South Carolina and multiple other colleges and universities. WIS is located downtown, just two blocks from the South Carolina State House.

Our community combines affordable quality of living with a variety of entertainment and activities to accommodate your lifestyle, whether it's our 50,000-acre Lake Murray, our Columbia Fireflies minor league baseball team, the Riverbanks Zoo & Gardens, nearby Congaree National Park, or so much more.

Job Summary/Description:                       

Are you a visionary leader who thrives on the adrenaline of a fast-paced newsroom? Do you believe that being "Your First Alert" isn't just a slogan, but a commitment to keeping a community informed, prepared, and connected across every screen they own? WIS-TV, the #1 local media organization in Columbia, South Carolina, since 1953, is looking for a News Director to lead our award-winning team into the future. We’re looking for a multiplatform strategist and a culture-builder who will inspire a talented staff to reach new heights of journalistic excellence.

Duties/Responsibilities include (but are not limited to):

What You'll Do:
• Lead the legacy: Take the helm of the largest news staff in the market, driving the strategic vision for a station that has been a community staple for over 70 years.
• Own the "Your First Alert" brand: Oversee all systems and workflows to ensure we are the most trusted source for breaking news and weather, delivering urgency and accuracy every single time.
• Drive multiplatform growth: Use data and research to aggressively grow our audience on emerging platforms, ensuring our content is as dynamic on a smartphone as it is on a TV.

• Collaborate across the building: Partner with other station leaders to set and smash collective goals, participating in annual strategic planning to keep WIS at the top.
• Manage with precision: Handle the business side of news, from disciplined budget management and ROI delivery to contract negotiations and HR support, with total confidence.

What You Bring:

• A multiplatform mindset: You produce content for the "news finds me" crowd in today's algorithm-driven environment, and you adapt accordingly as the wind shifts direction.
• Proven leadership experience: You’ve successfully led a newsroom (or a significant department) and have the track record to prove it.
• Impeccable journalistic integrity: You have a deep understanding of media law and ethics, ensuring our reporting is always fair, accurate, and impactful.

• A passion for community: You understand the unique pulse of South Carolina's Midlands and are ready to represent WIS at public events and community initiatives.
• Sense of urgency: You thrive under deadline pressure and know how to lead a team through the chaos of a major breaking news event.

Why You'll Love It Here:
• The #1 spot: You’ll be leading the market leader, with the resources and reputation of a legacy station behind you.
• Innovation at scale: Gray Media is at the forefront of the industry’s evolution. You’ll have the tools and the freedom to experiment and innovate.
• Real community impact: In Columbia, WIS is an institution. You'll feel it the moment you wear our logo anywhere in town, and you'll see the direct results of your team's work every day.
• A deep bench of talent: You’ll work with some of the best journalists in the business who are as passionate about the mission as you are.
• Growth opportunities: We invest in our people with training, tools, mentorship, and more. We want to see you succeed.

Qualifications/Requirements:

• Excellent communication skills, both oral and written.
• Minimum of five years' experience in news programming production, with at least two years' experience in a leadership role.
• Experience guiding, directing, and motivating a team, including setting performance standards and monitoring progress.
• Experience establishing long-range objectives and specifying the strategies and actions to achieve them.
• Ability to identify the developmental needs of others and to coach, mentor, and inspire others to improve their knowledge of skills.
• Experience preparing and maintaining departmental budgets.
• Proficiency with newsroom and station technology.
• Ability to meet deadlines, prioritize assignments, and handle multiple tasks simultaneously.
• Ability to effectively listen to fully understand employee needs and communicate with a team to shape a solution.
• Coachable, committed, and aware, with the ability to accept candid feedback in the spirit that there's always room for improvement.

job.description:

About WECT:

WECT News has been Where News Comes First in Southeastern North Carolina for over 70 years. We're the NBC affiliate in the rapidly growing Wilmington market, serving New Hanover, Brunswick, Columbus, Pender, and Bladen counties that make up the beautiful coastal Cape Fear Region. WECT is the most accessible local news outlet in our market, with WECT.com, News & Weather apps, and streaming platforms. WECT is the dominant #1 station in the market.

Job Summary/Description:

Are you a visual storyteller who lives for the "wow" factor?

Do you thrive on the adrenaline of a breaking story and the satisfaction of a deep-dive community piece? We’re looking for a Multimedia Journalist (MMJ) who doesn't just report the news but owns it—across every screen.

Whether you’re crafting a lead for one of our on-air newscasts, going live on our streaming newscasts in the WECT Digital Studio, or engaging with our audience on social, you’ll be the heartbeat of the Cape Fear region.

If you’re a scrappy, digital-first journalist who wants to make a real impact in southeastern North Carolina, let’s talk.

Duties/Responsibilities will include (but not be limited to):

What You'll Do:
* Own the story: Manage and develop compelling content from initial concept to final publication across digital, social, and broadcast platforms.
* Drive digital engagement: Create platform-specific content that meets our audience where they are—on their phones, their TVs, and everywhere in between.
* Master the craft: Write, edit, and produce high-quality stories with speed, accuracy, and a killer creative eye.
* Respond with urgency: Jump into breaking news situations with authority and calm, keeping our community informed in real-time.
* Connect with the community: Build deep roots in the Cape Fear region, developing sources and uncovering the stories that truly matter to our neighbors.
*Step into the spotlight: Take advantage of potential anchoring opportunities to lead our coverage and connect directly with viewers.

What You Bring:
* A digital-first mindset: You understand that "news" happens 24/7, and you’re ready to feed the beast on social and streaming first.
* Killer storytelling skills: You know how to find the "human" element in every story and make it resonate with an audience.
* Technical chops: You’re a pro with a camera and an editing suite (and you’re not afraid to learn new tools as they emerge).
* Sharp news judgment: You know what’s important, what’s interesting, and how to tell the difference under pressure.
* A positive, "can-do" attitude: You’re a team player who lifts others up and thrives in a collaborative, fast-paced environment.
* Urgency and empathy: You care about the stories you tell and the people they affect, and you move fast to get them right.
* Flexibility: News doesn't follow a 9-to-5 schedule, and neither do you—you’re ready to go where the story takes you.

Qualifications/Requirements:

* Bachelor’s degree in journalism or related field preferred
* Strong writing skills (broadcast and print style)
* Experience with CMS/digital publishing platforms
* Experience with broadcast newsroom software such as ENPS
* Experience with video editing software (preferably Edius)
* Must be able to lift 25-30 lbs and pass a motor vehicle background check

Job Description/Summary:

WMTV 15 News wants a high-energy, digital-first Newscast Producer to join our award-winning team. You will be our utility player: own evening newscasts on-air or streaming, lead your own streaming show, and jump in to help across the week.

Duties/Responsibilities include (but are not limited to):

You will be our utility player: own evening newscasts on-air or streaming, lead your own streaming show, and jump in to help across the week. Our additional media properties include video production companies Raycom Sports, Tupelo Media Group, and PowerNation Studios, as well as studio production facilities Assembly Atlanta and Third Rail Studios.

About KBTX:

KBTX Media operates the CBS and CW affiliates in Bryan-College Station, Texas, serving an 18-county area known as the Brazos Valley. For nearly 70 years, we’ve been the dominant choice for local news and entertainment. Our team produces nearly 40 hours of broadcast content each week, along with a constant presence online at KBTX.com.
KBTX is routinely recognized among the best in the state by organizations including the Associated Press, RTDNA, and the Lone Star EMMY Chapter of the National Academy of Television Arts and Sciences. The station has won four consecutive Texas Association of Broadcasters’ Bonner McLane Public Service awards, and in 2023 won a National Edward R. Murrow Award for Digital content. KBTX is also a recent Texas AP Broadcasters/Freedom of Information Foundation of Texas Station of the Year and Texas Associated Press Broadcasters Station of the Year.

The station has launched the careers of many well-known journalists, meteorologists and network executives, and takes pride in helping talent grow quickly into the nation’s largest television markets. The work family of KBTX is made up of a group of dedicated, professional, and passionate individuals who are the backbone of our daily mission.
Bryan-College Station, Texas, is a community of more than 250,000 people and the largest single metro in the Waco-Temple-Bryan DMA. The twin cities have a unique small-town feeling, but offer big city amenities, including a vibrant arts community, a city-wide, all-terrain trail system, and world-class dining and nightlife. Bryan and College Station are routinely recognized as a leader in quality of life and as one of the fastest-growing communities in the country.
College Station is home to Texas A&M University, the nation’s largest university. Aggie home football games attract more than 100,000 in the stands, with tens of thousands more camped outside celebrating at tailgates during football weekends.

Learn more about KBTX at www.kbtx.com.

Job Summary/Description:

About WMTV:

WMTV is the NBC affiliate and Gray Television-owned station serving south-central Wisconsin. We are the #1 station—leading the market in news and weather coverage. We are recognized for sharing information with accuracy and immediacy on all platforms.

We work hard and take pride in getting it right. For four years in a row, WMTV was honored as the Wisconsin Broadcasters Association “News Operation of the Year”. As well as being the recipient of the Edward R. Murrow Regional "Overall Excellence" Award.

What’s better than working at the #1 station in the nation’s #1 city? Join our award-winning team and live, work, and play in a community that is consistently named one of the best places to live in America. We are just 1.5 hours from Milwaukee, 2.5 hours from Chicago, and 5 hours from Minneapolis/St. Paul.

Job Summary/Description:

WMTV has an immediate opening for a Technical Media Producer. The Technical Media Producer (“TMP”) is responsible for operating the equipment in our broadcast control center that keeps WMTV’s programming on air and online. The TMP directs live and prerecorded productions as assigned, using our Ross Overdrive production automation system paired with coding in ENPS to deliver a quality News Show. The TMP also handles all master control duties in our facility, such as recording, playback, switching, and quality-checking programming for air. This position offers an opportunity for video editing and field directing.

Duties/Responsibilities include (but are not limited to):

- Monitoring and quality control of all inbound and outbound / broadcast signals, as well as ensuring that all content airs as intended and is logged
- Maintaining compliance with relevant FCC and other governmental agency regulations
- Directing assigned live and prerecorded productions using Ross Overdrive production automation
- Preparing the production rundowns for automation operation by coding the rundown in AP ENPS / Ross Overdrive plugin
- Understanding of all relevant equipment in the studio, production, and technical core areas
- Editing video for playback and working closely with the news team to ensure quality
- Field directing Special projects including WMTV's "Share your Holidays", UW Madison's Homecoming Parade, and our "On the Road segment

Qualifications/Requirements:

- 2 years of previous broadcast or production experience with master control or production control is preferred, but we will train the right person. Ross Overdrive experience is a plus.
- Demonstrated ability to learn new concepts quickly and thoroughly
- Proven track record of prioritizing complex tasks
- Ability to communicate effectively – written and verbal
- Strong commitment to working effectively with others; both being trained by and training others in a team environment is a must
- Positive attitude and ability to adapt to changes
- Must be willing to work holidays and weekends if needed

About KOSA:

First Alert 7 / KOSA-TV is the top-rated, long-time news leader in West Texas and southeastern New Mexico.

Based in Midland/Odessa, we pride ourselves on being the dominant player in a highly competitive market where there is never a shortage of news that impacts people on the regional level, throughout the state of Texas, and very often on the national stage. Our team of professionals is committed to sharing the most compelling stories every day…and we know that requires outstanding writers, creative photographers and an innovative production team. Whether we're following local officers to the nation's capital to remember their fallen brothers; traveling to Marine boot camp to highlight a local man's journey; covering a hometown president (George W. Bush) during his eight years in office; or tracking the latest developments in the oil and gas industry – KOSA is located at the epicenter of some of the most important news stories of our generation.

As the only community in the country with an International Air and Space Port, travel to and from Midland from anywhere in the world (and very soon even out of the world!) is quick and easy. We are also nestled in a picturesque region of Texas, often referred to as a hidden jewel that makes for exciting weekend trips for the outdoors adventurer or the lover of rare or unique art.

Job Summary/Description:

First Alert 7/KOSA-TV seeks a high-energy, self-motivated individual with exceptional communication skills to join our team as a Technical Media Producer (TMP). The TMP is a technical lead for production during live or taped studio broadcast productions and is responsible for the setup and operation of the production switcher and associated technical equipment in the Production Control Room and/or live location environment. They are responsible for evaluating and assigning all video inputs, taking into consideration timing and video levels, all while orchestrating the control room setup. The TMP will operate as the right hand of the News Producer to develop and execute the creative and technical “look” of the production by creating special effects via the production switcher.

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: 

Live/Taped Productions:
- Set up and operate production switchers and all associated technical equipment in a Production Control Room and/or Live Location environment during live game and/or studio broadcast productions.
Orchestrate control room setup while simultaneously evaluating and assigning all video inputs, taking into consideration timing and video levels
- Collaborates with the Producer to execute the technical and artistic vision for each live newscast and/or studio production
- Lead the technical portion of the production team during the production setup and coordinate the faxing of their equipment and show elements, since their equipment and work passes through the production switcher
- Collaborate with traffic and HUB entities needed to verify that all video and audio signals are routed correctly and are making it to their final destinations
- During a live and/or studio broadcast production, recall video sources, transitions, and effects, and route studio monitors as instructed by Producers.
Continuously monitor all sources used during production to ensure all video levels look correct and stay in time, which includes external feeds
- Must be able to handle the pressures of live programming and limited time constraints

Collaboration & Communication:
- Work closely with the Technical Operations and Production Engineering to identify, troubleshoot, and solve technical problems for Live Locations, PCRs, and Studio productions. Making sure each problem is resolved to completion
- Collaborates with Production Engineering, Technical Operations, and Production Management to identify and special-order any equipment needed for live or taped studio broadcast productions

Qualifications/Requirements:

- Minimum of 2 years of broadcast experience operating as a TMP, live remote, and/or live studio productions with hands-on experience in control room areas such as switching, audio, graphics, character generator, robotics, and automated rundown software
- Knowledge of current industry standards
- Knowledge of video signal flow and video router operations
- Knowledge of IP router operations and the software used to edit panels
- Must be able to technically operate various models of video switchers, digital effects devices, and other associated ancillary equipment
- Experience using ENPS or similar news production systems
- Experience using Ross Overdrive automation
- Knowledge of current broadcast technologies appropriate to the position's job responsibilities
- Knowledge of FCC regulations
- Must take ownership and accountability for assigned projects
- Experience using Edius; Adobe Creative Suite editing software preferred
- Computer skills, using MS Office
- Able to work flexible, non-traditional hours, including weekends and holidays

KOLO is a station that gets the job done. Many of our employees have been with the company for years, and they pride themselves on their expertise and their ability to succeed. While Reno/Tahoe is a 100+ market, it has all the characteristics of a much larger West Coast market. In fact, some say Reno has a superior lifestyle and outdoor activities to its much larger neighboring markets. For these and many other reasons, KOLO is able to attract top-notch individuals. We pride ourselves on not limiting ourselves to the "news conference or press release journalism" stories that are easy to get. Our journalists know they need to tell stories on issues that matter to the Northern Nevada community and our viewers. Much of the station's identity is from KOLOCares, a program designed to better serve Northern Nevada through the wonderful non-profit organizations that are part of the community. KOLOCares was recently honored by the National Association of Broadcasters' Celebration of Service to Community Award. Every station is tasked to serve their community, but KOLO takes pride in finding unique ways to help our non-profit partners to reach their goals.

Reno has an illustrious history of boom or bust, and right now the area is booming! Life in Reno/Tahoe is not just about work. Northern Nevada boasts remarkable outdoor activities highlighted by the spectacular beauty of Lake Tahoe, world-renowned ski resorts in the Sierra, trout fishing in the Truckee River and Pyramid Lake, placid campgrounds, miles of hiking and biking trails and, yes, casinos. San Francisco, Yosemite, and Napa Valley are all an easy drive for a weekend getaway. Many Northern Californians spend their weekends in Reno, especially with the summer festivities that feature balloon races, Hot August Nights, and the nation's largest BBQ rib festival. There is always something happening in Reno, the "Biggest Little City in the World."

Job Summary/Description:  

The Technical Director will be a technical lead for production during live or taped studio broadcast productions. Full-Time

_______________________

Job Summary/Description:

Do you have a passion for holding the powerful accountable? Are you the kind of reporter who can take a complex legislative bill and turn it into a story that actually matters to a family in Duluth, Mankato, or Rochester? We’re looking for a high-energy, autonomous State Capitol Reporter to be the face of Minnesota politics for our stations across the state. Based in the heart of the Twin Cities, you’ll be the bridge between the halls of power and the communities we serve—delivering news that lives on every screen, from the 6 PM broadcast to a viral social thread.

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:  

What You'll Do: 

• Own the Capitol: Be the first to know—and the first to report—on the legislative sessions, policy shifts, and political maneuvers that shape Minnesota.
• Tell stories that travel: Craft compelling content for four major Gray stations (KBJR, KEYC, KTTC, KVLY) and occasionally represent Minnesota on a national stage.
• Master the multi-platform pivot: Shoot, write, and edit your own content, ensuring it’s optimized for a digital-first audience before it even hits the airwaves.
• Lead the election charge: Take a featured role during election cycles, breaking down races and results with urgency and authority.
• Connect the dots: Coordinate with newsrooms across the state to provide live hits and localized angles on statewide issues.
• Build a source network: Quickly develop deep relationships with lawmakers, advocates, and community leaders to uncover the stories others miss. 

Why You’ll Love It Here 

• Unmatched reach: Your work will be seen across the state and the country, giving you a massive platform to grow your brand.
• True autonomy: You’re the lead on this beat. We trust you to find the stories and tell them your way.
• Innovation at scale: Join a company that is leading the digital evolution of local news—not just talking about it.
• Community impact: You aren’t just reporting on politics; you’re helping Minnesotans understand the decisions that affect their lives every day.

Qualifications/Requirements:

What You Bring:

• 2+ years of on-air experience: You’re comfortable in front of the camera and even more comfortable digging through a legislative docket.
• A "Digital-First" brain: You don’t just "post to web"—you understand how to engage an audience on social and streaming platforms.
• Technical scrappiness: You can shoot, edit, and go live from the field (and yes, you can handle the 50 lbs of gear that makes the magic happen).
• Political curiosity: You have a deep interest in state government and the ability to explain "how it works" without the boring jargon.
• Independence and urgency: You thrive in a remote setup where you’re the boss of your beat, meeting deadlines with ease and a "desire to win."
• A clean driving record: You’ll be traversing the Twin Cities and beyond, so a valid license is a must.
• Humanity and grit: You have the empathy to tell human stories and the toughness to ask the hard questions.

job.description:
About Gray Media:

Today, we are a growing multimedia company headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. About WIS:

WIS is the #1 local media organization in the capital city market of Columbia, South Carolina. It is the market’s top-rated broadcast television station, a digital publisher reaching tens of millions of users each year, and the home of GDM Columbia, a full-service in-house digital advertising agency with national scale. WIS is also the hub for Palmetto Sports & Entertainment, a statewide broadcast sports network, and an affiliate of Telemundo SC.

Serving South Carolina's Midlands since 1953, WIS offers the opportunity to join an award-winning culture for a popular brand built upon decades of market leadership. Named the South Carolina Broadcasters Association's Station of the Year a record 17 times, WIS has earned the Edward R. Murrow Award for Journalism Excellence, the National Association of Broadcasters' Service to America Award, the George Foster Peabody Award, and is an annual attendee of the Southeast Emmy Awards.

Among the many notable former journalists who helped set our standard, NBC Today Show co-host Craig Melvin began his career with WIS as an intern, photographer, reporter, and then anchor.

WIS produces more than 60 hours of local, original programming per week. The station offers a unique variety of multiplatform advertising solutions, sponsored content, and professional creative services for businesses of any size.

Columbia, South Carolina, is a vibrant and growing capital city with a diverse population. It is home to the U.S. Army's largest installation for Basic Combat Training, Fort Jackson, along with the University of South Carolina and multiple other colleges and universities. WIS is located downtown, just two blocks from the South Carolina Statehouse.

Our community combines affordable quality of living with a variety of entertainment and activities to accommodate your lifestyle, whether it's our 50,000-acre Lake Murray, our Columbia Fireflies minor league baseball team, the Riverbanks Zoo & Gardens, nearby Congaree National Park, and so much more.

Job Summary:

WIS offers this exclusive, paid newsroom internship each semester, honoring one of our most notable alumni, NBC TODAY anchor Craig Melvin, who began his journalism career in our Columbia newsroom.

This opportunity places you inside the same award-winning environment that helped launch Craig’s trajectory from WIS intern to NBC network anchor. This internship provides hands-on experience as a valued member of the newsroom team, plus guidance directly from Craig, who will generously share his time and insight.

As a paid intern, you won’t sit and watch someone else doing their job. Gray’s intern program is an immersive experience where you serve as a valued team member on our award-winning teams.

Not only will you walk away with an expanded resume and portfolio, but Gray’s paid internship also opens doors to begin your full-time career with Gray Media. job.title: 2027 Summer Internship- Creative (Writing/Editorial)
job.description:
ABOUT HALLMARK’S INTERNSHIP PROGRAM  

We're looking for curious, creative, and consumer-focused interns who are passionate about storytelling, trends, culture, creativity, and human connection. 

This posting includes two distinct Creative Internship opportunities within Hallmark Greetings Creative .

 

Writing Studio & Greetings Editorial Intern 

This internship provides hands-on experience in creative writing, content development, editorial planning, trend research, and greeting card product strategy. Interns will partner with writers, editors, and product teams to develop consumer-focused content and concepts that help Hallmark create meaningful connections through greeting cards and related products.  

 

What you'll do 

  • Create original writing for greeting cards and related Hallmark products. 
  • Explore emerging trends, voices, and cultural insights relevant to Gen Z and Gen Alpha consumers. 
  • Learn how Hallmark plans, develops, and curates greeting card programs. 
  • Conduct editorial analysis and consumer research to identify future content opportunities. 
  • Develop concepts and editorial content that authentically connect with consumers. 
  • Partner with writers, editors, designers, and product teams throughout the creative process. 
  • Present recommendations and creative concepts to business and creative leaders. 

               

              BASIC QUALIFICATIONS 

              The following is required to be considered for this role: 

              • Pursuing a bachelor's degree in English, Journalism, Communications, Creative Writing, Advertising, Marketing, Public Relations, or a related field 
              • A graduation date of December 2027, May 2028, December 2028, May 2029, December 2029, or May 2030.  

                 

                PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 

                Your resume and application will stand out if you are: 

                • Demonstrated interest in writing, content creation, publishing, media, advertising, or product development 
                • Strong writing and editing skills 
                • Familiarity with social, cultural, and consumer trends relevant to Gen Z and Gen Alpha audiences 
                • Experience through coursework, publications, student organizations, freelance work, or personal creative projects is a plus 

                        

                      ADDITIONAL DETAILS 

                      • A portfolio is required for this position. Your portfolio should be compiled into one PDF document that is no larger than 5 MB. If your portfolio file size is above the 5MB limit, you can submit a one-page overview of your work (see example). You can also submit a link to a personal portfolio website to supplement your uploaded portfolio. Applicants who do not upload a portfolio or one-page overview will not be considered.
                      •  Candidates selected to move forward in the interview process will be asked to complete a few brief exercises later in the process.
                      • Our internship program is 12 weeks long, starting in late May and ending in early August. 
                      • This summer internship is a hybrid position, with the flexibility to work from both our recently renovated headquarters building in Kansas City, MO, and from your summer residence within the KC metro area. 
                      • Some relocation and housing assistance is provided for interns whose permanent address is outside of the KC metro area. Relocation is required for this role. 

                             

                            Interested? Follow the application instructions below to apply. 

                             

                            APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS  

                            Along with your resume and application, please provide up to 10 samples of your own writing that demonstrate:

                            • Your unique voice
                            • A range of content types (academic, creative, journalistic, prose, verse, etc.)
                            • Ability to edit for clarity / conciseness (for example, a piece of writing that shows before and after edits)
                            • Success in writing for a variety of audiences

                             

                            You must show how you meet the basic qualifications in a resume or document you upload, or by completing the work experience and education application fields. Accepted file types are Microsoft Word (DOC or DOCX), PDF, HTML, or TXT.  

                             

                            In compliance with the Immigration Reform and Control Act of 1986, Hallmark Cards, Inc. and its subsidiary companies will hire only individuals lawfully authorized to work in the United States. Hallmark does not generally provide sponsorship for employment. Employment by Hallmark is contingent upon the signing of the Employment Agreement, signing of an agreement to arbitrate in connection with the Hallmark Dispute Resolution Program, completing Form I-9 Employment Eligibility Verification, passing the urinalysis drug screen, education verification and satisfactory reference and background checks. 

                             

                            ABOUT HALLMARK – Because Connecting With Each Other Has Never Been More Important  

                             

                            For more than a century, Hallmark has been bringing people together and improving the relationships that matter most. That’s why millions of people all over the world connect with the Hallmark brand. It has always been a mission so much bigger than any one of us who work here. Today, we need empathetic learners, strategic thinkers, and enthusiastic visionaries with diverse experiences and skills to help us create the rest of Hallmark’s second century as we shift to a more digitally savvy, unified approach that combines the best of brick-and-mortar retail with the efficiency of dot-com spaces. Help us imagine what our next hundred years could look like!  

                            When you join Hallmark, we will go out of our way to make you feel like part of the team, even in a remote/hybrid work environment. In the day-to-day, we’ll make the best use of the skills and talents you already have. We’ll also give you leadership opportunities and show you multiple potential pathways to future success.  

                            Our culture of care for our consumers and for one another shows in the way we embrace different backgrounds, identities, and working styles, deliberately seeking out ways to be more inclusive both internally among our work groups and externally through the ings we make and sell to our retail partners and consumers. We believe that a broadly inclusive, equitable approach is also our best path to future success. We’re seeking out those who can bring a fresh perspective to our business and would love your input as someone new to our team! We can only change and grow when we intentionally include new perspectives–like yours.

job.title: Building Services Department Manager
job.description:

For over 100 years, Hallmark has helped people connect and strengthen the relationships that matter most. Today, we’re building the next century of connection—blending the warmth of in-store experiences with the ease of digital innovation. We’re looking for empathetic learners, strategic thinkers, and enthusiastic visionaries from all backgrounds to help shape what’s next. If you’re ready to bring fresh ideas and energy, we’d love to have you on the team! As a Building Services Department Manager, you will lead facility operations, infrastructure, and building services at our Lawrence Production Center. You’ll be responsible for ensuring a safe, reliable, and compliant facility environment while overseeing capital improvement projects, contracted services, and emergency response planning. You’ll manage facility resources and budgets, drive continuous improvement initiatives, and support uninterrupted manufacturing operations. You’ll develop talent and align resources to meet the evolving needs of the site. 

The Building Services Department Manager will: 

  • Lead facility operations and building services, ensuring the safety, functionality, and reliability of plant buildings, utilities, HVAC systems, grounds, and site infrastructure.
  • Oversee capital construction, renovation, and facility improvement projects while ensuring projects meet budget, schedule, and quality expectations.
  • Manage vendor relationships and contracted services including janitorial, groundskeeping, pest control, waste management, security, and specialized building trades.
  • Ensure compliance with OSHA, environmental regulations, fire codes, permits, inspections, and corporate facility standards.
  • Serve as the Facility Emergency Coordinator, leading site preparedness and response for emergencies, severe weather, utility outages, and other facility-related incidents.
  • Develop and manage operating and capital budgets while supporting long-term facility planning and asset lifecycle management.
  • Lead and develop Building Specialists and HVAC Specialists while partnering closely with Operations, Engineering, Maintenance, Security, and EHS teams.

The role may require occasional weekend or after-hours work, depending on business needs.

  • Bachelor’s Degree or four years of demonstrated management experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.

  • Four years of experience managing front-line employees.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Word and Excel.
  • Good aptitude for utilizing business applications and systems.

  • DOT, EPA Hazardous Waste, and OSHA-related training.
  • Demonstrated experience managing emergency situations and facility-related incidents.

job.title: Data Engineer - Business Intelligence (Remote)
job.description:
WHO WE ARE & WHAT WE DO

Hallmark’s Data & Business Intelligence organization turns enterprise data into trusted insights that help teams across Hallmark make better, faster decisions. We build and manage the data platforms, pipelines, semantic models, and analytics solutions that support critical business areas including retail, product, consumer, merchandising, planning, finance, and executive reporting.

 

WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING & THE IMPACT YOU’LL MAKE

We are looking for an experienced BI Engineer to design and build scalable, governed analytics solutions that enable trusted and intuitive access to enterprise data. This role will focus on developing Power BI semantic models, reusable business/context layers, and self-service analytics capabilities, leveraging Microsoft Power BI, Microsoft Fabric, Snowflake, and AI-assisted development practices. The ideal candidate will have 6–8 years of experience in Business Intelligence, Analytics Engineering, Data Engineering, or related areas, with strong hands-on expertise in Power BI, dimensional modeling, semantic model development, SQL, and modern cloud data platforms. This role also requires an AI-first engineering mindset. The engineer will be expected to use approved AI capabilities to accelerate development, testing, documentation, optimization, and modernization while maintaining accountability for the quality, security, and maintainability of production solutions.

This is a progressive role that will be filled at the level based on the skills and experience of the selected candidate.

 

ADDITIONAL DETAILS

  • The salary range for this role is $85,000 - $110,000. Final compensation varies based on several factors.
  • This is a U.S.-based remote role.* We’re committed to creating a connected, collaborative culture, no matter where you are. You’ll have access to virtual tools, team support, and opportunities to engage and grow with us. *Due to state-specific benefits regulations, Hallmark cannot consider candidates for remote positions who reside in Alaska, Hawaii, or Puerto Rico, or any country outside of the United States.
  • This is a progressive role designed to grow with you. We’ll match the job level to your skills and experience so you can hit the ground running and keep building your career.
  • Hallmark is committed to recognizing and rewarding performance. Employees are eligible for annual merit-based increases, aligned with individual and company performance.
  • In alignment with our culture of care, Hallmark offers a competitive benefits package, including medical, dental and vision plans, paid time off, 401K with company match, and profit-sharing.

 

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS (the following is required to be considered for this role):

  • At lease 6 years of experience in Business Intelligence, Analytics Engineering, Data Engineering, or a related technology discipline.
  • Hands-on experience with Microsoft Power BI, including semantic model development, DAX, Power Query/M, dimensional modeling, Power BI Service, data security, and performance optimization.
  • Experience designing and developing dimensional data models using star schemas, facts, dimensions, aggregations, relationships, hierarchies, measures, and KPIs.
  • Demonstrated experience building shared and reusable semantic/business layers, rather than primarily developing individual reports.
  • Experience developing and implementing self-service analytics capabilities for business users.
  • Experience developing and optimizing SQL queries for performance and efficiency.
  • Hands-on experience working with Snowflake or a comparable cloud data platform.
  • Experience developing analytical solutions using Microsoft Fabric.
  • Understanding of modern analytical architectures spanning data platforms, analytical data products, semantic models, and visualization layers.
  • Experience designing or developing modern analytical architectures that include data platforms, analytical data products, semantic models, and visualization layers
  • Experience translating complex business requirements into scalable technical and analytical solutions.
  • Demonstrated experience incorporating Generative AI or AI coding assistants into real-world development workflows.
  • Ability to use AI effectively to generate, review, refine, and troubleshoot SQL, DAX, M, semantic-model metadata, documentation, and other engineering artifacts.
  • Experience using AI across multiple stages of the development lifecycle, including design, development, testing, troubleshooting, optimization, and documentation.
  • Ability to evaluate AI-generated solutions for correctness rather than accepting generated code without appropriate engineering review.
  • Experience applying responsible AI development practices, including data protection, security, validation, governance, and human accountability

 

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS (your application will stand out if you have the following):

  • Advanced experience with Microsoft Fabric, including Lakehouse, Warehouse, OneLake, Direct Lake, Dataflows Gen2, and data pipelines.
  • Experience integrating and optimizing Power BI with Snowflake.
  • Experience with medallion or layered data architectures and curated analytical data products.
  • Experience with CI/CD, Git integration, deployment pipelines, source control, and DevOps practices for BI and analytics solutions.
  • Experience establishing BI governance, semantic-model standards, common metric definitions, and self-service analytics frameworks.
  • Experience modernizing legacy BI/reporting platforms to Power BI, Fabric, Snowflake, or other modern cloud analytics platforms.
  • Experience with metadata management, data catalogs, lineage, business glossaries, or Microsoft Purview.
  • Experience developing AI-enabled accelerators, agents, reusable prompts, or automated development workflows for BI and analytics engineering.
  • Experience applying AI to accelerate BI modernization, report migration, semantic modeling, metadata management, testing, and self-service analytics.

We’re seeking out those who can bring a fresh perspective to our business and would love your input as someone new to our team!
