It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role

The New York Times advertising department's mission is to create work that helps brands make their mark in the world, and our canvas is the full breadth of The New York Times and its associated media platforms, including digital, mobile, audio, print, events and more.

The Advertising Strategy team's award-winning work includes activations across digital, audio, and print and spans the breadth of NYT's portfolio, like Cooking, Wirecutter, Games, and The Athletic, as well as our premier editorial events like the Dealbook conference.

The Director, Strategy will bring experience working cross-category and possess a passion for uncovering how different categories intersect with media and culture to spark inspiring creative ways-in and ideas. Strategy is a team sport, and you will be an expert collaborator with experience leading versatile teams, including creative, program management, sales, and planning, toward a common goal. Success within the advertising strategy team requires the ability to uncover human and cultural truths across multiple categories like finance, media, entertainment, healthcare, and consumer goods as well as a passion for big ideas expressed through media, a love of The New York Times, and a high standard for creating visual presentations.

  • Management and Mentorship: You are a skilled manager with practice and proficiency in teaching and guiding teams through the strategic process.
  • Operational Skills: You have some experience with strategic resourcing of team members and managing stakeholders around workflows
  • Research, Insights, and Creative Brief Development: You are an expert at using proprietary tools, third-party resources and desk research to uncover meaningful insights, human truths and whitespace opportunities that will lead to a compelling way in for creative and media.
  • Creative Briefing: You are experienced in writing compelling creative briefs, briefing creative teams, and being an inspiring strategic partner to creative teams.
  • Media Strategy: You are experienced in making recommendations for how to use media to bring ideas to life in ways that meet clients' campaign objectives. Although you will not be responsible for writing media plans, you are comfortable and expert in guiding internal teams as well as clients in making smart and creative media choices.
  • Client Deliverable Development: You are experienced in owning and creating client-ready visual proposals that are polished and inspiring.
  • Category Fluency: You are constantly learning and reading about macro trends in business and culture.

Responsibilities:

  • Manage 3-6 strategists across 2-3 Categories
  • Co-lead resourcing across the Strategy Team
  • Consult with Sales leadership to improve processes, practices and strategic deliverables
  • Engage with teams across the Ad Department to guide cross-functional solutions and innovations
  • Use research and data to articulate and support sales stories
  • Author and deliver creative briefs on sometimes-tight turnarounds
  • Create and guide others in the creation of powerful proposals with effective storytelling that responds to client needs and telegraphs the value of NYT media offerings
  • Develop a broad understanding of all New York Times assets
  • Lead and project manage across relevant departments (including Sales, Ad Product, T Brand Studio, Ad Operations, Research, Marketing, Events) to create integrated programs for clients
  • Develop, articulate and share innovative programs, partnerships, innovations and opportunities
  • Research, write, and guide others in the creation of content strategy briefs
  • Attend key sales calls to pitch advertising and media ideas to mid/senior-level executives
  • Manage internal senior team members, communicating proposal and program status to management
  • Educate and keep the Strategy team/department abreast of trends and what opportunities or challenges they might present for our business
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Executive Strategy Director

Basic Qualifications:

  • 12+ years of cross-platform Advertising experience in brand and media strategy
  • Interest in managing high-volume categories
  • Experience working on RFPs
  • Experience working in collaborative sales and marketing processes, including working with sales teams or in a sales environment
  • An understanding of the current social, branded content, digital, audio and mobile media landscapes
  • Experience with how to translate the long-term goals of advertisers into solutions and recommendations that can be provided by The New York Times

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree or equivalent work experience

It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role:

Analytics Data Products (ADP) is an enablement team in the Data Platform mission. We support Product Engineering teams across The Times in creating, operating, and stewarding data products by providing onboarding workflows, developer experience, modeling expertise, and data-lifecycle standards. We also build shared behavioral data products, such as Pageviews, Sessions, and client-side Interactions, so core reader behaviors can be measured consistently across missions and standalone experiences. Mission teams remain accountable for their domain data while we work alongside them as a forward-deployed team to help them onboard and publish. You will report to the Senior Director of Data Platform.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can expect to come into the office 3+ days/week.

Responsibilities:

  • Hire, develop, and lead a high-performing engineering team, fostering a culture of collaboration, innovation, and high productivity
  • Own developer experience and tooling (onboarding, CLI, templates, validation, automation) and define and track success metrics such as producer adoption and data reliability
  • Oversee roadmap execution, architectural guidance, technical decisions
  • Develop and maintain budgets, forecasts and a cost attribution model for your team's cloud solutions
  • Partner with product managers and stakeholders to define requirements and manage change while systematically retiring legacy systems.
  • Develop and maintain budgets, forecasts and a cost attribution model for your team's cloud solutions
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

Basic Qualifications:

  • 1+ years of formal people management experience
  • 4+ years building and supporting production data pipelines
  • Demonstrated experience managing or leading technical teams with diverse skill sets and backgrounds
  • Experience enabling successful collaborations across engineering teams and have a knack for bringing engineers together to achieve shared goals
  • Ability to jump in as needed to assist technically with code reviews, design discussions, and analysis
  • Experience using SQL to transform data and a working knowledge of at least one of: Python, Java or Go
  • Knowledge of relational, columnar, and key-value storage technologies as well as data modeling for analytics
  • Passion for the Times' mission and desire to join us at a moment in history where our data has the power to transform every aspect of creation and practice of journalism

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience building developer tooling, onboarding workflows, or internal platforms that other engineering teams adopt
  • Experience with distributed systems and event-driven architectures and event instrumentation
  • Experience leading migrations or retiring legacy systems

About the Role:

The New York Times is seeking an Engineering Manager to lead a multidisciplinary team across iOS, Android, Web, and Backend. Partnering closely with Product, Design, Data, and Production, you will drive audience growth across NYT Games digital platforms. This team's focus is top-of-funnel growth, seeking to uncover the growth loops that are most effective in driving net new audience to Games. You'll play a pivotal role in growing our first 2-player game, Crossplay, and contributing to strategic partnerships.

Reporting to the Director of Games Engineering, you will build high-quality software and cultivate high-performing engineering teams to advance our mission of becoming the premier destination for digital puzzles.

We push code to production and improve the speed of delivery without compromising on quality. We generally build APIs in Go on AWS, iOS apps in Swift/Swift UI, Android apps in Kotlin/Jetpack Compose and web front-ends in React. Engineering Managers motivate and guide teams to deliver high-quality work on time, and aligning their team members with our goals, creating a culture and processes that keep developers productive.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can typically expect to come into the office 3+ days/week.

Responsibilities:

  • Manage a team of engineers across iOS, Android, Web, and Backend disciplines

  • Translate squad goals and north-star metrics into actionable technical priorities and clear deliverables

  • Foster engineer growth through targeted coaching, mentorship, and continuous feedback

  • Partner with Product, Design, and Production to ship high-quality web and mobile experiences that expand our audience

  • Advocate for engineering best practices, including the effective leverage of AI coding tools

  • 1+ years of Engineering Manager experience, leading mobile engineering teams

  • 5+ years hands-on experience building complex web, iOS, or Android applications

  • Hands-on exposure to modern web frameworks and native mobile technologies

  • Proven ability to navigate fast-paced environments, bringing clarity and decisive judgment amidst evolving priorities

  • Track record of strategic technical leadership and sound architectural decision-making across complex initiatives

  • Strong collaborative mindset partnering across Product, Design, and Engineering disciplines

  • A growth-mindset coaching style using open-ended questioning to drive continuous team improvement

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience leading engineering for consumer-facing products, particularly products with an audience-growth focus

  • Demonstrated passion for building mobile or digital games

job.title: Fellow, Opinion Video
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

Join the 2027 New York Times Fellowship class as an editor of video commentary in the Opinion section in New York.

As a vertical video editor, you will create videos for nytimes.com and social media. While editing is at the core of this position, you will be equal parts producer, writer and editor. This opportunity will allow you to conceive of new video formats for mobile-first journalism.

You will exercise journalistic and creative judgment to ensure excellence and accuracy in your work, and you should be eager to experiment with different forms of storytelling. You might be hosting a video one day and the next day be deep in an edit or rewrite of a script. You will collaborate with the Opinion Audience team, as well as department journalists and external contributors.

The Opinion department is separate from the newsroom. This is an in-office position and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance. You may be required to work some nights, weekends and holidays as needed.

Responsibilities:

  • Produce, write and edit vertical videos
  • Act as a host in some videos to help translate our journalism for off-site audiences
  • Write engaging, SEO-driven social captions
  • Post videos to our site and platforms such as TikTok and YouTube
  • Collaborate with other journalists and editors to adapt, script and edit videos
  • Work with editors on inventive on-site and social formats that align with Opinion’s mission and identity
  • Participate in training and social programs designed for the fellowship
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

Basic Qualifications:

  • No more than five years of full-time, professional journalism experience, excluding internships
  • 3+ years of experience with creative video editing, with demonstrated success in the creation of innovative journalism in a fast-paced environment
  • Can produce and publish short-form vertical videos on tight deadlines
  • Experience in video and graphics editing with Adobe Premiere and AfterEffects
  • Experience in archive producing, including using photo, video, graphics and audio

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Record of multiple journalism internships, or equivalent experience
  • Can appear and speak on camera as a host
  • Deep knowledge of TikTok and Instagram, and broad knowledge of the social media landscape and awareness of platform trends as they change

To apply, upload a résumé and cover letter. You should also include a link to a portfolio of your work. The application will prompt you when to upload materials and ask you for the link to your portfolio. Applications that fail to include any of these materials or follow these instructions will not be considered.

You must be authorized to work in the United States. We will not sponsor work visas for the fellowship, but we will consider applicants with valid work authorization or a valid student visa that can be extended with Optional Practical Training.

You may apply to only one fellowship position per year. For instance, if you apply as a shows editor in Opinion, you should not apply for any other positions in the fellowship. Duplicate applications will be discarded.

The application deadline is 5 p.m. Eastern Standard Time on Nov. 20. 

The Times Fellowship generates a high level of interest, so we cannot acknowledge the status of applications upon receipt or during the vetting process, which can take eight weeks or more. We cannot accept applications that are mailed or emailed to us. We will contact you for interviews as needed.

The fellowship program will begin on or about June 7, 2027, and end on May 26, 2028, subject to satisfactory performance. There is no guarantee of a full-time position upon completion of the program.

For more information about the Times Fellowship, visit here.

 

This position is represented by the NewsGuild of New York.

About the role

The HR Operations Specialist supports employees across the company by coordinating HR transactions, resolving production issues, and responding to questions. This role partners with employees, department managers, HR Partners, Payroll, and other teams to keep HR processes running smoothly and employee data accurate. You will report to the HRIS Operations Supervisor.

This is a hybrid role based in our Norfolk, Virginia office. You can typically expect to work in the office three days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Be the primary contact for employee HR inquiries, partnering with the appropriate teams to provide clear, guidance.
  • Work with department managers and HR Partners to gather information, process employee transactions, and maintain accurate employee data in Workday.
  • Process complex administrative transactions and participate in Workday HR system workflows.
  • Troubleshoot Workday production issues across HCM modules, including HCM Core, Recruiting, Time and Attendance, and Compensation; resolve related support tickets involving HR processes and employee data.
  • Support biweekly payroll processing by reviewing and validating payroll transactions and inputs, processing vacation payouts, and managing paid time off (PTO) adjustments in Workday following established procedures.
  • Work with Payroll and other teams, handling confidential information.
  • Help with user acceptance testing, configuration and reporting requests, and testing for biannual Workday releases.
  • Build and upload Enterprise Interface Builder (EIB) files for employee and company changes.
  • Help employees use HR-related technology by answering questions and contributing to user enablement and training.
  • Develop training materials using Google Sites.
  • Manage end-user channels and the team email group, responding to inquiries from employees, HR Partners, and managers.
  • Audit HR processes and employee transactions to support data quality and integrity; follow security and data-handling protocols.
  • Process employment verification requests.
  • Manage a varied daily workload, reprioritizing to complete incoming transactions and department requests.
  • Take on other tasks as assigned.

Basic qualifications:

  • 2+ years of experience working with Workday HCM processing HR transactions.
  • Solid awareness of how human resources transactions influence payroll processing, financial reporting, and broader operational tasks.
  • At least one year of experience using Microsoft Excel, including formulas and pivot tables.
  • You know how to provide clear, professional guidance.
  • Care for the impact your work can have across related processes.
  • You are resolution-oriented.
  • You have strong attention to detail.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Hands-on experience with Workday Payroll processing.
  • A bachelor's degree in business, information systems, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Familiarity with additional Workday modules and teams, such as Benefits, Payroll, Finance, Security and Integrations.

job.title: Local Investigations Fellowship Expression of Interest
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times offers a menu of programs and opportunities aimed at up-and-coming journalists and professionals from all backgrounds and with various skill levels.

Learn more about career programs here.

The application window for the Local Investigations Fellowship is currently closed and will reopen in summer of 2027.

Cover Letters for the Local Investigations Fellowship include at least one story idea or pitch, but multiple may be sent in each cover letter. Answers to these questions help us assess where you are in the reporting process and what editorial support and resources the local investigative fellowship could offer you.

  1. What is your investigative story idea or area of focus? How would your story expose something new, something no one else has already revealed?
  2. Describe who has been harmed and in what way. Is the harm enough to spark outrage?
  3. Will your story hold someone accountable? Who and how?
  4. What critical records, data and human sources will be required to tell your story? Describe how you have, or could, obtain these critical sources.
  5. What do you need help with to report this story, and what are the barriers?
  6. Can you give us a sense of what has been written about the subject? Please include clips of notable reporting on the topic.

We appreciate proposals that are as detailed as possible. Previous successful applicants have included specifics about what they aimed to prove through their investigations. 

For example, a reporter for The Baltimore Banner had reason to believe that the city’s overdose crisis was the worst in the nation. Mississippi Today had evidence of abuses in local sheriffs offices. And a reporter for The Desert Sun in Palm Springs, Calif., suspected a pattern of deaths inside local jails. 

Please submit five published clips that show excellence — in evocative writing, through high-impact news stories and by highlighting the voices of local communities. Your clips should be uploaded to the additional materials question below. Please include the full text of your clips, not just the links.

What makes a good local investigation?

  • Starts with high stakes
    How does the story affect people’s lives and livelihoods? Their health, safety and basic quality of life?
  • Has a clear line of accountability
    Great investigations have a line of accountability to someone or some group with significant power.
  • Reveals something
    Does your investigation reveal something that someone or some institution is trying to keep secret?
  • Has a clear sense of place
    The most important element for any local investigation: How is it (e.g. the policy, the circumstance or the failure) unique to your community?

job.title: Open Source Reporting, Graphics (Graphics Multimedia Editor)
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times Graphics team is looking for a reporter with extensive open-source and investigative reporting skills to turn raw evidence into impactful visual stories. You have a track record for uncovering exclusive information off the news.

The Graphics team is a leader in using spatial and visual techniques on investigative stories, and we're looking for someone who is passionate about accountability journalism using cutting-edge reporting techniques.

Below are a few examples of the kinds of stories that you will be a part of:
  • An exclusive look at the failed columns of the Midtown Manhattan near-collapse
  • A 3-D analysis of why firefighters' lines of sight were limited in the deadly LaGuardia Crash
  • An investigation into the mass graves in Syria
  • An investigation into the causes of a Miami building collapse
  • A spatial investigation into a deadly fire in the Bronx
  • A forensic analysis of an apartment building collapse in the Turkey earthquake
Working with journalists on the Graphics team and across the newsroom, you will play an important role in shaping visual reconstructions and investigations that rely on spatial analysis or use 3-D modeling. You will gather and analyze evidence for stories across a wide range of topics for both quick-turn stories as well as longer-term enterprise.

You will be expected to take the initiative in leading major storylines, with the goal of uncovering new or exclusive findings across multiple visual story formats. You should be curious and driven, and be comfortable with moving between solo deep dives and fast-paced, cross-desk collaborations.

This is an in-office position based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office four days a week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:
  • Bring core OSINT fluency to the desk's coverage: geolocation, chronolocation, satellite/aerial imagery analysis, audio-video research, and more.
  • Analyze a variety of data sources, including satellite and aerial imagery, flight/vessel tracking data, social media platforms and radio scanner data.
  • Vet and build relationships with a network of sources on stories.
  • Generate ideas that help the team develop custom tooling to automate open-source reporting for analyzing and visualizing evidence.
  • Find new ways to report beyond the standard OSINT toolkit, by using computational techniques, including through machine learning, computer vision and approved AI tools.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to an Assistant Editor on the Graphics desk.
Basic Qualifications:
  • 5+ years of relevant experience as an investigative reporter, open-source researcher or forensic expert.
  • Proven experience conducting open-source investigations by sourcing audio and visual evidence across a variety of platforms.
  • Experience producing accountability journalism, with a strong portfolio.
  • Experience producing clear copy about the visual evidence on tight deadlines.
  • Experience verifying user-generated content from social media for authenticity.
  • Skilled in building timelines using a variety of sources, including official statements and metadata from user-generated content.
  • Familiarity with open-source intelligence tools and techniques like Google Earth, satellite imagery platforms, scanner audio data, flight or vessel tracking, or similar.
Preferred Qualifications:
  • Experience working both independently and collaboratively while managing multiple research threads.
  • Experience with advanced tools for reporting, such as QGIS, Blender for 3-D scene reconstructions, data analysis methods, audio and image forensics tools.
  • Adept at creating clear, visual explainers piecing together complex findings.
  • Familiarity with programming and custom tool development.
  • Familiarity with Adobe Suite and Figma.
  • Experience with web scraping tools and working with APIs.
  • Experience using command line tools.
  • Willingness and flexibility to work evenings and weekends as needed.
This position is represented by the NewsGuild of NY.   REQ-020693

The New York Times Opinion section is looking for a fact-checker to work on guest essays and other work produced by Opinion, with a specific emphasis on data-driven essays. The New York Times' Advertising team is looking for a Sales Director to join our Luxury Sales Team. Sales Directors use existing relationships and establish new ones across agency and client groups to secure advertising investment and ensure success of campaigns. You will tailor and pivot the NYT pitch and solution based on advertisers' needs and goals. Through a consultative approach, you will pitch to clients our full New York Times portfolio, which includes The Athletic, NYT Cooking, Wirecutter, NYT News, Games, Audio, and more.

About the Role

Your primary goal is to grow and diversify the advertising revenue from a slate of enterprise accounts. You are a team player and contribute to the goals and success of The NYT's Advertising Department, and our mission. You will be external-facing, meeting with clients in person frequently, and travel for client meetings will be necessary. This is a hybrid role based in our New York headquarters, reporting to the Head of Category. You can typically expect to be in the office 3 days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Oversee and grow a portfolio of luxury clients and agency relationships, building influence with senior decision-makers and expanding partnership depth over time.

job.title: Senior Analytics Engineer, People Data and Insights
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role

The New York Times is rebuilding how we use people data. Instead of one-off reports and ad hoc pulls, we are building governed, reusable data tools that HR leaders, HR partners, and their counterparts use to make decisions. You will help build this layer. People data at The Times lives in several systems, each with its own definitions and history. You will turn that into a modeled, tested, documented foundation that products can be built on repeatedly. You will lead the models, transformations, and data quality behind every product this team ships. You will report to the Senior Director, People Data and Insights. You will work out of the New York office on a hybrid schedule. 

Responsibilities:

  • You will design, build, and maintain the data models and databases that our products run on.
  • You will oversee the transformation layer from source systems into governed, tested, documented models.
  • You will turn metric definitions from the data dictionary into executable logic, so that a definition and the number it produces cannot drift apart.
  • You will build data quality into the pipeline: tests, validation, and reconciliation across sources that surface problems before team members do.
  • You will work with the Program Manager to translate product requirements into models, and push back when a requirement and the underlying data do not agree.
  • You will handle effective-dated and historical data correctly, so that point-in-time questions get point-in-time answers.
  • You will implement and maintain access controls appropriate to compensation, demographic, and other sensitive data.
  • You will document models and lineage so that all can understand why something was built the way it was.
  • You will demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

Basic Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience in analytics engineering, data engineering, or an equivalent role building production data models.
  • You are a SQL expert
  • Strong dimensional modeling skills, and the judgment to know when to normalize and when not to.
  • 5+ years of experience with a transformation framework such as dbt, and with version control and code review as part of normal practice.
  • 5+ years of experience handling slowly changing dimensions, dated records, and point-in-time reporting.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 2+ years of experience with HR or people data, and with systems such as Workday, Greenhouse, or One Model.
  • Python for orchestration, API work, or data validation.
  • 2+ years of experience with AWS data services.
  • Familiarity with BI and analytics tooling such as Hex, Tableau, or Looker.
  • 2+ years of experience in an organization with distinct populations operating under different rules, such as union and non-union groups.

REQ-020839

  • Peak Season: An additional 10 hours on weekends during peak periods.

  • Available Shifts (subject to change):

    • Shift A: 9:00 AM – 1:00 PM

    • Shift B: 1:00 PM – 5:00 PM

  • You will provide customer support across our primary communication channels: email and chat.

  • Technical Expertise: at least 2 years of experience with Shopify, Gorgias, and Loop Returns.

  • AI Chat & System Optimization: at least 1 year of experience working with AI chat tools, managing live chat queues, creating macros, configuring auto-responses, and performing advanced administrative tasks within Gorgias.

  • Work Environment: at least 3 years of experience in a high-volume retail environment, meeting strict response time expectations during peak season.

job.title: Senior Full-Stack Software Engineer, Games – Web Platform
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role

The New York Times is looking for a Senior Full-Stack Engineer to join the Games Web Platform squad. You'll help shape the platform behind The Times' suite of games, building the capabilities that help our teams to deliver engaging, reliable experiences for players. You'll take ownership of complex engineering work across our application, and help the team turn new puzzle ideas into scalable product capabilities.

You'll strengthen the technology behind our existing games and help create the foundation for new experiences. Working with engineers, designers, product managers, and production partners, you'll guide technical decisions from discovery through launch, balancing a high-quality player experience with maintainable, reliable systems. You'll also share your expertise through mentorship, thoughtful technical reviews, and contributions to an engineering organization that values transparency, diversity, learning, and a community of practice.

Our team builds web applications with React, semantic HTML, and SCSS, prioritizing accessibility and performance in the player experience. You'll contribute across the stack: shaping front-end architectures and shared platform capabilities, and designing and building performant Go APIs that support the Games ecosystem. Our infrastructure runs on Amazon Web Services, with Fastly providing edge delivery and caching. We're looking for someone who can make sound architectural tradeoffs, improve the systems they work on, and help other engineers deliver high-quality work.

You will report to the Engineering Manager, Platform squad.

This is a hybrid role based at our New York City headquarters. You can typically expect to come into the office 2-3+ days/week.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead the design and evolution of foundational web platform capabilities and shared component libraries, helping Games teams deliver reliable, accessible, high-quality experiences.

  • Lead the design and operation of performant, scalable Go APIs and services that support the evolving needs of the Games ecosystem.

  • Partner with Product, Design, and Production on complex projects. Shape technical approaches, weigh tradeoffs, and turn creative concepts into reliable product capabilities.

  • Improve performance, accessibility, and reliability across the Games suite, applying modern front-end practices and edge delivery capabilities to create a great player experience.

  • Improve developer experience by building and evolving tools, including Claude Code tooling, that help engineering teams deliver high-quality software.

  • Provide technical leadership through architecture and code reviews, clear engineering standards, and mentorship that helps teammates grow and teams deliver.

  • Strengthen production quality by using appropriate testing, monitoring, and operational practices to identify and address issues in the systems you own.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualiﬁcations:

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience building, deploying, and operating high-traffic web applications and distributed systems

  • Lead complex engineering work from design through production, making sound technical tradeoffs and partnering across Product, Design, and Editorial to build maintainable solutions

  • Build accessible, performant web experiences with modern JavaScript (ES6+), semantic HTML, CSS/SCSS, and React or a similar framework

  • Design shared component libraries or platform capabilities used by multiple teams, with attention to API design, documentation, adoption, and long-term support

  • Build performant, scalable APIs and services using Go, Java, or Python

  • Deploy and operate production services in cloud environments such as Amazon Web Services or Google Cloud Platform, using technologies such as databases, Redis, Docker, and CDNs or edge platforms like Fastly

  • Strengthen production quality and reliability through testing, monitoring, and observability; contribute technical leadership through design and code reviews, sound technical decisions, mentorship, and knowledge-sharing

Additional Qualifications:

  • Prior engineering experience in the gaming industry with web-based games, puzzles, or interactive media

  • Demonstrated interest in mission-driven engineering and a desire to partner with an accomplished team to support the journalistic independence of The New York Times

  • Experience with CI/CD automation (e.g., GitHub Actions, Drone, or Terraform) and a "DevOps" approach to platform stability

  • Familiarity with monitoring and observability tools (e.g., Datadog, Sentry, or Grafana) to improve the player experience

  • A "product-ﬁrst" mindset, with an obsession for end-user satisfaction and editorial efficiency

  • A growth-oriented mindset: You embrace technical challenges, learn from mistakes, and are eager to share your ﬁndings to help the whole team level up

job.title: Senior Producer, Metro
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role, Mission or Department Overview

The Metro desk at The Times is seeking a creative, knowledgeable and collaborative Senior Producer for its video journalism. Metro's journalism spans fast-moving breaking news, enterprise and investigations on a range of beats, from politics and education to transportation and criminal justice. We bring the issues of New York and its surrounding tri-state region to readers around the world, with deeply-reported narratives and unexpected tales.

You will bring a passion for news, a commitment to fast, authoritative coverage of breaking and developing stories, and the news judgment to identify enterprise stories and exclusives. An experienced video journalist and a manager, you'll help broaden Metro's coverage in a range of video formats. You are a talented storyteller and strong people manager who is passionate about breaking news, live journalism and enterprise.

Metro is known across the newsroom for its collegial culture. You'll work closely with Metro editors and reporters, and build strong relationships across the newsroom — especially Video and Photo — and partner with Metro leadership to shape and drive coverage. You'll bring an innovative, collaborative approach to motivating and inspiring teams to scale video on the desk and deliver fast-turnaround and ambitious work.

You will oversee everything from live streams and news clips to enterprise projects and Reporter Video, managing a team of video journalists to execute on each of those priorities. Your sharp visual and editorial skills will ensure that the right stories are assigned. Before videos are published onsite and on social media, you will ensure that they meet the editorial standards, style and quality of the Times.

This is an in-office position based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • You will drive innovative, exclusive video coverage across a range of video formats, from short-form live-blog updates to Reporter Videos featuring Times journalists, enterprise stories and columns, and occasional field deployments.

  • You will manage and help hire video journalists on the desk.

  • You will help colleagues assess whether a story is suited to video and whether it should be told primarily or exclusively in that format, and mentor them as they develop their video storytelling skills.

  • You will lead story development and story edits.

  • You will review, assign and provide clear feedback on video productions.

  • You will support and guide script writing and visual approaches for effective short-form video.

  • You will oversee production across multiple projects.

  • You will guide interviews and shoots as needed, both in studio and field.

  • You will work with Metro and Video leadership to develop new video approaches and editorial strategies for the desk.

  • You will coordinate breaking news coverage with Video's Daily News and The Times's Live team, which produces real-time updates and analysis.

  • You will work with the Editor, Video Training to identify coaching opportunities for on-camera and shooting skills.

  • You will oversee the production of social content and off-platform video.

  • You will draw ideas from a range of video sources, including wire services, UGC, eyewitness video, archival footage, motion graphics, and originally-shot footage.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • You will report to the Metro editor.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 8+ years experience producing digital news videos.

  • 4+ years experience managing video journalists or newsroom teams.

  • Demonstrated expertise in sourcing, assessing and verifying video from a range of sources.

  • Expert knowledge of digital storytelling formats.

  • Understanding of mainstream and emerging social channels.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Excellent writing, editing and communication skills.

  • Expert knowledge of current events with advanced level experience covering breaking news stories in New York and experience covering news in the eastern United States.

  • Experience overseeing geolocation and UGC verification work.

  • Experience developing and editing visual material for social platforms.

  • Flexibility to work extended hours and some weekends.

  • Able to meet and make quick decisions under deadlines and to adapt to change in a daily, unpredictable news environment.

Times Opinion is looking for a Senior Producer to lead the original reporting of our enterprise video team. You have experience guiding groundbreaking journalism with an eye for innovation and creative storytelling. You bring a filmmaker’s eye to journalism, pairing cinematic storytelling with a strong understanding of what engages audiences on YouTube and other digital platforms.

Beyond enterprise video journalism, you will help create video guest essays that bring compelling arguments to life. Contributors range from subject-matter experts and public officials to artists, celebrities and ordinary people with extraordinary perspectives. It’s an opportunity to bring fresh voices and bold ideas to our audience, challenging viewers to think differently about the world as it is—and imagine what it could become.

You will shape original ideas, make sound editorial decisions and oversee the work of journalists and editors. You will be a trusted resource for colleagues, offering clear editorial guidance and constructive feedback. The ideal candidate thrives in a fast-paced newsroom, helping the team meet deadlines while maintaining high standards of journalism and craft.

This position is based in New York City and requires attendance in the office four days a week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely, subject to departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Guide reporting, approve casting, frame and advance stories
  • Edit scripts and re-writes
  • Provide notes in edit and rough cut stages

  • Review, critique stories

job.title: Senior Product Marketing Manager, The Athletic
job.description:

The New York Times is hiring a collaborative Senior Product Marketing Manager for The Athletic. Reporting to the Director of Product Marketing, you will combine strategic product partnership with go-to-market leadership for priority Athletic products, features, and experiences.

In this role, you will bring market insights directly into product development by transforming customer needs, marketplace dynamics, and behavioral data into relevant recommendations. You will partner with product teams from discovery and strategy through launch and measurement, helping the team build experiences that support acquisition, engagement, and retention.

You will also lead go-to-market strategies for major launches and product updates working with Product, Marketing, Research, Editorial, Creative and other teams. You will define positioning, develop messaging, align team members, and ensure launches reach the right audiences with the right value proposition.

This role sits at the intersection of customer insight, product strategy, positioning, launch planning, and performance measurement. You are comfortable operating in ambiguity, influencing without authority, and making complex ideas clear. You are a hands-on builder yourself who enjoys building prototypes to help get your ideas across. You have direct experience scaling adoption and habituation with apps.

Responsibilities:

  • Partner directly with Product teams to represent customer and market perspectives in planning, prioritization, and roadmap decisions.

  • Use research and data to identify customer needs, prioritize use cases, and uncover market opportunities for Athletic products and experiences.

  • Translate complex product capabilities into compelling customer benefits and clear value propositions tailored for sports fans.

  • Collaborate with Growth Marketing and Product teams to uncover opportunities across the entire user journey (acquisition, activation, onboarding, engagement, conversion, upsell, and retention).

  • Define success metrics, analyze post-launch performance, and establish feedback loops to inform future product and marketing strategy.

  • Build clear narratives, frameworks, and presentations that align partners around customer needs, product strategy, and project impact.

  • Foster trusted relationships across the organization by bringing structure to complex programs, facilitating productive discussions, and sharing best practices to improve product marketing standards.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • 6+ years of product marketing experience with an understanding of product-led growth concepts that impact acquisition, activation, engagement, and retention.

  • Expertise in go-to-market strategy, lifecycle marketing across owned and paid channels, and planning, testing, and shipping features for B2C subscription apps.

  • Experience using customer research, audience insights, competitive intelligence, and analytics tools to inform positioning, value propositions, and messaging strategies.

  • Experience partnering with Product, Data, Tech, and Research teams to influence roadmap decisions, run test-and-learn agendas, and measure outcomes.

  • Clear and engaging communication, with the ability to tailor complex information to a range of audiences.

  • An interest in sports and an understanding of how fans discover, follow, and engage with sports coverage.

About the Role:

The Graphics department at The New York Times seeks to hire an experienced and versatile senior visual editor to manage and execute the presentation of our graphics journalism in formats beyond nytimes.com, including social media, email newsletters and the print newspaper. This is a high-impact role designed for a senior journalist who wants to pioneer best practices and drive our off-platform visual storytelling.

You will guide the adaptation of complex graphics for audiences on social media, including Instagram, Facebook, X and other emerging surfaces. You will be responsible for coordinating strategy with the Social Visuals team and for assigning, editing and in some cases crafting graphics to meet that strategy, and help to do the same for Times newsletters, including The Morning and On Politics. And you will work with the Print Hub to coordinate production and edit graphics for the Times print edition.

You possess impeccable news judgment and have extensive experience creating and editing a wide range of types of information graphics. You operate with autonomy to proactively identify new opportunities to extend the reach of our journalism.

This is an in-office position based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Conceptualize and execute unified visual styles that can effectively translate complex data, maps and diagrams into digestible, high-impact visual assets to fit a variety of formats.
  • Produce and edit news graphics under tight deadlines during breaking news environments.
  • Guide and edit the work of other visual journalists who translate interactives, spatial models and breaking news graphics into these formats.
  • Expertly and independently carry out all aspects of visual production, serving as the primary leader of all off-platform displays.
  • Work with the Social Visuals and Audience teams to direct the packaging of graphics journalism off-platform.
  • Maintain strong relationships and coordinate across other multidisciplinary desks (Graphics, Design, Video and the Print Hub) to track projects and establish publishing workflows.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to a deputy graphics editor.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of professional experience producing and editing visual journalism or multimedia graphics at a major news organization.
  • Deep familiarity with visual storytelling devices, including a strong portfolio demonstrating hands-on execution of maps, charts, diagrams, 3-D modeling or motion graphics.
  • Expert proficiency with Adobe Creative Suite (specifically Illustrator, Photoshop and After Effects) and Figma.
  • Experience with creating, editing or art directing graphics for a print publication.

  • Familiarity with reading and editing code (HTML, CSS, JavaScript).

job.description:

The New York Times Opinion is seeking an experienced editor to join its guest-essay team as a lynchpin of its domestic coverage. We are looking for an editor who can commission and edit ideas-based opinion journalism across a range of core news topics. They should be able to recruit and work with a diverse range of newsmakers, scholars, novelists and lawmakers — anyone at the center of the debates driving the national conversation.

This editor will need the skills to interrogate ideas, political platforms and accepted dogma. They must have a track record of taking a spark of an idea through to publication. And they will need an ample dose of flexibility and nimbleness to pivot to the most important topics without sacrificing quality or sophistication. While the make up of this editor's portfolio will depend on the candidate, applicants should expect politics, business and the economy to be high on our list of priorities.

We are seeking an editor with sound judgment, sharp instincts, and the ability to focus on both fast news and meaningful enterprise. A fondness for experimenting with formats is a plus. This editor must be ready to work closely with colleagues across the department. Collegiality and diplomacy are essential.

This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

You will report to the Opinion Deputy Editorial Director.

  • Meeting the moment on big news with fast, thoughtful ideas journalism
  • Seeing around corners to ensure we have the right big enterprise ready to go when the moment is ripe
  • Ensuring our coverage interrogates big new events from a wide range of viewpoints
  • Collaborating with colleagues across guest essays to brainstorm ideas and priorities
  • Working on novel formats and helping develop new ones
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

Basic Qualifications:

  • At least 7 years of experience at a digital or daily publication
  • At least 5 years of experience editing staff or contributing writers
  • Excellent news instincts, with razor-sharp line editing skills
  • A proven track record of ideas journalism
  • An enterprise mindset — open to collaboration and innovation
  • A commitment to independent journalism and The Times's mission and values

You are passionate about breaking and developing news and have deep knowledge of visual digital journalism. Previous experience working on digital live coverage and with content management systems is a plus. You will bring a strong understanding of editorial priorities and collaborate with visual journalists on the team. You will be responsible for producing immediate updates with short video clips that take our audience to the scene for ongoing stories, brainstorming visual opportunities for the blog for tentpole news events and pitching relevant visual stories that complement our coverage.

You have strong organizational skills and are able to communicate requests in a clear and efficient manner. You can work under deadlines and thrive in a dynamic and fast-paced environment. We're looking for a candidate who will relentlessly find the best video for a news story and has a track record of working on multiple projects at any given time.

This is an in-office position based in New York City and includes regular attendance four days a week. There may be some flexibility per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Own and coordinate coverage plans for news video in live blogs and related programming work, including livestreams, videos for reporter updates and clips for carousels.
  • Collaborate with the Live news team to plan for upcoming news events and visual opportunities.
  • Monitor the news day across core areas of coverage.
  • Identify opportunities to improve workflow, project tracking and automated reminders for production updates.
  • Manage workflow and process documentation.
  • Pitch visually driven videos for live blogs.
  • Use news wire services such as AP and Reuters to acquire material.
  • Guide the work of others on the team by overseeing clips and assigning daily news targets
  • Experiment with different forms of vertical and mobile visual storytelling.

  • This role reports to the Daily News Director on the video team based in New York.

  • 8+ years of journalism, video storytelling or video production experience, preferably in a digital video newsroom
  • Significant and proven experience reporting in complex and breaking-news environments under tight deadline
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently and decisively, take initiative and carry out all aspects of production with limited guidance
  • Proficient in Adobe Premiere Pro, able to edit quickly and accurately.
  • Strong editorial news judgment and writing skills, with a passion for breaking news.
  • Demonstrated social media platform expertise
  • Experience setting priorities, managing multiple projects and guiding or coordinating the work of other video journalists

  • Thorough knowledge of global current events and a track record of covering news across multiple subject areas or regions
  • A foundational knowledge of legal, ethical, copyright and usage issues for visuals.

Engaging our readers, monitoring on-site and off-platform conversations for story ideas and integrating readers’ contributions into our report is essential. 

You will know how to adjust social programming targets and priorities amid a shifting global, 24-hour news cycle and ever-changing platform landscape. You will also work with reporters and editors across the newsroom on how social media and readers’ voices can inform our journalism, both pre- and post-publication.

This is a hybrid, weekend position based in Seoul, with a Saturday-Tuesday schedule. It includes regular attendance in the office, per your departmental guidance. The role will report directly to the Editor, Social, based in Los Angeles.

Main responsibilities:

  • Supporting The Times’s social presence across our main accounts, ensuring coverage of breaking news and live events; strategizing around social video; conceiving and executing innovative social plans for enterprise projects; and leveraging videos, photography and graphics to elevate our off-platform report.
  • Support the increase in video production across the newsroom by prioritizing time-sensitive projects and ensuring that our video journalism reaches a wide audience off-platform. 
  • Developing and refining the voice of The Times on all of our off-platform channels, exhibiting excellent news judgment and audience-sensitive framing
  • Collaborating with Social Visuals editors and across our Video team, especially in Seoul, on developing and executing visual storytelling formats and strategies for social platforms 
  • Building creative social native content (e.g. visual cards, Instagram stories, etc.)
  • Skillfully editing, shaping and elevating headlines, copy and visual assets for social media
  • Suggesting story ideas, identifying video opportunities and partnering with desks across the Seoul newsroom to produce stories that:
    • Anticipate readers’ prospective social and search needs sparked by a Times exclusive or a news event
    • Respond to readers’ real-time social and search needs and trends
  • Developing testing strategies around medium (images, video) and message (headline, social share text), to inform a constantly updating set of best practices for engaging off-platform audiences (social, search, etc.)
  • Partner with editors across the newsroom to workshop on-platform framing of articles that leverage off-platform performance insights and reader interest
  • Interpreting data and signals to know what pieces are the right fit for what audiences both on and off our platforms
  • Tracking success through engagement rates, growth statistics, reader responses and other metrics
  • Working with journalists in the newsroom on best social media practices, including framing pieces for specific audiences
  • Collaborate with other audience editors, in Seoul and around the world, on flagging coverage opportunities informed by off-platform trends and sharing performance insights and case studies with desks
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world. 

Our ideal candidate:

  • Proven experience in social media and digital journalism
  • Deep understanding of all mainstream and some emerging social channels
  • Deep understanding of how social video travels off-platforms
  • Consistent record running Facebook, Twitter/X and Instagram accounts for major media outlets
  • Demonstrated interest in visual storytelling, including through video
  • Strong editorial judgment; comfortable with experimenting and refining strategies to optimize sharing for different social audiences
  • A passion for news and a dedication to The Times and its journalistic mission
  • Skill at bridging specialties, including reporting, editing, product, analytics, design and user research
  • Strong writing and editing skills, and knowledge of Times style or the ability to absorb and apply it quickly
  • Strong analytical skills and familiarity with how to use data to inform editorial decisions 
  • Experience working independently and collaborating across time zones

The GraphQL Platform team builds and operates The New York Times' federated API layer that helps product and engineering teams deliver trusted journalism and experiences across our products. We are looking for a Staff Software Engineer to shape the architecture and technical direction of this mission-critical platform as it scales in traffic, complexity, and the number of teams building on it.

  • Set technical strategy and architecture for the GraphQL federation platform.
  • Design capabilities to improve reliability, performance, traffic management, and cost efficiency.

  • Experience improving reliability, performance, or observability in production systems, and using data to guide technical decisions.

job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. About the Role:

The Times is seeking a versatile, experienced and fast-adapting journalist and visual editor to join the photo department in a dual role working both with the special projects team and as a floater photo editor on various desks and projects as needed.

As a photo editor working with the Projects and Initiatives (P&I) team, you will collaborate with P&I editors and relevant desk editors to shape the visual approach for a variety of stories or series throughout the year. You will assign and research a wide array of news and feature photographs, working productively with staff and freelance photographers, wire services, agencies and all other sources of visuals. Projects will range across subject areas and may be visually rooted in archival photography, traditional news and documentary work, or image-making that experiments with new technology.

As a floater photo editor, you will temporarily take on photo editing roles across various desks and a wide range of beats and subject areas. Flexibility is essential, as your schedule may vary week to week and can include nights, weekends, and holidays.

You are an editorial generalist with deep curiosity, and you thrive in a collaborative environment — working productively with editors, designers, videographers and developers. You are capable of pivoting between disparate subject matters—from hard news to culture and features and long-lead enterprise—without sacrificing quality or editorial depth. Also, you bring a strong demonstrable passion for visual journalism across modern digital formats.

This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Conceive, pitch, develop, edit, pace and help build powerful and innovative visual stories with attention to detail in a fast-paced newsroom.
  • Maintain the highest standard of photography and multimedia assigning for feature, news and enterprise stories for all platforms including mobile, print and social.
  • Seamlessly toggle between breaking news workflows and long-lead enterprise projects, recalibrating editing pace and narrative style as coverage demands.
  • Identify, vet and onboard new contributing photojournalists as needed. Ensure that new contributors are versed and committed to ethical journalistic rigor, independence and integrity. Build relationships with the photographers you are directing through briefings, regular contact and feedback.
  • Collaborate with designers, writers, reporters, video journalists, editors and photographers to shape ideas into visual story opportunities.
  • Demonstrate strong editorial judgment, working with Times editors and legal department for all vetting, copyright, legal and ethical questions.
  • Focus on working with a diverse range of subjects and photographers, keeping our global and multigenerational audience in mind.
  • Coordinate with newsroom desk editors and security team members to ensure the utmost preparation, training and safety of our photojournalists in the field.
  • Maintain and work within the photo budget, process/approve invoices.
  • Actively contribute to photo department meetings with reports and updates of your desk's visual priorities.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to a Deputy Editor of Photography.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years experience in a newsroom or equivalent.
  • Experience assigning and directing photojournalists in a variety of situations.
  • Proven deep research skills.
  • Expertise in handling electronic images, photographic usage and copyright issues.
  • Strong technical skills, including proficiency in digital tools and programs, including content management systems, Photoshop, PhotoMechanic, video editing tools and social media platforms.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • An enthusiasm for visual journalism and current events, coupled with keen news judgment and a firm sense of journalistic ethics.
  • Strong organizational, communication and collaborative abilities.
  • Knowledge of Adobe Premiere.
  • Experience prioritizing and managing multiple projects in fast-moving environments
  • The initiative to take on and learn new technologies and tasks.
  • Openness to working a flexible schedule as news demands.
  • Experience making quick decisions under deadlines and a high-pressure news environment.

job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. About the Role

The Developer Platforms mission at The New York Times builds the foundational platforms, tooling, and paved paths that help product teams ship high‑quality experiences quickly and safely. Our Application Delivery team owns the shared software delivery platform (CI/CD, artifact management) and deployment workflows used by hundreds of engineers across News, Cooking, Games and Audio to ship software.

As the Times leans into AI‑assisted and agentic development, Application Delivery is where those changes become real. You will set the technical direction for how AI‑generated and agent‑driven change flows safely, observably, and at scale through CI/CD.

You'll help teams reduce release risk with modern deployment patterns, and turn effective delivery practices into reusable pipelines and templates that scale across the organization, much like our GenAI platform roles turn internal practices into reusable tools and agents. When you improve this platform, you change how The New York Times ships software.

You will report to the Engineering Manager of the DevEx Application Delivery team. This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days/week.

Responsibilities

  • Lead the technical direction of software delivery as a shared product: shape paved paths in our shared platform that improve code health, release quality, and delivery speed for product teams.

  • Set the technical direction for agent‑ready delivery: design the policy, guardrails, and paved paths that turn AI‑generated and agent‑driven changes (migrations, test generation, pipeline maintenance) into safe, observable releases at scale by partnering with our Developer AI team.

  • Collaborate with Product, engineering leaders, and internal users to shape the roadmap for the delivery platform and bring measurable impact on quality and speed.

  • Deliver scalable, secure, and observable software delivery systems and workflows that improve reliability, and overall software quality and velocity.

  • Champion engineering excellence in delivery by setting best practices for testing, deployment strategies, progressive delivery, and observability that are easy to adopt through the platform.

  • Mentor engineers across the mission, contribute to hiring, and help foster an inclusive, collaborative engineering culture centered on shared platforms and high‑quality software delivery.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our mission and values and a commitment to our purpose to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience building the technical strategy and driving software delivery (Github Actions, Argo CD or equivalent CI/CD systems) or similar platform work with broad organizational impact beyond operations.

  • Experience building and scaling a platform as a product for internal engineers with multi-tenancy serving many teams through self‑service paved paths, with attention to adoption, backward compatibility, and isolation/guardrails between tenants

  • Demonstrated proficiency in building and maintaining production services in one or more general‑purpose programming languages (e.g., Go, Python, TypeScript/Node.js, or Java), including code review and debugging complex issues.

  • 5+ years of experience with containers, Kubernetes, package management tools(Helm or equivalent), IAC tools(Terraform or equivalent), Gitops‑based deployment workflows and cloud services such as AWS, GCP.

  • Experience using delivery and productivity metrics (e.g., DORA, SPACE) and platform observability to measure and improve release quality and delivery.

  • Proficiency with GenAI‑assisted developer tooling (e.g., Cursor, Copilot, or Claude Code) and judgment about how to integrate agentic workflows into CI/CD safely.

  • Experience leading cross‑team technical work, communicating trade‑offs, and building understanding among diverse partners including Product, platform, and product engineering teams.

  • Experience mentoring engineers and contributing to an inclusive, collaborative engineering culture.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Exposure to artifact/package management (e.g., Artifactory or similar) with attention to security, retention, cost, and ease of use for engineers.

This is a role with the opportunity to lead high-profile work that helps us achieve our enterprise goals, find new areas of growth, and make our operations more effective.

It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The Publishing group at The New York Times builds and maintains the content management system powering all Times platforms. We empower engineering teams to evolve digital experiences while providing creators with interconnected tools to uphold our journalistic mission.

The Content Data Products team governs the centralized, compliance-cleared platform for all Times content data. Partnering closely with the New AI Products and Platforms (NAPP) team—whose Discovery Engine (search, knowledge graph, and AI) relies on our infrastructure—we ensure our rich archive is ingested, structured, attributed, and indexed across all brands (News, Cooking, Wirecutter, The Athletic, Games) and multimedia formats (articles, video, interactives).

We are looking for a Technical Product Manager II to lead our content data warehouse roadmap and its feeding pipelines. Reporting to the Senior TPM for NAPP, you will partner with engineering to bring product strategy across editorial, AI, and partner requirements.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days/week.

Responsibilities:

  • Roadmap Execution: Lead the strategy and delivery for the content data warehouse and ingestion pipelines for new content types and metadata enrichment.

  • Data Modeling & Indexing: Define specifications for modeling, ingesting, and indexing new content formats (e.g., video, interactives, acquired brand content) for search, retrieval, and AI use cases.

  • Catalog Optimization: Partner with operations, legal, and teams to audit archival structures, address metadata gaps, and improve catalog completeness.

  • Collaboration: Gather requirements, establish data contracts, prioritize features, and communicate roadmap progress and risks across engineering, design, editorial, and leadership.

  • Product Delivery: Guide the end-to-end product development lifecycle from concept to launch with high quality.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 3–5 years of experience in technical product management with a focus on content data and platform infrastructure.

  • 3+ years of experience launching complex software products in close partnership with engineering teams.

  • Demonstrated experience with unstructured or multimedia data ingestion pipelines and downstream integrations (e.g., search indexes, analytics, ML/AI systems).

  • Experience navigating ambiguous spaces, conduct research, define technical requirements, and experience communicating complex technical concepts to a variety of audiences to diverse audiences.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Information Science, Journalism, or equivalent experience.

  • Familiarity with search/retrieval systems and how structured metadata powers search engines and AI capabilities.

  • Working knowledge of SQL, relational database architecture, and schema auditing.

#LI-Hybrid

REQ-020848

Compensation and Benefits For This Role:

In addition to base salary, this role is also eligible for variable pay, such as an annual bonus and restricted stock. Benefits include medical, dental and vision benefits, Flexible Spending Accounts (F.S.A.s), a company-matching 401(k) plan, employee stock purchase plan, paid vacation, paid sick days, paid parental leave, tuition reimbursement and professional development programs.

 

 

 

The annual base pay range for this role is between:$120,000—$142,000 USD

Candidate Use of GenAI Tools:

We’re excited to learn more about you and your experience. To keep our hiring process as fair and authentic as possible, we ask that you submit your own work and not use GenAI tools to generate substantive content during the application and interview process.

If you’re an engineering candidate, we’ll let you know what specific GenAI tools you are permitted to use for your technical assessment.

 

The New York Times Company is committed to being the world’s best source of independent, reliable and quality journalism. To do so, we embrace a diverse workforce that has a broad range of backgrounds and experiences across our ranks, at all levels of the organization. We encourage people from all backgrounds to apply.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and do not discriminate on the basis of an individual's sex, age, race, color, creed, national origin, alienage, religion, marital status, pregnancy, sexual orientation or affectional preference, gender identity and expression, disability, genetic trait or predisposition, carrier status, citizenship, veteran or military status and other personal characteristics protected by law. All applications will receive consideration for employment without regard to legally protected characteristics. The U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC)’s Know Your Rights Poster is available here. 

The New York Times Company will provide reasonable accommodations as required by applicable federal, state, and/or local laws. Individuals seeking an accommodation for the application or interview process should email reasonable.accommodations@nytimes.com. Emails sent for unrelated issues, such as following up on an application, will not receive a response.

For information about The New York Times' privacy practices for job applicants, click here.

Please beware of fraudulent job postings. Scammers may post fraudulent job opportunities, and they may even make fraudulent employment offers. This is done by bad actors to collect personal information and money from victims. All legitimate job opportunities from The New York Times will be accessible through The New York Times careers site. The New York Times will not ask job applicants for financial information or for payment, and will not refer you to a third party to do so. You should never send money to anyone who suggests they can provide employment with The New York Times.

If you see a fake or fraudulent job posting, or if you suspect you have received a fraudulent offer, you can report it to The New York Times at NYTapplicants@nytimes.com. You can also file a report with the Federal Trade Commission or your state attorney general.
