job.title: Head of Shows, New York Magazine
job.description:
THE ROLE

New York Magazine is seeking a Head of Shows to lead our multiplatform show strategy across audio and video programming. This person will identify the most promising opportunities across our editorial brands, develop original franchises, and build a sustainable slate of shows that extend the reach and impact of New York Magazine across audio, video, social, and live platforms.

The ideal candidate is both a creative leader and a skilled production operator: someone who has successfully developed and launched multiple shows out of newsrooms, understands the audio and video landscape, and can recognize distinctive editorial voices and talent that translate into compelling programming.

In this role, you will work across New York Magazine’s portfolio, including The Cut, Vulture, and its four additional verticals, to identify talent, concepts, and audience opportunities that can become signature New York franchises.

This is a permanent, full-time position. This job is benefits-eligible. We pride ourselves in providing comprehensive benefits to support all of our employees wherever they are in life.

This role is located in our New York City office.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Develop and execute a long-term video and audio strategy for New York Magazine, identifying the largest audience, editorial, and business opportunities across the magazine’s brands, coverage areas, and talent roster.
  • Conceive, develop, and launch new show concepts from idea through pilot, testing, and release, including the creation of multiple pilots and proof-of-concept projects in the first year.
  • Oversee all aspects of show development, including editorial direction, host development, visual approach, production workflows, and programming.
  • Build a long-term roadmap and development pipeline for a portfolio of multiplatform shows that support audience growth, engagement, and revenue objectives.
  • Partner with audience, video, and social teams to develop programming and distribution strategies for YouTube, podcast platforms, and social channels, including episode packaging, clips, and original social content.
  • Use audience insights and performance data to refine formats, grow existing shows, and inform development and investment decisions.
  • Identify and evaluate the potential to acquire or partner with existing external shows, creators, and talent when there is an opportunity to strengthen coverage areas aligned with the magazine’s audio and video strategy.
  • Build and manage a team, recruiting producers, external creative partners, and talent as needed, and oversee production budgets and schedules.
  • Work with the editorial team to integrate show appearances and video opportunities into major editorial bookings.
  • Partner with editors and production teams to develop author-read audio versions of major stories at a regular cadence.
  • Lead broader cross-functional stakeholder management and execution, e.g., collaborating with the audience team to develop multiplatform growth strategies and partnering with ad sales and subscription teams to build out franchise business opportunities

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

  • 10+ years of experience developing, launching, and growing original video programs, podcasts, or multiplatform franchises.
  • Demonstrated track record of taking shows from concept to launch and audience growth, with experience across both video and audio.
  • Strong editorial instincts and experience translating culture, politics, business, lifestyle, or entertainment coverage into compelling audio and video formats.
  • Experience identifying, developing, and coaching on-air and on-camera talent.
  • Experience cultivating, managing, and collaborating with top-tier talent, creators, and celebrities.
  • Strong understanding of original video programming, video podcasting, creator-led media, and cross-platform content strategies.
  • Deep knowledge of audience behavior and distribution across YouTube, podcast platforms, and social channels.
  • Understanding of how shows can extend into newsletters, community, and live experiences.
  • Experience building teams, managing production budgets, and establishing development and production workflows.
  • Excellent project management, communication, and cross-functional leadership skills, including experience working closely with audience and revenue teams.
  • Ability to operate strategically while also executing hands-on development work.
  • Entrepreneurial mindset and comfort building programs from the ground up

job.title: Producer, Vox Video
job.description:
WHO WE ARE

Vox candidly shepherds audiences through politics and policy, business and pop culture, food, science, and everything else that matters.

Vox is part of Vox Media, the leading modern media company. We guide our audience from discovery to obsession. We inspire essential conversations about what’s now, what’s next, and what’s possible.

As a community of journalists and storytellers, business professionals, creators and technologists, we believe it is a moral and business imperative to amplify voices: to cultivate diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout our organization and media. This applies to our candidates, our teams, our storytelling, our creative work, and our platforms, products, and partnerships.

THE ROLE

Vox is looking for an experienced producer and on-camera host to join our award-winning video team. You will be part of a team that creates thoughtful, original midform videos, preserving the explanatory DNA that is essential to Vox, while also developing new video formats and series. 

Top candidates will have a professional background in video journalism with exceptional reporting, scripting, and editing skills. The producer will be expected to pitch, develop and host original video explainers on deadline and produce best-in-class video storytelling that Vox has become known for. The ideal candidate will have an established track record of timely, relevant video journalism, as well as a portfolio of on-camera work. 

This person will also be a creative thinker who wants to experiment with new storytelling formats. We want someone who’s not afraid to try new things and learn from them. There are many ways to create an explainer, and the right candidate will bring innovation and fresh ideas to the position. 

This is a permanent, full-time position. This job is benefits-eligible. We pride ourselves in providing comprehensive benefits to support all of our employees wherever they are in life. This role is a part of the Vox Media Union, represented by the Writers Guild of America, East.

This role is located in our New York City office.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Pitch, research, report, script, and host original video stories. 
  • Produce timely, relevant midform videos aligned with the news cycle.
  • Shoot and edit videos in-studio and in the field. 
  • Host videos on camera, bringing a natural presence and a distinct voice to the work.
  • Manage every aspect of video production from start to finish, delivering high-quality results efficiently and on deadline. 
  • Manage multiple projects at various stages of production in a fast-paced setting and maintain a pipeline of work; this role will require strong organizational and time-management skills. 
  • Collaborate closely with journalists across the Vox newsroom to turn our journalism into smart, timely videos.
  • Pitch, develop and test new storytelling techniques, formats, and series.
  • Adhere to all journalistic and legal standards at all times.
  • Complete additional duties as assigned.

WHO YOU ARE

We’re looking for a creative, enthusiastic producer with a passion for Vox’s explanatory mission. You’ll have:

  • 3-5 years of experience in video journalism. 
  • A portfolio of on-camera journalism that brings clarity to the subject and demonstrates an ability to connect with audiences.
  • A passion for Vox’s mission of helping audiences understand what really matters.
  • An established record of deep research, reporting, scripting and high-quality field production.
  • Expert-level understanding of Adobe Suite, with a high-level of expertise in Premiere and knowledge of After Effects, Photoshop and Illustrator.
  • Familiarity with YouTube video production and publishing, as well as, vertical video editing tools such as Capcut, Descript.
  • Proficiency with studio lighting setups and field shoots
  • Strong communication, organizational and time-management skills, as well as, attention to detail.
  • Collaborative team player who will enjoy working across the organization.

To apply, please submit a cover letter outlining your skills and experience. Include links to three videos that demonstrate your ability to pitch, develop, script, and edit original video stories. At least one video example should prominently feature your on-camera work.

job.title: Senior Product Designer
job.description:
About the Role

This role is on the New York Magazine Product team, which is responsible for the experience of  its digital products. The Senior Product Designer works closely with other members of the product design team and product managers, and collaborates  with Consumer Revenue, Editorial and other teams as necessary..

 

The Product team creates, maintains, evaluates and evolves  the platforms that connect New York Magazine’s journalism with our audiences. We’re adept, curious problem-solvers who transform creative ideas into successful products. Great design and user experience are essential to our ability to connect with our readers. The Product Design team plays an important role, ensuring that our products are engaging, useful, and beautiful.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Create  and shape  user-centric, cross-platform digital experiences & interfaces that our audiences love, and which support our subscription business. .
  • Design and execute projects across the entire product lifecycle, from concepts to multi-platform product launches.
  • Present solutions to stakeholders, frame design decisions, articulate tradeoffs, and advocate for the reader and subscriber, while concurrently driving core business objectives.
  • Solve complex design problems, while synthesizing multiple inputs along the way.

job.title: Senior Video Producer, Pivot
job.description:
Pivot is hiring a Senior Video Producer who will treat our YouTube channel and social video accounts as products in their own right. The successful candidate will use their creativity to produce appealing content and craft strategies that grow each channel.  This is a hands-on role for someone who's obsessed with how YouTube and short-form platforms actually work — not just a content calendar manager, but someone who analyzes the metrics, tests thumbnails and titles, and knows what makes a clip travel. Speed matters as much as strategy here: we record twice weekly, and the producer needs to turn around publish-ready clips fast — same-day or next-day — to capitalize on news moments while they're relevant. You'll also direct a small remote freelance editing team on longer-turnaround pieces. This role blends strategy, fast hands-on editing, and people management.

What You'll Do

  • Turn around quick, publishable social clips fast — same-day or next-day — with clean cuts, captions, pacing, and sound/music design that fit each platform's native style, prioritizing speed without sacrificing quality; this is a daily part of the role. 
  • Write clear, shot-by-shot scripts and edit briefs for social video clips.  
  • Edit short-form social video: clean cuts, captions, pacing, and sound/music design that fit each platform's native style, with fast turnaround as the default expectation. 
  • Optimize clipping workflow with ongoing testing and assessment of AI clipping tools.
  • When necessary, assign and oversee freelance social video editors. (Freelancers are typically reserved for higher-volume days or less time-sensitive content.)
  • Review and QC freelancer cuts for pacing, accuracy, and brand fit, and give direct feedback to keep quality consistent.
  • Partner closely with our podcast production team to guide clip selection and format decisions based on what's performing well.
  • Own YouTube channel strategy end-to-end: titles, thumbnails, descriptions, chapters, and a dedicated YouTube Shorts pipeline. Run a continuous testing process on titles and thumbnails to improve click-through and retention.
  • Set and manage the posting calendar and platform-specific strategy across Instagram, TikTok, and Threads.
  • Deliver monthly analytics reporting (subscriber growth, average view duration, CTR, follower growth by platform) and use it to inform what gets prioritized editorially on social channels.
  • Stay ahead of platform changes and emerging formats, and bring new ideas to the team proactively.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years running YouTube and/or social channels for a media brand, podcast, or creator, with a track record of measurable audience growth.
  • Fast, efficient video editing skills and a demonstrated ability to hit tight, same-day/next-day turnarounds without cutting corners on quality — this is one of the most important skills for the role.
  • Hands-on proficiency in Premiere Pro, CapCut, or similar, with a portfolio of short-form clips you've cut yourself (captions, pacing, sound design, platform-native formatting).
  • Experience writing or directing edit scripts/briefs for other editors, and comfort managing remote or freelance contributors — assigning work, giving feedback, and holding a quality bar.
  • Deep fluency in YouTube Studio analytics and YouTube Shorts; comfort with tools like TubeBuddy or VidIQ is a plus.
  • Strong short-form platform instincts — you can look at a piece of content and tell us whether it will work on TikTok vs. Instagram vs. YouTube Shorts, and why.
  • Experience with news, politics, business, or tech content is a strong plus given Pivot's subject matter.
  • Comfortable working with raw or long-form video/audio content and collaborating with editors on cuts.
  • A strategic, analytical mindset paired with genuine creative instinct and hands-on craft — this role is equal parts data, taste, and execution.

 

PAY TRANSPARENCY

Job Title: Analyst, Income Tracking


A little bit about our team:

The Income Tracking Analyst role falls within the overall structure of the Administration Team and has a direct impact on our songwriters through tracking and recovering revenue from all streams of income. The role will liaise with all areas of our business and work closely with our Finance, Royalty, Copyright and Automation teams. You will have the opportunity to work with international affiliates, licensees and collection societies.


This department is vital to the service Warner Chappell provides to its clients: the songwriters.


Your role:

In this role, you will be responsible for the forensic analysis of income received against income expectations for catalog and new deal income across all major revenue streams and instigate back-claims, adjustments and supplemental payments where required.  You will enjoy the opportunity to provide input into the creation of tools that support Income Tracking as well as the opportunity to collaborate with internal departments to create and improve processes that adapt to the constantly evolving nature of music licensing. If you love music and have a mind for business this could be the position for you! 


Here you’ll get to:

  • Work as an integrated member of a future-facing administration team.
  • Evolve workflows to take our income tracking to the next level.
  • Identify and make claims for shortfalls in income.
  • Provide market share insights to key stakeholders and executives
  • Monitor accurate deal level revenue across all income streams 
  • Deliver monthly updates of deal performance for priority deals
  • Analyze and confirm payment posting of prior publisher income for applicable deals
  • Ensure affiliate income queries relating to domestic income are resolved
  • Support the Admin team on projects including ad hoc queries and income analysis
  • You will work closely with the US Royalty and Copyright teams to both resolve and  proactively prevent against problems arising with the collection of income

About you:

  • You have skills to analyze, extract & manipulate data from high volume data files
  • You have advanced Excel capabilities including Power Pivot & advanced formulae
  • You have a solid understanding of the flow of publishing income and copyright registration
  • You are passionate about music and enjoy working with spreadsheets
  • Excellent organizational and time management skills
  • The ability to manage multiple projects at once and hit time-sensitive deadlines
  • The ability to join dots, think laterally and understand both downstream and upstream impact of events

We’d love it if you also had:

  • Experience working with PRO’s as well as HFA, MLC, and/or other collection societies
  • Experience with Alteryx, Snowflake, and/or Tableau
  • Ability to design high-quality decks and visual materials using presentation platforms, such as Canva or Google Slides.
  • A proactive approach to integrating Generative AI (e.g., Gemini) into everyday work to support and streamline daily tasks and overall productivity.

At Warner Music Group, our Strategic Finance team serves as the analytical engine that drives both our high-level business strategy and day-to-day operations. By extracting actionable intelligence from core financial data, the team partners seamlessly across Warner Music’s Central Functions, Recorded Music, and Music Publishing to uncover deep business insights. Ultimately, Strategic Finance sits at the forefront of the company, mapping the financial dynamics and emerging trends that are actively shaping the future of the global music industry.

Your role:

As the Data Scientist for Strategic Finance, you will act as the crucial link between our financial strategists and the Technology department. A key part of your mission is collaborating closely with the technology engineers and data scientists who are building our state-of-the-art predictive forecasting platform, ensuring the tool perfectly aligns with business needs. Alongside this, you will deploy modern AI solutions to automate complex financial workflows and transform ambiguous, disparate data into standardized, cohesive datasets—moving the department away from fragile legacy spreadsheets and toward a highly automated, self-service data ecosystem.

Here you’ll get to:

• Partner closely with Technology and Affiliate Finance teams to gather requirements, design, and deploy a robust financial forecasting and planning tool that supports WMG's long-term modeling.
• Spearhead AI and automation initiatives to eliminate manual bottlenecks and streamline workflows across Strategic Finance.
• Enforce data integrity within Strategic Finance by collaborating with data management teams to architect datasets and automate rigorous quality controls.
• Work directly with senior finance collaborators to clarify complex problems and build the right analytical or technology-based approaches using large, dynamic datasets.
• Act as the trusted liaison between Strategic Finance, Technology, and data platform collaborators to ensure all technical solutions perfectly align with business priorities.

Distribution operations are the specialist team within the WEA Global Operations dept that supports WMG’s distribution business including ADA. In the Distribution Operations department, we work to ensure that releases from independent labels and artists are delivered on time and in accordance with industry standards, DSP guidelines, and the creative strategy of our partners. This is a collaborative role that interfaces with internal business entities as well as other Global Operations teams as well as external label partners and artists. We’re a group of creative problem solvers whose goal is to support independent music and position labels and artists for success. Getting products to market is the backbone of a distribution company!


Your role:

As Manager of Revelator Distribution Operations, you will play a critical role in supporting key clients and internal teams during US business hours. You will build deep expertise in the Revelator platform to oversee end-to-end operational workflows. In this position, you will drive seamless catalog ingestion support, monitor release deliveries, resolve technical DSP issues, optimize metadata and assets, and deliver actionable operational reporting to ensure independent labels and artists are set up for success across global digital service providers.


Here you’ll get to:


  • Catalog ingestion & delivery - provide support to the DSCO Catalog Ingestion team as they lead on catalog creation and delivery into Revelator
  • Delivery monitoring - Monitor delivery feeds and supply chain events daily; identify failed, stalled and rejected deliveries and action them within agreed turnaround time
  • Delivery monitoring - Manage (Investigate and resolve) DSP delivery errors, metadata rejections and asset failures
  • Delivery monitoring - bring up relevant issues to engineering with reproducible detail where a platform fix is required.
  • Delivery monitoring - Raise, track and chase tickets with DSP partners (Apple, Spotify, YouTube, Amazon and others) through to closure.
  • Metadata & asset optimization - Identify and optimize metadata including artist disambiguation / profile mapping, contributor enhancement, artwork / audio replacement, 
  • Operational reporting - Produce recurring operational reporting on delivery volumes, error rates, open partner tickets and ingestion progress.
  • Operational reporting - Respond to internal and client queries on delivery and catalogue status within agreed service levels
  • Key direct operational contact - provide key direct operational support to US time zone business entities

About you:

  • 2–4 years' experience in digital distribution, digital supply chain or content operations within the music, media or entertainment industry.
  • Hands-on experience of content ingestion, metadata management and delivery to digital service providers including their unique CMSs (Apple Connect, S4MP etc)
  • Working knowledge of music metadata standards and the identifiers that underpin them (ISRC, UPC/EAN, ISNI), and familiarity with DDEX message types and delivery feeds.
  • Intermediate SQL — able to write and adapt queries with joins and filters against a relational database without assistance.

We’d love it if you also had:

  • Passion for supporting independent music
  • An interest in efficiency tools (Airtable etc) and application of AI tools for business 
  • Working knowledge of industry developments and commercial practices

  • Executive Leadership: Partner closely with the C-suite, technology teams, and global business unit heads to integrate supply chain capabilities into the broader corporate data ecosystem.

Leveraging a deep, authentic fluency across Hip-Hop, R&B, Afrobeats, and emerging subgenres, you will build distinct, competitive brand identities that penetrate both mainstream markets and niche subcultures.

This is a high-visibility leadership role requiring a synthesis of creative intuition, subcultural intelligence, and data-backed decisiveness.   • Direct cross-functional alignment across Digital Strategy, Streaming/Commerce, Sync, Radio, PR, and International Teams, ensuring a unified strategic vision across every consumer touchpoint
  • Utilize real-time consumer analytics, social listenership data, and consumption telemetry to adapt campaigns mid-flight, maximizing ROI and hitting label OKRs
  • Collaborate with Creative Services, visual directors, and creative partners to curate and cultivate authentic visual worlds, video strategies, and story arcs across all campaign channels
  • Partner with touring teams, live agents, and festival promoters to align recorded releases with immersive live experiences, pop-ups, and global tour rollouts
  • Partner with Commerce and Direct-to-Fan teams to design exclusive physical drops, limited-edition vinyl/merch variants, and streaming strategies that deepen fan loyalty and generate incremental revenue
  • Secure non-traditional alliances across sports, streetwear, gaming, luxury, and LGBTQ+ subcultures to extend artist footprints into broader sectors

job.title: Justice Reporter
job.description:
Application Instructions

Please list all professional experience and explain any gaps in employment history. All of your application materials, which may include PDF files of work samples and/or links to audio, video, photography or graphics, must be uploaded to the field labeled Resume/Cover Letter/Work Samples to be considered for the position.


Join the future of news

We’re on a mission to deliver riveting storytelling for all of America. At The Washington Post, you’ll help reinvent news. Our work is driven by a deep investigative spirit and enhanced by innovation to bring audiences closer to the stories that matter most.


About Our Team


The Washington Post is powered by the passion and talent of our people. It takes all of us to reinvent news. Beyond our award-winning News and Opinions teams, we work across many departments, including Brand & Events, Communications, Customer Care, Engineering & Product, Finance, Human Resources, Legal, Marketing & Advertising, Print Operations, and Sales.


Why This Role Matters

 

The Washington Post is seeking an experienced, rigorous journalist to cover the Department of Justice, the FBI and other federal law enforcement agencies and those institutions’ relationships with the White House, Congress, and candidates for federal office. This reporter will break news and produce authoritative journalism about federal investigations, prosecutions and law enforcement policy across a wide range of subjects. 


This is a highly competitive beat that requires persistence, discretion and an ability to distinguish significant developments from the noise surrounding high-profile investigations. The successful candidate will help readers understand not only what federal law enforcement is doing, but how decisions are being made, what forces are influencing them and what the consequences are for individuals, institutions and the country.


This coverage is central to The Post's mission and frequently intersects with politics, national security and other major areas of our report. A collaborative spirit and enthusiasm for partnering with journalists across the newsroom are essential.


This position is based in our Washington, D.C., newsroom.


What Motivates You

  • You are driven to break consequential news and uncover what is happening inside powerful institutions.
  • You thrive on developing sources and building the trust necessary to produce sensitive, exclusive reporting.
  • You are fascinated by the intersection of law enforcement, politics, national security and power.
  • You enjoy moving between fast-breaking developments and deeper enterprise work.
  • You are committed to fair-minded reporting, particularly when covering allegations, investigations and prosecutions with significant consequences for the people involved.

How You’ll Support the Mission

  • Break news on the Justice Department, FBI and other federal law enforcement agencies, developing authoritative coverage of investigations, indictments, prosecutions and major policy decisions.
  • Develop and maintain a deep network of sources across federal law enforcement, the legal community, government and other institutions relevant to the beat.
  • Cover major investigations involving prominent individuals and institutions.
  • Produce smart, timely analysis that helps readers understand the significance of complicated legal and investigative developments.
  • Develop ambitious stories that reveal how federal law enforcement operates and hold officials and institutions accountable.
  • Handle highly sensitive source reporting with exceptional judgment, discretion and attention to verification.
  • Report and write quickly as urgent news requires while continuing to develop longer-term reporting targets.
  • Translate complex legal proceedings, investigative processes and institutional dynamics into clear, accessible journalism for a broad audience.
  • Collaborate closely with colleagues across Politics & Government, Investigations, National, International and other departments on stories that cross coverage areas.
  • Work with visual journalists and social video teams to identify the most compelling ways to present complex and consequential stories.
  • Adhere rigorously to the highest standards of accuracy, fairness and journalistic ethics, including giving subjects of our reporting meaningful opportunities to respond.

The Skills and Experience You Bring

  • A demonstrated track record of high-profile scoops, exclusive reporting and consequential accountability journalism.
  • Knowledge of federal law enforcement, criminal justice and the institutions and processes surrounding them.
  • A strong source base — or a demonstrated ability to develop one — among federal law enforcement officials, attorneys and others relevant to the beat.
  • Proven ability to cover breaking news with speed, precision and authority.
  • Experience handling sensitive sourcing and reporting on investigations in which accuracy, fairness and discretion are paramount.
  • Demonstrated ability to produce ambitious enterprise, investigations and compelling explanatory journalism.
  • Excellent writing skills and an ability to make complicated legal and institutional subjects understandable to a broad audience.
  • Strong news judgment and the ability to manage multiple competitive storylines simultaneously.
  • A collaborative mindset and eagerness to work with journalists throughout the newsroom.
  • A commitment to accuracy, fairness and the highest standards of journalism.

Interested candidates should upload a cover letter, résumé and three examples of their work (as PDFs) to our jobs portal. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled, but those received by Nov. 25 will be prioritized. job.title: Justice Reporter
job.description:
Application Instructions

Please list all professional experience and explain any gaps in employment history. All of your application materials, which may include PDF files of work samples and/or links to audio, video, photography or graphics, must be uploaded to the field labeled Resume/Cover Letter/Work Samples to be considered for the position.


Join the future of news

We’re on a mission to deliver riveting storytelling for all of America. At The Washington Post, you’ll help reinvent news. Our work is driven by a deep investigative spirit and enhanced by innovation to bring audiences closer to the stories that matter most.


About Our Team


The Washington Post is powered by the passion and talent of our people. It takes all of us to reinvent news. Beyond our award-winning News and Opinions teams, we work across many departments, including Brand & Events, Communications, Customer Care, Engineering & Product, Finance, Human Resources, Legal, Marketing & Advertising, Print Operations, and Sales.


Why This Role Matters

 

The Washington Post is seeking an experienced, rigorous journalist to cover the Department of Justice, the FBI and other federal law enforcement agencies and those institutions’ relationships with the White House, Congress, and candidates for federal office. This reporter will break news and produce authoritative journalism about federal investigations, prosecutions and law enforcement policy across a wide range of subjects. 


This is a highly competitive beat that requires persistence, discretion and an ability to distinguish significant developments from the noise surrounding high-profile investigations. The successful candidate will help readers understand not only what federal law enforcement is doing, but how decisions are being made, what forces are influencing them and what the consequences are for individuals, institutions and the country.


This coverage is central to The Post's mission and frequently intersects with politics, national security and other major areas of our report. A collaborative spirit and enthusiasm for partnering with journalists across the newsroom are essential.


This position is based in our Washington, D.C., newsroom.


What Motivates You

  • You are driven to break consequential news and uncover what is happening inside powerful institutions.
  • You thrive on developing sources and building the trust necessary to produce sensitive, exclusive reporting.
  • You are fascinated by the intersection of law enforcement, politics, national security and power.
  • You enjoy moving between fast-breaking developments and deeper enterprise work.
  • You are committed to fair-minded reporting, particularly when covering allegations, investigations and prosecutions with significant consequences for the people involved.

How You’ll Support the Mission

  • Break news on the Justice Department, FBI and other federal law enforcement agencies, developing authoritative coverage of investigations, indictments, prosecutions and major policy decisions.
  • Develop and maintain a deep network of sources across federal law enforcement, the legal community, government and other institutions relevant to the beat.
  • Cover major investigations involving prominent individuals and institutions.
  • Produce smart, timely analysis that helps readers understand the significance of complicated legal and investigative developments.
  • Develop ambitious stories that reveal how federal law enforcement operates and hold officials and institutions accountable.
  • Handle highly sensitive source reporting with exceptional judgment, discretion and attention to verification.
  • Report and write quickly as urgent news requires while continuing to develop longer-term reporting targets.
  • Translate complex legal proceedings, investigative processes and institutional dynamics into clear, accessible journalism for a broad audience.
  • Collaborate closely with colleagues across Politics & Government, Investigations, National, International and other departments on stories that cross coverage areas.
  • Work with visual journalists and social video teams to identify the most compelling ways to present complex and consequential stories.
  • Adhere rigorously to the highest standards of accuracy, fairness and journalistic ethics, including giving subjects of our reporting meaningful opportunities to respond.

The Skills and Experience You Bring

  • A demonstrated track record of high-profile scoops, exclusive reporting and consequential accountability journalism.
  • Knowledge of federal law enforcement, criminal justice and the institutions and processes surrounding them.
  • A strong source base — or a demonstrated ability to develop one — among federal law enforcement officials, attorneys and others relevant to the beat.
  • Proven ability to cover breaking news with speed, precision and authority.
  • Experience handling sensitive sourcing and reporting on investigations in which accuracy, fairness and discretion are paramount.
  • Demonstrated ability to produce ambitious enterprise, investigations and compelling explanatory journalism.
  • Excellent writing skills and an ability to make complicated legal and institutional subjects understandable to a broad audience.
  • Strong news judgment and the ability to manage multiple competitive storylines simultaneously.
  • A collaborative mindset and eagerness to work with journalists throughout the newsroom.
  • A commitment to accuracy, fairness and the highest standards of journalism.

Interested candidates should upload a cover letter, résumé and three examples of their work (as PDFs) to our jobs portal. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled, but those received by Nov. 25 will be prioritized. The cover letter should be addressed to Justice Editor Maria Glod, Deputy Politics & Government Editor Jennifer Liberto, Politics & Government Editor Nick Baumann and Managing Editor Peter Spiegel.

The salary range for this position is $137,300 - $228,900. The actual starting salary within this range will depend on individual skills, experience and qualifications as they relate to specific job requirements.

job.title: Manager, FP&A - Revenue & Growth
job.description:
Join the future of news

We’re on a mission to deliver riveting storytelling for all of America. At The Washington Post, you’ll help reinvent news. Our work is driven by a deep investigative spirit and enhanced by innovation to bring audiences closer to the stories that matter most.


About Our Team


The Washington Post is powered by the passion and talent of our people. It takes all of us to reinvent news. Beyond our award-winning News and Opinions teams, we work across many departments, including Brand & Events, Communications, Customer Care, Engineering & Product, Finance, Human Resources, Legal, Marketing & Advertising, Print Operations, and Sales.


Why This Role Matters

 

The Manager, FP&A – Revenue & Growth is a key finance business partner supporting The Washington Post’s B2C digital subscription, B2B revenue, and emerging growth initiatives. This role translates business performance, market dynamics, and operating decisions into clear financial insight that helps leaders invest wisely, manage risk, and build sustainable revenue.

Reporting within the FP&A organization, the Manager leads planning, forecasting, and performance analysis for assigned revenue businesses while developing financial talent and strengthening the tools, processes, and partnerships that support informed decision-making across the company.

 

What Motivates You

  • You are energized by helping mission-driven media organizations build durable, diversified revenue models.
  • You enjoy translating complex financial and operating data into clear insights that guide decisions.
  • You value collaborative partnership with leaders across Product, Marketing, Sales, Newsroom, Data Analytics & Insights, and Finance.
  • You are motivated by improving planning processes, models, and reporting so teams can act with greater clarity and confidence.
  • You take pride in developing financial talent and creating an inclusive, accountable team environment.

 

How You’ll Support the Mission

  • Lead annual budgets, quarterly forecasts, and long-range plans for assigned revenue streams, producing aligned financial plans that support enterprise priorities and growth goals.
  • Develop driver-based revenue models that connect pricing, volume, pipeline, customer behavior, and other operating metrics to reliable financial outcomes.
  • Analyze actual revenue performance against budget and forecast, identifying variance drivers, risks, opportunities, and outlook changes that enable timely leadership action.
  • Advise business leaders on operating performance, investment choices, and resource-allocation decisions, resulting in actionable recommendations grounded in financial and strategic analysis.
  • Evaluate new products, partnerships, pricing strategies, and growth initiatives through business cases, scenario analyses, and financial models, enabling informed decisions on investments and tradeoffs.
  • Partner with Marketing, Sales, Product, Newsroom, Data Analytics & Insights, and other teams to improve revenue performance and align business plans with financial objectives.
  • Incorporate relevant market, competitive, and industry trends into forecasts and planning, strengthening the organization’s ability to anticipate changes in the revenue environment.
  • Strengthen revenue reporting, forecasting, and planning processes through improved data quality, automation, and planning tools, increasing consistency, efficiency, and confidence in financial information.
  • Integrate monthly close results and performance-review insights into forecasts, ensuring leaders understand results and their implications for the forward outlook.
  • Manage and develop financial analyst(s) through clear priorities, coaching, and quality review, building stronger financial modeling, business acumen, and partnership capabilities.
  • Lead strategic analyses and ambiguous growth-related projects, structuring complex questions and communicating conclusions that advance executive decision-making.

 

The Skills and Experience You Bring

  • Six or more years of progressively responsible experience in financial planning and analysis, strategic finance, corporate finance, or a related discipline.
  • Experience supporting revenue-oriented, subscription, digital, consumer, B2B, or growth businesses; media-industry experience is valuable but not required.
  • Experience managing, coaching, or formally leading financial analysts and reviewing complex analytical work.
  • Strong financial modeling, forecasting, budgeting, and scenario-analysis skills, including the ability to connect operating drivers to financial results.
  • Ability to synthesize complex financial and business information into concise, practical recommendations for senior leaders.
  • Strong communication and relationship-building skills, with demonstrated success partnering across functions and levels of an organization.
  • Sound judgment, intellectual curiosity, and comfort navigating evolving priorities and incomplete information.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

 

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with financial planning and analysis platforms, such as Oracle, SAP, Planful, Adaptive Insights, or Anaplan.
  • Experience with data analytics and visualization tools, such as Tableau or Power BI.
  • Knowledge of digital media, consumer subscription, advertising, SaaS, or other recurring-revenue business models.
  • Familiarity with investment analysis, corporate development, partnerships, or mergers and acquisitions.
  • MBA, CFA, CPA, or comparable advanced finance credential.

 

Collaboration makes us stronger. That’s why our offices are designed with open layouts, modern technology, and easy access to transportation. With certain exceptions for newsgathering and business travel, we work on-site five days a week.

Compensation and Benefits

Wherever you are in your life or career, The Washington Post offers comprehensive and inclusive benefits for every step of your journey:

  • Competitive medical, dental and vision coverage

  • Company-paid pension and 401(k) match

  • Three weeks of vacation and up to three weeks of paid sick leave

  • Nine paid holidays and two personal days

  • 20 weeks paid parental leave for any new parent

  • Robust mental health resources

  • Backup care and caregiver concierge services

  • Gender affirming services

  • Pet insurance

  • Free Post digital subscription

  • Leadership and career development programs

Benefits may vary based on the job, full-time or part-time schedule, location, and collectively bargained status.

The salary range for this position is:

$105,600 - $176,000 Annual

The actual salary within this range will depend on individual skills, experience, and qualifications as they relate to specific job requirements. This position may be eligible for a bonus or incentive program, and a member of the Talent Acquisition team will discuss bonus payment terms and conditions during the interview process.

Your story awaits. Apply today!

Learn more about The Post at careers.washingtonpost.com.

job.title: Manager, Software Development, iOS Mobile App
job.description:
Join the future of news

We’re on a mission to deliver riveting storytelling for all of America. At The Washington Post, you’ll help reinvent news. Our work is driven by a deep investigative spirit and enhanced by innovation to bring audiences closer to the stories that matter most.


About Our Team


The Washington Post is powered by the passion and talent of our people. It takes all of us to reinvent news. Beyond our award-winning News and Opinions teams, we work across many departments, including Brand & Events, Communications, Customer Care, Engineering & Product, Finance, Human Resources, Legal, Marketing & Advertising, Print Operations, and Sales.


Why This Role Matters

 

The Washington Post is seeking a Manager, Software Development to lead the engineering team responsible for our iOS app, the foundation for personalization, ads, sections, articles, App Store subscription management, analytics, audio, video and more, and one of The Post’s most important channels for reader engagement. This role provides dedicated people and delivery leadership for the team while partnering closely with Android, Staff Engineering, Product, and shared engineering teams to deliver high-quality mobile experiences quickly and predictably.


This is a hands-on engineering management role. The Manager, Software Development will set priorities and assignments, develop engineers, remove blockers, identify delivery risks early, and establish clear accountability for delivering approved work to readers, while remaining close enough to the technology to guide difficult engineering decisions. The manager is expected to write code, build prototypes, and review pull requests on a regular basis, and will partner with Staff Engineers and feature leads to verify progress, identify misalignment, and follow work through to release.


The ideal candidate combines strong people leadership with deep iOS engineering knowledge, sound technical judgment, and a disciplined approach to execution. This manager will help the team ship faster while maintaining the architecture, performance, reliability, quality, and technical health readers expect from The Washington Post’s flagship mobile experience. The role is data-driven: priorities, estimates, improvements, and results are tracked against agreed baselines and measured by evidence, such as time to users, commitments met, blocker resolution time, and app stability and performance, not by activity or opinion.


What Motivates You

  • You want to help bring The Washington Post’s journalism to readers through high-quality mobile experiences.
  • You measure success by the value delivered to users and how quickly it reaches them.
  • You develop engineers through direct feedback and clear expectations, and you judge your impact by their growth.
  • You care about predictable execution. You know the real remaining work, test whether estimates and status reports are credible, and surface risk before it becomes a missed commitment.
  • You want to stay technically hands-on, writing code, prototyping, and reviewing pull requests to solve problems, evaluate approaches, and stay connected to the systems your team builds.
  • You care deeply about mobile architecture, application quality, performance, reliability, and maintainability.
  • You enjoy removing blockers and working across engineering and product teams to move complex work forward, while leaving ownership with the people who hold it.
  • You hold yourself to the standard you set for others: you own your commitments, communicate risk early, and confirm that issues are closed.
  • You look for wasted effort and ways to improve how teams work, and you measure whether those improvements create value.
  • You enjoy building AI agents and automation that solve real mobile engineering problems, and you care about proving that they work and that people actually use them.
  • You stay current on the iOS ecosystem, including new Apple platform releases, Swift language and concurrency changes, and AI-assisted development in Xcode, and you know which changes are worth adopting and when.

How You’ll Support the Mission

  • Lead and develop the software engineers responsible for The Washington Post’s iOS app, providing timely feedback, career development, performance management, and coaching that builds independent ownership and accountability.
  • Establish priorities and assignments, set delivery baselines, and track progress against estimates through to availability for users. Report on measures such as time to users, commitments met by the agreed date, and blocker resolution time, and surface material delivery risks early with clear facts, tradeoffs, and decisions needed.
  • Address performance concerns promptly and directly, set clear expectations, and confirm that behavior and results improve.
  • Partner with the Android Manager, Staff Engineers, Product, feature leads, and shared teams to sequence work, resolve dependencies and blockers, and keep mobile initiatives aligned without taking over others’ ownership.
  • Provide technical leadership across iOS architecture and development in partnership with Staff Engineers, helping the team make sound decisions on application design, performance, testing, maintainability, and platform best practices across Swift, SwiftUI, UIKit, Objective-C, and Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP).
  • Track changes in the iOS ecosystem, including new Apple OS releases and design updates, Swift and Swift Concurrency evolution, and agentic and AI-assisted tooling in Xcode, and turn them into clear recommendations on what the team should adopt, when, and at what cost.
  • Stay hands-on by writing code, building prototypes, and reviewing pull requests to solve technical problems, evaluate approaches, and set the quality bar for the team.
  • Establish and reinforce engineering practices that support robust testing, code quality, application performance, reliable releases, and the long-term health of the iOS platform.
  • Identify bottlenecks, unnecessary work, technical debt, and opportunities to improve engineering processes and productivity, setting a baseline before each change and measuring the benefit afterward against its cost, rework, and any regressions.
  • Partner with Product and engineering leadership to balance reader experience, business priorities, delivery commitments, and long-term technical health.
  • Build and roll out AI agents and automation that solve iOS and mobile engineering problems, including crash and issue triage, test generation, code review assistance, release workflows, estimation, and detection of stalled work. Verify their output, keep human accountability for decisions, and measure whether they remove delay and effort or only move it.

The Skills and Experience You Bring


Minimum Qualifications

  • BA/BS in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 7+ years of professional native iOS development experience with the iOS SDK, including Swift and modern iOS tools and frameworks, and experience building and releasing production mobile applications.
  • Substantial experience writing production iOS code and designing app architecture, including modular design, concurrency, performance, and testable code, with the ability to review pull requests and architecture proposals at a senior level, evaluate tradeoffs, and diagnose and fix defects.
  • Experience directly managing software engineers, including coaching, career development, and performance management, with a record of timely, specific feedback and of coaching engineers toward independent ownership.
  • Experience leading complex engineering work from planning and estimation through implementation, testing, release, and production support, including setting priorities, managing dependencies, identifying delivery risks, and revising forecasts as evidence changes.
  • Experience with automated testing, CI/CD, version control, and software delivery practices for production mobile applications.
  • Strong communication and problem-solving skills, with experience partnering effectively with Product, senior technical contributors, other engineering teams, and cross-functional stakeholders, including escalating material risks promptly.
  • Experience defining and using engineering metrics and delivery data, including baselines and targets, to identify bottlenecks, make decisions, and demonstrate improvement in team effectiveness.
  • Working knowledge of the current iOS platform, Swift, and Xcode tooling.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Deep experience developing and releasing large-scale consumer iOS applications to the App Store.
  • Experience with modern iOS technologies such as SwiftUI, UIKit, Swift Concurrency, App Intents, Apple’s latest design system, on-device AI frameworks, or comparable technologies; familiarity with Objective-C and Kotlin Multiplatform.
  • Experience with mobile performance optimization, debugging, memory management, and application reliability.
  • Experience integrating RESTful APIs, third-party SDKs, or other services into native mobile applications.
  • Experience leading teams responsible for the full mobile application lifecycle, including architecture, development, automated testing, CI/CD, release, observability, and production support.
  • Experience coordinating engineering work across iOS, Android, backend, platform, or other shared technical teams.
  • Experience improving engineering productivity, delivery predictability, or development processes and measuring the impact of those improvements.
  • Experience mentoring engineers across career levels and partnering effectively with Staff-level or other senior technical contributors.
  • Hands-on experience building AI agents or automation that solve real iOS or mobile engineering problems, with verification of the output and measured benefit.
  • Experience with agentic development workflows in Xcode and with connecting agents to engineering tools such as issue trackers, CI, crash reporting, and source control, for example through Model Context Protocol (MCP).

 

Collaboration makes us stronger. That’s why our offices are designed with open layouts, modern technology, and easy access to transportation. With certain exceptions for newsgathering and business travel, we work on-site five days a week.

Compensation and Benefits

Wherever you are in your life or career, The Washington Post offers comprehensive and inclusive benefits for every step of your journey:

  • Competitive medical, dental and vision coverage

  • Company-paid pension and 401(k) match

  • Three weeks of vacation and up to three weeks of paid sick leave

job.title: Senior Financial Accounting Process and Automation Analyst
job.description:
Join the future of news

We’re on a mission to deliver riveting storytelling for all of America. At The Washington Post, you’ll help reinvent news. Our work is driven by a deep investigative spirit and enhanced by innovation to bring audiences closer to the stories that matter most.


About Our Team


The Washington Post is powered by the passion and talent of our people. It takes all of us to reinvent news. Beyond our award-winning News and Opinions teams, we work across many departments, including Brand & Events, Communications, Customer Care, Engineering & Product, Finance, Human Resources, Legal, Marketing & Advertising, Print Operations, and Sales.


Why This Role Matters

 

The Financial Accounting team enables The Washington Post to report accurately, operate with sound controls, and make timely business decisions. The Financial Accounting Process and Automation Analyst strengthens the way that work gets done by translating accounting needs into practical process improvements, automation opportunities, and ERP-enabled solutions. This role helps reduce manual effort, improve data quality, and create consistent, well-documented workflows across the financial accounting function.


What Motivates You

  • You enjoy understanding how accounting work moves from source data to financial reporting and finding practical ways to make each step clearer, faster, and more reliable.
  • You are curious about automation, ERP capabilities, and data, and you can connect technical possibilities to real accounting and control needs.
  • You value disciplined processes, accurate records, and thoughtful documentation because they make it easier for people to do high-quality work.
  • You like working across Accounting, Finance, Technology, and external partners to turn requirements into solutions that colleagues can adopt.
  • You take ownership of details, follow through on commitments, and use feedback and results to continuously improve the work.

How You’ll Support the Mission

  • Map financial accounting processes by documenting current-state workflows, systems, dependencies, controls, and pain points across areas such as the general ledger, close, reconciliations, reporting, and accounting operations, creating a shared foundation for improvement.
  • Design improved workflows by translating accounting requirements into clear future-state processes, business requirements, and acceptance criteria that reduce rework, improve consistency, and preserve appropriate financial controls.
  • Advance automation opportunities by identifying repeatable manual work, evaluating automation and AI-enabled options with appropriate human review, and helping implement solutions that improve efficiency, accuracy, and auditability.
  • Contribute to ERP design and enhancement by supporting requirements gathering, configuration decisions, testing, data validation, and release readiness so ERP capabilities meet financial-accounting needs.
  • Strengthen data quality and controls by investigating process and data issues, partnering with stakeholders to resolve root causes, and helping maintain reliable handoffs, reconciliations, and documentation.
  • Enable change adoption by developing process documentation, job aids, and training materials that help accounting colleagues understand and consistently use new workflows and tools.
  • Support close and reporting readiness by coordinating process improvements with the accounting calendar and ensuring changes are tested, communicated, and implemented without disrupting critical reporting obligations.
  • Measure process performance by maintaining process metrics, issue logs, and improvement recommendations that help the Controller and accounting leaders prioritize work and assess results.
  • Collaborate across teams by serving as a trusted accounting-process partner to Financial Accounting, FP&A, Technology, Internal Audit, and vendors, bringing clear requirements and disciplined follow-through to shared initiatives.

The Skills and Experience You Bring

  • 3-5 years of experience in financial accounting, accounting operations, finance systems, audit, consulting, or a comparable environment that combines accounting knowledge with process improvement.
  • Working knowledge of U.S. GAAP, core financial-accounting processes, internal controls, and the close and reporting cycle.
  • Experience documenting business processes, gathering requirements, testing changes, and translating stakeholder needs into usable process or system improvements.
  • Experience working with ERP, financial-reporting, workflow, or reconciliation tools; familiarity with platforms such as Workday, Oracle, SAP, BlackLine, Alteryx, or comparable tools is welcome.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to investigate data or process exceptions and identify practical root-cause solutions.

job.description:
Join the future of news

We’re on a mission to deliver riveting storytelling for all of America. At The Washington Post, you’ll help reinvent news. Our work is driven by a deep investigative spirit and enhanced by innovation to bring audiences closer to the stories that matter most.


About Our Team

Why This Role Matters

 

The Financial Accounting team enables The Washington Post to report accurately, operate with sound controls, and make timely business decisions. The Financial Accounting Process and Automation Analyst strengthens the way that work gets done by translating accounting needs into practical process improvements, automation opportunities, and ERP-enabled solutions. This role helps reduce manual effort, improve data quality, and create consistent, well-documented workflows across the financial accounting function.


What Motivates You

  • You enjoy understanding how accounting work moves from source data to financial reporting and finding practical ways to make each step clearer, faster, and more reliable.
  • You are curious about automation, ERP capabilities, and data, and you can connect technical possibilities to real accounting and control needs.
  • You value disciplined processes, accurate records, and thoughtful documentation because they make it easier for people to do high-quality work.
  • You like working across Accounting, Finance, Technology, and external partners to turn requirements into solutions that colleagues can adopt.
  • You take ownership of details, follow through on commitments, and use feedback and results to continuously improve the work.

How You’ll Support the Mission

  • Map financial accounting processes by documenting current-state workflows, systems, dependencies, controls, and pain points across areas such as the general ledger, close, reconciliations, reporting, and accounting operations, creating a shared foundation for improvement.
  • Design improved workflows by translating accounting requirements into clear future-state processes, business requirements, and acceptance criteria that reduce rework, improve consistency, and preserve appropriate financial controls.
  • Advance automation opportunities by identifying repeatable manual work, evaluating automation and AI-enabled options with appropriate human review, and helping implement solutions that improve efficiency, accuracy, and auditability.
  • Contribute to ERP design and enhancement by supporting requirements gathering, configuration decisions, testing, data validation, and release readiness so ERP capabilities meet financial-accounting needs.
  • Strengthen data quality and controls by investigating process and data issues, partnering with stakeholders to resolve root causes, and helping maintain reliable handoffs, reconciliations, and documentation.
  • Enable change adoption by developing process documentation, job aids, and training materials that help accounting colleagues understand and consistently use new workflows and tools.
  • Support close and reporting readiness by coordinating process improvements with the accounting calendar and ensuring changes are tested, communicated, and implemented without disrupting critical reporting obligations.
  • Measure process performance by maintaining process metrics, issue logs, and improvement recommendations that help the Controller and accounting leaders prioritize work and assess results.
  • Collaborate across teams by serving as a trusted accounting-process partner to Financial Accounting, FP&A, Technology, Internal Audit, and vendors, bringing clear requirements and disciplined follow-through to shared initiatives.

The Skills and Experience You Bring

  • 3-5 years of experience in financial accounting, accounting operations, finance systems, audit, consulting, or a comparable environment that combines accounting knowledge with process improvement.
  • Working knowledge of U.S. GAAP, core financial-accounting processes, internal controls, and the close and reporting cycle.
  • Experience documenting business processes, gathering requirements, testing changes, and translating stakeholder needs into usable process or system improvements.
  • Experience working with ERP, financial-reporting, workflow, or reconciliation tools; familiarity with platforms such as Workday, Oracle, SAP, BlackLine, Alteryx, or comparable tools is welcome.

  • Ability to use data, automation, and AI-enabled tools responsibly, with attention to data governance, source validation, access controls, and human review.

job.title: Senior Product Manager, Subscriptions
job.description:
Join the future of news

We’re on a mission to deliver riveting storytelling for all of America. At The Washington Post, you’ll help reinvent news. Our work is driven by a deep investigative spirit and enhanced by innovation to bring audiences closer to the stories that matter most.


About Our Team


The Washington Post is powered by the passion and talent of our people. It takes all of us to reinvent news. Beyond our award-winning News and Opinions teams, we work across many departments, including Brand & Events, Communications, Customer Care, Engineering & Product, Finance, Human Resources, Legal, Marketing & Advertising, Print Operations, and Sales.


Why This Role Matters

 

The Washington Post is seeking a Senior Product Manager, Subscriptions. Our product team shapes how readers discover our subscription, decide to join, and build habits as long-term subscribers. We own the flows people move through on the way to becoming a subscriber, and we work closely with our subscriptions marketing team to bring new readers in.

 

The Senior Product Manager, Subscriptions, leads a cross-functional team focused on turning unknown users into known users, and known users into paying subscribers. You will dig into how people behave, find the spots where they hesitate or drop off, and turn what you learn into a clear roadmap. You will also work with our revenue science team on the models that help us show the right offer to the right user at the right time.


What Motivates You

  • You get energized by the puzzle of why people choose to subscribe and what makes them stay.
  • You like working across teams and are good at turning ideas from marketing, design, data science, and engineering into something everyone can build toward.
  • You're curious about customers. You want to understand what they need, where they get stuck, and what would make the experience feel easy.
  • You care about the mission and values of the organization and bring determination and good organization to the work.

How You'll Support the Mission

  • Own the roadmap for conversion and acquisition flows, from a reader's first visit through registration, checkout, and early onboarding.
  • Develop strategies that move unknown users to known users and known users to payers.
  • Partner with the revenue science team on the models and testing that inform which offer reaches which user, and when.
  • Partner closely with the subscriptions marketing team to plan and launch experiments and campaigns that bring in new subscribers.·       Work with Engineering, Design, Marketing, Analytics, and QA to ship high quality products on a steady rhythm.
  • Write clear requirements and prioritize features against our acquisition and revenue goals.
  • Use A/B testing and other experimentation to learn what works, then apply it to the next round of improvements.
  • Spot roadblocks early and clear them before they slow the team down.
  • Share updates, risks, and new opportunities with leadership on a regular basis.
  • Keep up with trends in subscription products, conversion optimization, and consumer behavior.

The Skills and Experience You Bring


Minimum Qualifications

  • 5+ years of product management experience, preferably in digital subscriptions.
  • Experience improving conversion funnels or acquisition flows, ideally in a B2C digital subscription product. This is a strong plus.·      
  • Experience using data to inform decisions, including a track record of running experiments and combining numbers with customer feedback to decide what to build.
  • Comfort working with data science or analytics partners on models and personalization, even if you aren't building the models yourself.
  • A collaborative style and the ability to build good working relationships with marketing, design, engineering, and analytics partners.    
  • Strong attention to detail, and the ability to juggle several projects in a fast-moving environment.    
  • Excellent communication skills, including the ability to explain complex ideas and share results with people at every level of the company.
  • Experience working with research and design teams to run qualitative studies and turn what you learn into product improvements.  
  • Media experience is welcome and not required.

 

Collaboration makes us stronger. That’s why our offices are designed with open layouts, modern technology, and easy access to transportation. With certain exceptions for newsgathering and business travel, we work on-site five days a week.

Compensation and Benefits

Wherever you are in your life or career, The Washington Post offers comprehensive and inclusive benefits for every step of your journey:

  • Competitive medical, dental and vision coverage

  • Company-paid pension and 401(k) match

  • Three weeks of vacation and up to three weeks of paid sick leave

  • Nine paid holidays and two personal days

  • 20 weeks paid parental leave for any new parent

  • Robust mental health resources

  • Backup care and caregiver concierge services

  • Gender affirming services

  • Pet insurance

  • Free Post digital subscription

  • Leadership and career development programs

Benefits may vary based on the job, full-time or part-time schedule, location, and collectively bargained status.

The salary range for this position is:

$119,700 - $199,300 Annual

The actual salary within this range will depend on individual skills, experience, and qualifications as they relate to specific job requirements. This position may be eligible for a bonus or incentive program, and a member of the Talent Acquisition team will discuss bonus payment terms and conditions during the interview process.

job.title: Senior Systems Engineer
job.description:
Join the future of news

We’re on a mission to deliver riveting storytelling for all of America. At The Washington Post, you’ll help reinvent news. Our work is driven by a deep investigative spirit and enhanced by innovation to bring audiences closer to the stories that matter most.


About Our Team


The Washington Post is powered by the passion and talent of our people. It takes all of us to reinvent news. Beyond our award-winning News and Opinions teams, we work across many departments, including Brand & Events, Communications, Customer Care, Engineering & Product, Finance, Human Resources, Legal, Marketing & Advertising, Print Operations, and Sales.


Why This Role Matters

 

  • The Senior Systems Engineer helps keep The Washington Post’s identity, collaboration, endpoint, and core IT service platforms secure, reliable, and available.
  • This role serves as a senior technical resource for Identity and Access Management, supporting Active Directory, Okta, single sign-on, and automated user-lifecycle processes.
  • Through hands-on systems engineering, administration, integration, and automation, this role improves the reliability and efficiency of technology services used across the organization.
  • Working with IT Operations, Cybersecurity, Legal, Compliance, HR, and other partners, this role helps translate operational and security requirements into practical technical solutions.
  • As an individual contributor, this role provides technical guidance and project leadership but does not have formal people-management responsibilities.

What Motivates You

  • You enjoy solving complex systems and infrastructure problems through careful analysis and hands-on technical work.
  • You are interested in identity management, enterprise platforms, automation, and secure service delivery.
  • You look for practical ways to reduce manual work, improve reliability, and strengthen operational controls.
  • You take pride in building solutions that are documented, supportable, and sustainable for the broader team.
  • You are comfortable responding to immediate operational needs while continuing to improve the underlying systems and processes.
  • You enjoy collaborating with cybersecurity professionals, administrators, engineers, and business partners to solve shared problems.
  • You value sharing your knowledge and helping colleagues develop their technical capabilities.

How You’ll Support the Mission

  • Administer and improve Identity and Access Management services, including Active Directory, Okta, single sign-on, multifactor authentication, and role-based access, supporting secure and reliable access to enterprise systems.
  • Design and implement automated provisioning, deprovisioning, and access-change workflows within established security and platform standards, improving the accuracy and timeliness of identity administration.
  • Develop and maintain integrations among platforms such as Workday, Okta, Active Directory, Google Workspace, Proofpoint, and ServiceNow, improving the consistency of data and service workflows.
  • Engineer and support assigned enterprise platforms, which may include Google Workspace, storage and collaboration services, endpoint-management tools, asset-management systems, and ITSM platforms, maintaining reliable day-to-day operations.
  • Use APIs, scripting, and systems-management tools to automate recurring administrative and operational processes, reducing manual effort and preventable errors.
  • Troubleshoot complex incidents involving identity, access, integrations, endpoints, systems administration, and enterprise applications, restoring service and identifying corrective actions.
  • Partner with Cybersecurity and Compliance to implement approved security configurations, access controls, and remediation plans, reducing identity and infrastructure risk.
  • Support the technical implementation of data-retention requirements, legal holds, and e-discovery requests in partnership with Legal, Cybersecurity, and designated data owners, ensuring requests are executed accurately and securely.
  • Contribute technical expertise to system upgrades, platform changes, integration projects, and service improvements, helping projects meet operational, security, and delivery requirements.
  • Maintain system documentation, technical procedures, integration records, and operational runbooks, improving service continuity and reducing reliance on individual knowledge.
  • Recommend improvements to system configurations, workflows, and working methods, strengthening the effectiveness and reliability of the IT Operations team.
  • Provide technical guidance, cross-training, and mentoring to engineers and administrators, helping colleagues resolve issues and work effectively within established standards.

The Skills and Experience You Bring

  • Five or more years of relevant experience in systems engineering, systems administration, enterprise infrastructure, Identity and Access Management, or a related discipline.
  • Advanced knowledge of Active Directory, Okta, SSO integrations, multifactor authentication, access provisioning, and role-based access controls.
  • Experience administering Google Workspace in a large or complex environment, including experience with the Google Admin SDK, OAuth, and service accounts.
  • Hands-on experience integrating enterprise systems, SaaS applications, IAM tools, HR platforms, or IT service-management platforms.
  • Proficiency in at least one relevant scripting language, such as Python, JavaScript, Bash, PowerShell, or Google Apps Script.
  • Experience working with REST APIs and troubleshooting system-to-system integrations.
  • Practical experience implementing identity, endpoint, configuration, or access controls in partnership with cybersecurity or compliance teams.
  • Experience supporting ITSM, CMDB, asset-management, endpoint-management, storage, or enterprise collaboration platforms.
  • Strong troubleshooting and analytical skills, including the ability to identify root causes and resolve issues involving multiple systems.
  • Ability to manage assigned projects and technical work independently while recognizing when decisions or risks require escalation.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical issues and recommendations to technical and nontechnical stakeholders.
  • Experience creating technical documentation, operational procedures, and support runbooks.
  • Ability to provide technical guidance and mentoring without formal supervisory authority.
  • Experience with infrastructure as code, version control, automated testing, CI/CD, or other modern systems-engineering practices is preferred.
  • Experience supporting legal holds, e-discovery, data retention, or information-governance processes is preferred.
  • A bachelor’s degree in information systems, computer science, engineering, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education, certifications, training, and practical experience.

 

Collaboration makes us stronger. That’s why our offices are designed with open layouts, modern technology, and easy access to transportation. With certain exceptions for newsgathering and business travel, we work on-site five days a week.

Compensation and Benefits

Wherever you are in your life or career, The Washington Post offers comprehensive and inclusive benefits for every step of your journey:

  • Competitive medical, dental and vision coverage

  • Company-paid pension and 401(k) match

  • Three weeks of vacation and up to three weeks of paid sick leave

  • Nine paid holidays and two personal days

  • 20 weeks paid parental leave for any new parent

  • Robust mental health resources

  • Backup care and caregiver concierge services

  • Gender affirming services

  • Pet insurance

  • Free Post digital subscription

  • Leadership and career development programs

Benefits may vary based on the job, full-time or part-time schedule, location, and collectively bargained status.

The salary range for this position is:

$108,700 - $181,100 Annual

The actual salary within this range will depend on individual skills, experience, and qualifications as they relate to specific job requirements. This position may be eligible for a bonus or incentive program, and a member of the Talent Acquisition team will discuss bonus payment terms and conditions during the interview process.

job.title: Weber Shandwick Careers
job.description: About Weber Shandwick Who are we? Weber Shandwick is one of the world’s leading PR and communications agencies, with a presence in 115 cities across six continents, including 13 in the Middle East. We’ve been voted PRWeek Global Best Agency in Middle East (2020), PRCA MENA Large Consultancy of the Year (2022, 2021) and PRCA MENA Digital Team of the Year (2022, 2021, 2020). In addition, we’ve been certified as a Great Place to Work® UAE | Turkey (2022). Our team comprises social media experts, digital specialists, creatives, strategists, analysts and PR professionals who believe in the power of collaboration to deliver high-value, high-impact communications and business solutions for our clients. By welcoming outstanding and diverse talents to our team, we complement our sector expertise with specialisms such as content, content production, creative design, creative technology, digital platforms, influencer marketing, integrated media, media relations, social strategy and engagement, strategic planning, and video productions.
