APAC AI Media Orchestration Senior Director – Japan

 About the role Help shape how AI transforms media and marketing for one of WPP Media's key clients: Google. This newly created leadership role within Media Futures Group (WPP Media's bespoke agency for Google) brings together media expertise, practical AI delivery and organizational transformation. Based in Japan, you will help pioneer agentic workflows at scale for Google, connecting regional and global capabilities with the needs of the local market. Your remit is to turn AI ambition into everyday practice: identifying high-impact opportunities, piloting and deploying AI agents across live campaigns, developing solutions for Japan-specific needs, and helping teams adopt new ways of working. You will partner with senior client and agency stakeholders, cross-functional media teams, and APAC AI specialists to move successful experiments into repeatable, measurable solutions. We are looking for someone who understands how media works, brings strong practical fluency in generative AI, and can lead change from initial use case through deployment and sustained adoption.

What you’ll do
  • Lead AI adoption in Japan. Own the execution of the Japan market AI agenda, aligning local priorities with regional and global capabilities.
  • Deploy AI into live media workflows. Partner with strategy, planning and activation teams to identify opportunities, pilot verified agents, and embed successful workflows into campaign delivery.
  • Build and localize solutions. Architect, localize, test, deploy and maintain custom AI tools and agents that address Japan-specific business and workflow needs.
  • Enable teams and lead change. Deliver practical workshops, training and onboarding, while working with cross-functional leaders to overcome adoption barriers and embed new ways of working.
  • Advise senior stakeholders. Translate business challenges into actionable AI initiatives, clearly communicating opportunities, trade-offs and results to client and agency leadership.
  • Measure, govern and scale. Track adoption, quality, productivity and business impact; uphold enterprise standards for responsible AI; and share successful local innovations across the wider APAC network.
What we’re looking for
  • Substantial relevant experience across media strategy, marketing transformation, consulting, marketing technology or adjacent disciplines, with demonstrated leadership of complex initiatives.
  • Business-level or native Japanese and professional English—both essential.
  • Strong understanding of the media ecosystem, including how campaigns are planned, activated, optimized and measured.
  • Deep understanding of Japan’s media landscape, audiences and cultural context.
  • A track record of driving AI adoption across teams, with hands-on experience piloting or deploying AI workflows or custom agents.
  • Strong practical fluency in generative AI and AI agents, including familiarity with GenAI tools and large language models.
  • Working knowledge of prompt and context engineering, agent testing and evaluation, and responsible AI practices.
  • Proven success leading large-scale change or technology adoption across cross-functional teams.
  • Experience working with major global brands and influencing senior stakeholders.
  • Strong strategic and analytical judgment, with the ability to translate complex business needs into practical solutions and measurable outcomes.
  • Confidence working across local, regional and global teams in a fast-evolving environment.
Why this role is different This is an opportunity to help define how agentic AI becomes part of everyday media delivery for Google, one of the world’s most influential technology brands. You will help build the playbook for Japan: shaping priorities, piloting new workflows, developing local capabilities and turning successful use cases into solutions that can scale. The impact spans both the work and the people delivering it—improving how campaigns run while equipping teams to achieve more with AI. With dedicated Japan ownership and connections across APAC, you will have the opportunity to influence local delivery and contribute to a broader transformation.

job.title: Business Development Representative
job.description:
WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. 

We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. 
 
We work with the world's most valuable brands and have global reach across 100+ markets, with deep local expertise.
 
Our people are the key to our success. We're committed to fostering a culture of creativity, belonging and continuous learning, attracting and developing the brightest talent, and providing exciting career opportunities that help our people grow. 
 
For more information, visit WPP.com.
 

JOB DESCRIPTION

Position Summary

Bottle Rocket helps clients plan, build, and improve digital products, leading with defined, outcome-oriented offerings. The Business Development Representative (BDR) is the engine at the top of the sales funnel and a key driver of the company’s growth. This role owns outbound prospecting, turning a strong volume of leads into calls, calls into meetings, and meetings into new clients.

The ideal BDR is driven, tenacious, and a great active listener. They understand the front-end digital experience and the back-end that enables it. They can distill the needs behind a prospect’s business challenges, connect them to the right Bottle Rocket solution, and hand a well-qualified opportunity to the Business Development Executive team.

Essential Functions

  • Drive a high volume of outbound activity (calls, emails, LinkedIn outreach, and multi-touch cadences) to create a consistent flow of new leads
  • Convert leads into live conversations, and conversations into qualified first meetings booked for the Business Development Executive team
  • Own and consistently hit weekly and monthly targets for activity, conversations, meetings booked, and pipeline generated
  • Lead outreach with Bottle Rocket’s productized offerings, positioning each around the business problem it solves rather than a list of services
  • Spot buying signals in research and discovery calls, and connect them to the right Bottle Rocket services:
    • Strategy & Research (Experience Strategy, Research & Insights): unclear priorities, fragmented experiences, a new idea to validate
    • Design & Build (Design & Development, Experience Optimization): aging or low-rated apps, redesigns, falling engagement or conversion
    • Enterprise Engineering (Technical Modernization, Cloud Enablement, AI & Data, Application Engineering): legacy platforms, cloud migration, AI pilots, integration gaps
  • Research and build targeted account and contact lists in priority industries (Healthcare, Gaming, Hospitality, Financial Services, and QSR) with Business Development leadership
  • Qualify prospects on pain points, fit, budget, decision-making authority, and timeline, and hand off to Business Development Executives with clear notes and context
  • Partner with Marketing on go-to-market (GTM) campaigns for each offering, and share feedback on messaging, objections, and what is resonating in market
  • Prepare meeting agendas, follow-up emails, and other prospect communications
  • Keep activity, lead, and opportunity data accurate and current in the CRM
  • Track and report on funnel metrics: activity → conversations → meetings → opportunities → new clients
  • Work closely with Business Development, Marketing, and Product Strategy to align on GTM goals, KPIs, and metrics

Additional Duties and Responsibilities

  • Stay current on trends in digital products, AI, cloud, and tech modernization, and on the business priorities of target industries
  • Learn Bottle Rocket’s offerings, case studies, and delivery model well enough to speak credibly with prospects
  • Other duties as assigned

Qualifications and Education Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Marketing, Communications, Economics, or a related field
  • 2–3 years of experience (post-college) in an outbound sales role, such as SDR or BDR, selling Technology or Consulting Services, SaaS, software, or similar technology products or services
  • Related backgrounds are welcome, such as technology-enabled services, digital agencies, or IT consulting
  • Proven, measurable record of meeting or exceeding activity, meeting, and pipeline targets

Key Competencies

  • Driven and tenacious: persistent follow-up, energized by high outbound volume, and quick to bounce back from a “no”
  • Great active listener: asks sharp questions, listens more than talks, and picks up on what a prospect isn’t saying
  • Technical curiosity: recognizes buying signals across Technical Modernization, AI & Data, Application Engineering, and Cloud Enablement, and can discuss them credibly at a business level (an engineering background is not required)
  • Problem-first, consultative approach that leads with outcomes rather than feature lists
  • Competitive, goal-oriented, and metrics-driven; thrives on clear targets and a visible scoreboard
  • Strong written communication, with the ability to write concise, compelling, personalized outreach
  • Confident and professional communicating with Director, VP, and C-level executives
  • Highly organized; keeps high activity volume and multiple cadences on track
  • Coachable, with a growth mindset and the ambition to step up into a Business Development Executive role
  • Self-starter who works well independently and as part of a fast-paced, collaborative team
  • Experienced using Microsoft Excel and Apple Keynote (preferred) or Microsoft PowerPoint
  • Regular attendance at work is required for successful performance

Preferred Skills

  • Experienced with CRM software; Salesforce preferred
  • Experience with sales engagement tools; Salesloft preferred
  • Experience with prospecting tools such as LinkedIn Sales Navigator or ZoomInfo
  • Experience with video conferencing (Zoom or Teams) and call recording tools; Gong preferred
  • Uses AI tools to research accounts and personalize outreach
  • Exposure to software development, cloud, or data concepts through a prior role, coursework, or personal projects
  • Experience selling into Healthcare, Gaming, Hospitality, Financial Services, or QSR
  • Previous experience in an entrepreneurial, small-company environment

Supervisory Responsibilities

No direct reports.

Contacts with this Position

Works primarily within GTM teams (Business Development and Marketing) and with the Product Strategy team to stay aligned on offerings. Frequently works with potential customers in the earliest stages of the sales process.

Physical Requirements (the info from here to the end must remain for EEO reasons)

  • Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer
  • Lift and carry up to 10 lbs.
  • Dexterity
  • Clear speech in the English language                                     
  • Reach with hands and arms throughout day
  • Talk clearly
  • Hear within normal range
  • Stand, walk, and bend several times per day

Mental/Reasoning Requirements

  • Reading – Complex
  • Writing – Complex
  • Analysis/Comprehension
  • Judgment/Decision Making
  • Advanced Math skills

Vision Requirements

  • Good vision with color perception
  • Near vision – able to see details at close range

Working Conditions

The physical environment requires the employee to work primarily inside. The employee may be requested to work overtime and weekends for special program events.

job.description:
WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands.

Why we're hiring:

As a Data Steward in the WPP’s Enterprise Technology Data team, you will be responsible for the hands-on administration and maintenance of master data across one or more enterprise data domains. Reporting to the Global Programme Director - Data, you will be the first line of stewardship, ensuring that golden records are accurate, source system mappings are maintained, and data governance standards are consistently applied.

You will execute matching and mapping activities, triage stewardship exceptions, and support the onboarding of new source systems into the MDM framework. Your work will directly impact the trustworthiness and completeness of master data flowing through WPP’s enterprise platforms.

This role involves daily data administration including investigating and resolving match conflicts, maintaining entity mappings and hierarchies, classifying data assets, and supporting the operational processes that keep master data healthy across the enterprise.

You will be part of a Data Steward team led by the Global Programme Director - Data, with the opportunity to develop deep expertise in master data management, data governance, and stewardship at enterprise scale.

What you'll be doing:

Master data stewardship and golden record maintenance

  • Execute day-to-day stewardship activities including reviewing, approving, and correcting master data records in line with governance standards set by the Global Programme Director - Data.
  • Maintain and curate golden records, ensuring survivorship rules are correctly applied and master entities remain accurate and complete.
  • Investigate and resolve match conflicts, potential duplicates, and merge exceptions, escalating complex cases to the Global Programme Director - Data with supporting analysis.
  • Process new entity creation requests, validating source data against matching rules before golden record creation.

Source system mapping and onboarding support

  • Manage and maintain mappings between source system entities and golden master records, ensuring traceability and accuracy.
  • Support the onboarding of new agencies and source systems by executing mapping activities and validating initial data loads against MDM standards.
  • Maintain reference data configurations, ensuring code sets and lookup values remain aligned across source systems.

Data governance and classification

  • Apply data classification standards to master data entities as defined by the governance framework, covering sensitivity, confidentiality, and regulatory categorisation.
  • Review and correct AI-generated data classifications, providing feedback to improve automated tagging accuracy over time.
  • Follow and enforce stewardship workflows including exception handling, approval processes, and escalation procedures.
  • Maintain accurate documentation of entity mappings, transformation rules, hierarchy structures, and stewardship decisions.

AI-assisted stewardship operations

  • Act as the human-in-the-loop for AI-assisted matching and entity resolution, reviewing model-suggested matches, adjudicating low-confidence merge candidates, and approving or rejecting proposed golden record updates.
  • Review and validate AI-generated mapping recommendations during source system onboarding, ensuring accuracy before mappings are committed.
  • Provide feedback on AI model outputs to support continuous improvement of match accuracy, classification quality, and enrichment relevance.
  • Work with AI-driven anomaly detection alerts, investigating flagged records and determining appropriate stewardship actions.

Data quality monitoring and remediation

  • Monitor data quality dashboards and alerts, investigating exceptions and applying remediation actions in a timely manner.
  • Execute data quality checks across master data entities, documenting findings and tracking resolution through to completion.
  • Maintain and update data quality rules as business requirements and source systems evolve, under the direction of the Data Manager.

Operational reporting and team support

  • Provide first-line support for master data issues raised by downstream consumers and business users.
  • Contribute to operational reporting on stewardship volumes, exception trends, match rates, and resolution times.

Support data migration and reconciliation activities during source system onboarding and platform changes.

What you'll need:

  • Experience in a data stewardship, data administration, or master data management role.
  • Practical understanding of MDM concepts including golden records, matching, survivorship, and entity resolution.
  • Familiarity with enterprise master data management and data governance solutions (e.g. Informatica MDM, Informatica Data Governance) or equivalent platforms is desirable.
  • Proficiency in SQL for data investigation, validation, and reporting.
  • Understanding of data governance principles including data classification, ownership, and stewardship workflows.
  • Willingness to work with AI and machine learning tools as part of day-to-day stewardship operations, including reviewing AI-suggested matches, classifications, and enrichments.
  • Experience working with ERP or HCM data (Workday, SAP, Dynamics, or similar) is an advantage.
  • Attention to detail with the ability to identify and resolve data discrepancies methodically.
  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple concurrent stewardship tasks and priorities.
  • Good communication skills with the ability to document and explain findings clearly to both technical and business audiences.
  • Self-motivated with a proactive approach to identifying and resolving data problems.
  • Enthusiasm for developing expertise in master data management, data governance, and AI-assisted data operations.

job.description:

Why we're hiring:

We are seeking a skilled eDiscovery & Forensics Analyst to join our team on a 12-18 month contract, providing dual support across both eDiscovery and Digital Forensics 
functions. This role is ideal for a candidate who can bridge investigative technology with legal/compliance requirements, while also possessing a strong technical understanding of how breaches occur and how malicious activity can be traced, analysed,and reported.
The successful candidate will conduct forensic investigations, malware analysis, and eDiscovery searches, and will be responsible for producing clear, evidence-based reports and findings that can be presented to senior stakeholders to support business, legal, and security decision-making

What you'll be doing:

Conduct digital forensic investigations across endpoints and enterprise systems, identifying indicators of compromise (IOCs) and root cause of security incidents.

Perform malware analysis (static and/or dynamic) to understand behaviour, impact, and scope of compromise.

Use Magnet Axiom and NUIX to acquire, process, and analyse digital evidence, and to build clear, defensible reports of findings.

Conduct searches and investigations using Microsoft Purview (eDiscovery, Content Search, Audit) to support legal holds, HR investigations, and compliance requests. 

Perform audit log searches (e.g., Microsoft 365 unified audit log, Azure AD signin/audit logs) to reconstruct user activity, timeline events, and identify anomalous 
behaviour.

Support the eDiscovery team with data collection, search term development, and review workflows

Support the business with breach investigations, chain-of-custody documentation, and technical write-ups.

Translate complex technical findings into clear, concise reports and presentations suitable for senior stakeholders, legal counsel, and non-technical audiences.

Maintain detailed and defensible documentation throughout all investigations to support potential legal or regulatory proceedings.

Stay current on emerging threats, attacker techniques (TTPs), and forensic/eDiscovery tooling best practices.

Collaborate cross-functionally with Legal, HR, IT, and Security teams as needed.

What you'll need:

Essential Skills & Experience:

Hands-on experience in acquiring and preserving digital evidence, forensic artifacts, and forensic images across multiple operating systems (Windows, Mac and Linux) to 
support forensic analysis, and legal investigations.
Experience with forensic tooling such as Magnet Axiom, NUIX, FTK, or equivalent enterprise forensic platforms.
Solid understanding of how security breaches occur, common attack vectors, and adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs).
Experience conducting audit log analysis and reconstructing timelines from system/user activity logs.
Solid experience with Microsoft Purview (eDiscovery, Compliance, Audit Search)
Ability to produce clear, well-structured investigative reports for both technical and executive/non-technical audiences.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with keen attention to detail.

Desirable Skills & Experience:

Experience supporting both eDiscovery and forensics functions concurrently.
Relevant certifications such as surrounding Magnet/NUIX vendor certifications.
Understanding around Microsoft Azure
Prior experience presenting findings to senior stakeholders, legal teams, or regulators.
Scripting/automation experience (PowerShell, Python) to support investigative workflows.
Experience with Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (MDE).

A candidate who is naturally curious, detail-oriented, and comfortable operating in high-pressure investigative environments. Someone who can flex between the technical depth required for malware/forensic analysis and the structured, defensible process needed for eDiscovery — while communicating findings confidently to senior  leadership

Finance Director - Burson

Reporting to: Norway and Sweden Market Leader & EMEA CFO

Location: Sweden

 

Who we are:
Burson is the global communications leader built to create value for clients through reputation. With highly specialized teams, industry-leading technologies and breakthrough creative, we help brands and businesses redefine reputation as a competitive advantage so they can lead today and into the future. When you work at Burson, you are part of a global community of lifelong learners who thrive at the edge of innovation.

Burson is part of WPP (LSE/NYSE: WPP), the creative transformation company. For more information visit bursonglobal.com and follow us on LinkedIn and Instagram.

More About the role

Burson is seeking a commercially focused Finance Director, to lead finance across our Swedish market, with oversight of Norway. This is a senior market finance leadership role, partnering closely with local and regional leadership to drive financial performance, strengthen operational discipline and support sustainable growth across the two markets.

The role will be responsible for financial planning, reporting, forecasting, controls, compliance and commercial finance support across a business of approximately $10m revenue. It requires someone who can operate strategically, but who is also comfortable being close to the detail in a smaller market environment.

We are looking for a pragmatic, hands-on and commercially astute finance leader who can provide clear insight, challenge and counsel to leadership teams, while ensuring strong governance, accurate reporting and effective financial management.

 

What you’ll do:

  • Lead finance across Sweden and Norway, ensuring strong financial management, governance and commercial discipline across both markets.
  • Act as a trusted finance partner to both market leadership, providing clear insight, challenge and counsel to support business performance and decision-making.
  • Own the budgeting, forecasting and planning processes, ensuring alignment with local market priorities, regional expectations and group reporting requirements.
  • Provide accurate, timely and meaningful financial reporting, including revenue, profitability, margin, cost management, cash flow and working capital performance.
  • Translate financial data into clear commercial insight, identifying trends, risks and opportunities that help leaders make informed decisions.
  • Partner with client and business leads on pricing, profitability, resourcing and commercial decision-making to support sustainable growth.
  • Oversee month-end, quarter-end and year-end close processes, working closely with local, regional, shared service and group finance teams.
  • Ensure the integrity of financial records, reporting and controls, maintaining compliance with Burson/WPP policies and relevant Swedish and Norwegian requirements.
  • Lead on audit, tax, statutory reporting and external advisor relationships, ensuring deadlines are met and risks are managed effectively.
  • Drive improvements in finance processes, systems and ways of working, creating greater consistency, efficiency and accountability across the markets.
  • Support strong operational discipline around revenue recognition, billing, collections, approvals and project financial management.
  • Lead, support and develop the local finance function, building strong relationships across a matrixed, international environment.

Experience You’ll Bring:

  • Significant experience in senior finance, financial control, Financial Planning & Analysis or commercial finance roles, ideally within a professional services, communications, consulting, agency or matrixed international environment.
  • Strong understanding of financial management within a smaller or mid-sized market, with the ability to balance strategic input with hands-on delivery.
  • Proven experience partnering with senior leaders to improve financial performance, commercial discipline and operational decision-making.
  • Strong budgeting, forecasting, reporting, variance analysis and performance management experience.
  • Good understanding of accounting, controls, audit, tax and compliance requirements across Sweden; exposure to Norway or wider Nordic markets would be advantageous.
  • Experience working with regional or group finance teams, ideally in an international network or multinational organisation.
  • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to interpret complex financial information and turn it into clear, actionable insight.
  • High level of integrity, sound judgement and confidence in providing constructive challenge.
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to influence senior stakeholders and explain finance matters clearly to non-finance colleagues.
  • Fluent English is essential; Swedish language skills are highly desirable. Norwegian language skills or experience working with Norway would be an advantage.

Why we're hiring:

WPP is delivering a significant People Technology transformation, modernising the platforms, processes and data that underpin how we manage and support our people globally.

We’re looking for an experienced PMO Lead to sit at the centre of this transformation, bringing the structure, discipline and visibility needed to successfully deliver a complex, global programme. This is more than a reporting PMO role. You’ll create the governance, integrated planning and delivery controls that enable leaders to make informed decisions and teams to deliver effectively. You’ll connect multiple workstreams, make risks and dependencies visible, ensure actions translate into delivery, and provide a clear view of whether the programme is achieving its objectives and intended benefits.

Working across the intersection of People, Technology, HR processes, data and organisational change, you’ll partner closely with programme leadership, Workstream Leads and cross-functional teams to turn strategy into an executable plan and create the rhythm and discipline needed to deliver transformation at scale.

What you'll be doing:

  • Own and maintain the integrated programme plan, ensuring milestones, dependencies, deliverables and critical paths are clearly understood and actively managed.
  • Establish and maintain effective programme governance, providing appropriate control over scope, cost, timelines, risks and delivery.
  • Lead programme reporting, providing clear and insightful updates on progress, risks, issues, dependencies, decisions and areas requiring intervention.
  • Own the programme RAID process, proactively identifying risks and issues and ensuring clear mitigation, escalation and resolution plans are in place.
  • Coordinate dependencies across workstreams, ensuring actions have clear owners, deadlines and accountability through to closure.
  • Support and facilitate programme governance forums, ensuring decisions are captured and translated into clear actions and outcomes.
  • Establish and maintain the frameworks, processes, templates and programme documentation required to drive consistency and effective ways of working.
  • Ensure programme benefits are clearly defined, baselined and tracked, with appropriate business ownership and measurable outcomes.
  • Develop meaningful metrics and reporting to monitor programme performance and benefits realisation.
  • Partner with Workstream Leads and delivery teams to identify roadblocks, resolve delivery challenges and maintain momentum.
  • Provide leadership and guidance to project and workstream teams, championing strong programme management disciplines and collaborative ways of working.
  • Work across the wider organisation to identify interdependencies with other transformation initiatives and ensure these are reflected in programme planning.
  • Identify opportunities to simplify processes, improve operational effectiveness and strengthen programme delivery.
  • Champion effective ways of working across globally dispersed and cross-functional teams.
  • Act as Project Manager for selected strategic initiatives or workstreams where additional delivery leadership is required

What you'll need:

  • Significant experience working as a PMO Lead, Senior PMO, Programme Manager or in a similar role within a large-scale transformation environment.
  • Strong programme management capability, with hands-on experience of integrated planning, governance, RAID management, dependency management and executive-level reporting.
  • Experience supporting complex programmes involving multiple workstreams, geographies and cross-functional teams.
  • Experience delivering People Technology, HR transformation or enterprise technology programmes would be highly valuable.

job.title: Global Programme Director - CRM
job.description:
WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. 

We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. 
 
We work with the world's most valuable brands and have global reach across 100+ markets, with deep local expertise.
 
Our people are the key to our success. We're committed to fostering a culture of creativity, belonging and continuous learning, attracting and developing the brightest talent, and providing exciting career opportunities that help our people grow. 
 
For more information, visit WPP.com.
 

Why we're hiring:

WPP is embarking on a major, multi-year global CRM transformation to create a simpler, more connected and consistent approach to managing our clients and growth opportunities across the organisation. The programme will consolidate CRM platforms and processes, standardise core client, pipeline and opportunity management practices, and strengthen the data, integration and governance foundations needed to provide a trusted global view of our clients.

We’re looking for a Global Programme Director, CRM to lead this transformation end to end, turning our ambition into an executable global programme and bringing together business, technology, data, architecture and change teams across agencies and markets.

This is a highly visible leadership role for someone who can navigate the complexity of a federated global organisation, challenge legacy ways of working and drive the decisions, delivery discipline and adoption needed to establish a common global CRM capability.

What you'll be doing:

  • Own the global CRM transformation vision, roadmap and delivery strategy, translating strategic ambition into a clear, executable multi-year programme across agencies and markets.
  • Lead the consolidation and simplification of CRM platforms and processes, establishing a clear approach to global standardisation while managing legitimate local requirements.
  • Drive the adoption of common global processes across client and contact management, pipeline and opportunity management, forecasting, client planning and cross-agency collaboration.
  • Lead programme delivery across CRM product, architecture, data, integrations, security, testing, migration, cutover and deployment, working closely with Enterprise Technology and business leaders.
  • Ensure CRM integrates effectively with the wider enterprise technology landscape and that client, account, contact and opportunity data is structured, governed and managed consistently.
  • Own the integrated programme plan, governance, dependencies, RAID, assurance and stage-gate process, providing clear visibility of delivery confidence, risk, decisions, budget and benefits.
  • Define and lead the global deployment, business readiness and adoption strategy, sequencing agencies and markets based on value, readiness, data quality and change capacity.
  • Establish robust go/no-go, cutover, hypercare and stabilisation processes to protect business continuity and ensure each deployment is successfully embedded.
  • Own the programme business case, budget, forecast and benefits framework, ensuring investment remains linked to measurable business outcomes.
  • Manage system integrators, CRM product partners and other third parties against clear deliverables, commercial commitments, milestones and quality expectations.
  • Act as the principal programme interface for executive sponsors and senior agency, market, technology and functional leaders, creating alignment and driving timely decisions.
  • Challenge complexity, local exceptions and assumptions that could undermine the global outcome, balancing business requirements with simplicity, scalability and long-term value.
  • Build and lead a high-performing, global matrixed programme team spanning programme management, product, process, architecture, data, testing, change and deployment.
  • Create an evidence-led delivery culture built on transparency, disciplined decision-making, early escalation and shared accountability for outcomes

What you'll need:

  • Extensive experience leading large-scale, multi-year global transformation programmes within a complex, matrixed or federated organisation.
  • Significant experience delivering major enterprise CRM transformation, ideally involving platforms such as Salesforce or Microsoft Dynamics 365.
  • A strong understanding of how CRM transformation connects technology, business process, operating model, data and organisational change, rather than treating CRM as simply a technology implementation.
  • Experience consolidating fragmented platforms or processes and establishing greater global standardisation across multiple businesses, markets or geographies.
  • Strong programme leadership across areas such as architecture, integration, master data, data migration, testing, security, deployment and business readiness.
  • A proven track record of managing complex programme governance, integrated plans, interdependencies, risks, stage gates and executive-level assurance.
  • Strong commercial and financial capability, including ownership of significant programme budgets, business cases, forecasting, benefits realisation and vendor performance.
  • Experience managing system integrators, software providers and strategic delivery partners in complex enterprise environments.
  • Exceptional senior stakeholder leadership, with the presence and credibility to influence executive sponsors, challenge constructively and secure decisions across competing priorities.
  • Experience leading large, geographically dispersed and matrixed teams across business and technology functions.
  • Strong change and adoption capability, with experience embedding new processes and ways of working and measuring whether transformation has genuinely landed.
  • The ability to translate complex programme, technology and data issues into clear executive-level decisions, risks and trade-offs.
  • A pragmatic, resilient and outcome-focused leadership style, comfortable operating through ambiguity and making difficult decisions when delivery is at risk

Desirable

  • A recognised programme or project management qualification such as MSP, PgMP or PRINCE2.
  • CRM platform certification or deep delivery experience within an enterprise Salesforce or Microsoft Dynamics 365 environment.
  • Change management accreditation such as Prosci, or equivalent practical experience leading enterprise-scale adoption.

job.title: Governance Analyst
job.description:
WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. 

We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. 
 
We work with the world's most valuable brands and have global reach across 100+ markets, with deep local expertise.
 
Our people are the key to our success. We're committed to fostering a culture of creativity, belonging and continuous learning, attracting and developing the brightest talent, and providing exciting career opportunities that help our people grow. 
 
For more information, visit WPP.com.
 

Role Purpose

The Governance & Assurance Analyst supports WPP's governance, certification, assurance, and digital risk management activities.

The role helps maintain governance documentation, support certification and audit readiness activities, coordinate evidence collection, and contribute

to client assurance requests and governance reporting.

Working closely with Strategy & Risk, Technical Security Governance, Assurance, Privacy, Legal, Enterprise Technology, and business stakeholders,

the Governance & Assurance Analyst helps ensure governance processes remain effective, documentation remains current, and evidence required

for certifications, audits, and client assurance activities is readily available.

A key focus of the role is supporting the day-to-day operation of WPP's Information Security Management System (ISMS), maintaining certification

readiness, and coordinating governance and assurance activities across the organisation.

Key Responsibilities

Governance & Policy Support

Maintain governance frameworks, policies, standards, procedures, and related documentation.

Support periodic reviews and updates of governance artefacts.

Maintain mappings between policies, standards, controls, and certification requirements.

Assist with governance forums, working groups, and documentation reviews.

Support the preparation of governance materials, meeting outputs, and action tracking.

Provide research and analysis to support governance activities and decision-making.

Digital Risk Governance Support

Support governance reporting activities related to digital risk management.

Assist with the collection and analysis of governance-related metrics and indicators.

Maintain governance dashboards, scorecards, and reporting materials.

Track governance actions and follow-up activities.

Support reviews of governance processes and documentation.

ISO 27001 & Certification Support

Support the operation of the Information Security Management System (ISMS).

Coordinate activities required to support ISO 27001 certification and surveillance audits.

Maintain certification-related records, registers, and supporting documentation.

Coordinate evidence collection and stakeholder engagement activities required for audits.

Track audit findings, corrective actions, and improvement activities through to closure.

Support management review preparation and governance reporting.

Help maintain ongoing audit and certification readiness.

Client Assurance Support

Coordinate responses to client security, governance, risk, and compliance due diligence requests.

Collaborate with relevant stakeholders to gather information required for assurance activities.

Maintain reusable assurance content, responses, and supporting evidence.

Track assurance requests and response status.

Support the continuous improvement of assurance documentation and response quality.

Evidence Management & Audit Readiness

Maintain repositories used to support governance, certification, audit, and assurance activities.

Coordinate evidence collection across relevant business functions.

Ensure evidence is current, appropriately classified, and available for authorised use.

Maintain evidence ownership information, review dates, and supporting metadata.

Identify missing, outdated, or incomplete evidence and coordinate remediation activities.

Support internal, external, certification, client, and regulatory reviews through effective evidence coordination.

Reporting & Operational Improvement

Support the development of governance dashboards, scorecards, metrics, and reporting packs.

Analyse governance and assurance data to identify trends and reporting insights.

Support the standardisation of governance documentation, evidence collection, and reporting practices.

Identify opportunities for process improvements and raise recommendations to management.

Contribute to the continuous improvement of governance operational processes and reporting effectiveness.

Skills & Experience Required

Must-Haves

Fluent English, written and verbal.

Bachelor's degree in Information Security, Risk Management, Audit, Compliance, Business Administration, or a related discipline, or

equivalent relevant experience.

2-4 years of experience in governance, information security, compliance, audit, risk management, assurance, or a related discipline.

Experience supporting an ISO 27001-based management system, audit programme, or certification activity.

Understanding of governance frameworks, controls, audit principles, and certification requirements.

Experience supporting audits, assurance reviews, or certification activities.

Experience coordinating evidence collection and documentation activities.

Strong reporting, documentation, and organisational skills.

Ability to work effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Strong communication and stakeholder coordination skills.

Ability to manage multiple priorities in a global environment.

Nice-to-Have

ISO 27001 Foundation, Lead Implementer, Lead Auditor, or similar qualification.

CISA, CISM, CRISC, CISSP, or equivalent certification.

Exposure to frameworks such as SOC 2, GDPR, NIS2, or similar.

Experience supporting client assurance or security questionnaire activities.

Experience using GRC, audit, compliance, or certification management platforms.

Experience within a large multinational organisation.

Key Behaviours & Competencies

Governance Awareness

Understands the importance of governance, accountability, and effective documentation in supporting organisational objectives.

Analytical Thinking

Uses structured analysis and evidence-based reasoning to support governance activities and reporting.

Quality Focus

Maintains attention to detail and supports high-quality governance and assurance outcomes.

Stakeholder Collaboration

Works effectively with stakeholders across business and technical teams.

Communication

Communicates clearly and professionally with a range of audiences.

Organisation & Planning

Demonstrates a structured approach to documentation, coordination, reporting, and action tracking.

Continuous Learning

Seeks opportunities to improve processes, skills, and ways of working.

Professional Integrity

Acts with objectivity, accountability, professionalism, and discretion.

What This Role Explicitly Does Not Do

This role does not:

Own governance frameworks, policies, or standards.

Own cyber security strategy.

Own enterprise risk management processes or risk registers.

Own Digital Risk Governance frameworks.

Make risk acceptance or risk treatment decisions.

Own technical security controls, security architecture, engineering, or operational security functions.

Perform incident response, vulnerability management, monitoring, or security operations activities.

Act as Internal Audit or provide independent assurance.

Own regulatory compliance programmes.

Serve as the accountable owner for ISO 27001 or certification outcomes.

Own the ISMS.

Design governance operating models or policy architectures.

Approve policies, standards, exceptions, or governance decisions unless formally authorised.

Replace the accountability of risk owners, control owners, policy owners, or business stakeholders.

job.description:

We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth.

Why we're hiring:

The Head of FinOps is a Senior Leadership role within the Business Platform Delivery Organisation accountable for WPP’s end-to-end FinOps capability, covering cloud and SaaS spend management, cost allocation, forecasting, optimisation, recharges and Ttechnology Support. The role leads the FinOps team as the primary point of support for cost visibility, reporting, recharge management, user guidance, and platform access across OpCos, projects and clusters.

Working closely with budget holders, the Cloud Hub, platform teams, ET Finance, and Procurement, the role will strengthen financial governance, improve spend transparency, resolve cost and recharge-related challenges, and embed FinOps best practices into Enterprise Technology decision-making. The role is also responsible for establishing a robust support model for Cloudability Premium and IBM Apptio, ensuring platform stability, effective service ownership, and driving continuous improvement initiatives to optimise cloud consumption and maximise value from technology investments.

 

What you'll be doing:

Key Roles and Responsibilities

FinOps Strategy, Governance & Leadership

  • Define and lead the enterprise FinOps strategy, operating model, governance framework, and roadmap for cloud, SaaS, and technology financial management.
  • Own the end-to-end FinOps function, ensuring effective cost allocation, recharge, forecasting, optimisation, financial control, and consumption transparency across the enterprise.
  • Lead and develop a high-performing FinOps organisation, establishing clear accountability, succession planning, and capability growth.

FinOps Platform & Product Ownership

  • Serve as the executive owner for FinOps Platforms such as IBM Apptio, Cloudability Premium, TBM Studio and associated solutions.
  • Define and drive the FinOps tooling strategy, ensuring platforms remain scalable, resilient, business-aligned, and continuously improved.
  • Own platform lifecycle management, support governance, adoption, and long-term sustainability.

Financial Management, Optimisation & Value Realisation

  • Lead enterprise-wide cloud and SaaS financial management, ensuring transparency, accountability, and effective stewardship of technology spend.

  • Provide strategic insight and recommendations to maximise return on technology investments and support business decision-making.

Reporting, Analytics & Data Governance

  • Lead the enterprise FinOps reporting and analytics capability, delivering accurate, timely, and actionable financial insights.

  • Establish reporting standards, KPIs, dashboards, and governance frameworks that enable informed technology and financial decisions.

Executive Stakeholder & Commercial Leadership

  • Act as the senior FinOps partner to Enterprise Technology, Finance, Procurement, Cloud Engineering, and business leadership.
  • Build strong cross-functional relationships to align technology consumption with strategic, operational, and financial objectives.
  • Lead vendor, commercial, and support governance for FinOps platforms and services, ensuring supplier performance, value realisation, and commercial effectiveness.

Risk, Control & Compliance

  • Establish robust financial controls, policies, and governance frameworks to ensure accuracy, auditability, compliance, and accountability for technology spend.

    • Strong knowledge on budgeting and forecasting process
    • Proven ownership of enterprise cloud and SaaS cost management, allocation, forecasting, recharge, optimisation and financial governance.

job.title: Head of Inclusion Partnerships and Industry Engagement
job.description:
WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. 

We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. 
 
We work with the world's most valuable brands and have global reach across 100+ markets, with deep local expertise.
 
Our people are the key to our success. We're committed to fostering a culture of creativity, belonging and continuous learning, attracting and developing the brightest talent, and providing exciting career opportunities that help our people grow. 
 
For more information, visit WPP.com.
 

ABOUT WPP

WPP is undergoing its most significant structural transformation in decades. Through Elevate28, we are moving from a holding company model to a single integrated operating company. The EVP WPP is building for the Elevate28 era is anchored on five dimensions – one of which is Inclusion & Belonging. This role ensures WPP shows up in the industry as one company and as a recognised leader in inclusive practice.

Within this transformation, WPP’s Inclusion & Impact (I&I) team is pioneering an innovative, enterprise-wide approach that moves decisively beyond traditional DEI. We treat inclusion as a strategic business enabler—designing and embedding scalable, measurable, and innovative practices directly into our business operations, creative work, client relationships, and workplace culture to shape meaningful behavioral change. This role ensures WPP show up across the creative, marketing, and media ecosystem as one unified company and recognized voice in inclusive practice.

ROLE OVERVIEW

The Head of Inclusion Partnerships & Industry Engagement is an enterprise-wide strategic, advisory, and ambassadorial leader who defines where and how WPP shows up globally for inclusion and impact. This role consolidates historically fragmented decisions into a unified WPP strategy—curating where we invest our brand equity, which strategic partners we ally with, which major industry stages we command, and which recognition benchmarks we pursue.

This is a brand positioning, external engagement, and strategically influential role, centered in inclusion. Operating at the intersection of brand reputation, industry engagement, and modern inclusion, you bring deep agency ecosystem fluency and the presence to build immediate credibility with senior executives, brand marketers, and cultural changemakers. You will establish rigorous investment criteria, steward a dedicated global budget, and serve as an articulate champion for WPP—shaping industry behavior, reinforcing client trust, activating diverse talent pipelines, and earning industry recognition.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  1. Strategic Inclusion Partnership & Investment Strategy (40%)
    Establish a criteria-led, enterprise approach to external alliances and partners.
  • Partnership Strategy: Set the global framework for identifying, assessing, and prioritising external inclusion partners, industry bodies, and community organizations – ensuring alignment to the Inclusion & Impact Strategy.
  • Sponsorship Governance: Build and lead an enterprise intake and evaluation model for global industry partnerships, transitioning legacy, ad-hoc agency investments into a cohesive, high-impact One WPP investment strategy.
  • Investment Allocations: Recommend annual allocations from the dedicated sponsorship budget based on strategic fit, audience, and expected impact. Spend tracking and vendor administration sit with P&C Operations and GBS.
  • Partnership Portfolio Leadership: Direct the overall partnership lifecycle – including renewals, tiering, strategic evolution – with guidance from the Inclusion Partnerships & Client Engagement Lead.

Key KPIs & Objectives:

  • Establish Partnership & Sponsorship Framework, with tiering, selection criteria, and an intake process for event and sponsorship requests.
  • Set an Annual Sponsorship Investment Plan recommended and approved within the allocated budget.
  • Consolidate Legacy agency-level commitments into high-yield, unified enterprise partnerships
  1. Industry Presence & Engagement (35%)
    Positioning WPP as a global growth partner centered on inclusion
  • Event Activation: Lead WPP’s inclusion presence at priority industry moments (e.g., Cannes Lions, Advertising Week, CES, Campaign, Adobe Summit), embedding I&I into mainstage programming, brand roundtables, and other engagements.
  • Frontline Ambassador: Serve as a representative, building relationships with partners, clients, and industry leaders across a range of settings and audiences.
  • Thought Leadership Curation: Translate progressive organizational practices into compelling public narratives; collaborate with Regional Inclusion Directors and MarComms to prepare, position, and amplify diverse executive voices, ERG leaders, and breakthrough creative talent on international stages.
  • Client Co-Creation & Alignment: Partner with client-facing agency leads and the Inclusion Partnerships & Client Engagement Lead to design joint, values-aligned thought leadership platforms and client-partner roundtables that deepen brand relationships.
  • Talent Pipeline Integration: Partner with Talent Acquisition to ensure global sponsorships and partnerships alliances actively generate pathways for emerging, diverse creative and strategic talent.

Key KPIs & Objectives:

  • Launch comprehensive Global Industry Activation Plan, that includes details on key messaging and objectives
  • Co-create diverse WPP Thought Leadership & Speaker Bureau.
  • Curate relationships with partners and clients to support business growth and inclusion client opportunities for ongoing engagement.
  1. Industry Recognition, Influence & Impact Measurement (25%)
    Earning recognition for WPP’s inclusive practices through industry benchmarks and measurable business impact.
  • Global Recognition Strategy: Define and lead the enterprise awards and recognition roadmap, identifying high-credibility global, regional, and industry inclusive benchmarks.
  • Integrated Benchmarking Process: Run a shared awards process with Regional Inclusion Directors, GBS team, and the Global Head of Inclusion & Impact.
  • Reputational Narrative Engine: Supply partnership, sponsorship, and award proof points to Talent Acquisition and Marketing & Communications to strengthen WPP’s reputation as an inclusive leader.
  • Impact Reporting: In partnership with the Enterprise Director, Inclusion, Brand, and Client Impact, own the End-of-Year Partnership Impact & ROI Report, using partner and client data provided by the Inclusion Partnerships & Client Engagement Lead.

Key KPIs & Objectives:

  • Unified Global Awards Strategy and submission process in place with Regional Inclusion Directors and GBS.
  • End-of-Year Partnership Impact & ROI Report.
  • Effectively communicate reach, engagement, and talent outcomes linked to sponsorship and partnership investment.

EXPERIENCE & PROFILE

  • Enterprise Strategy Experience: Significant senior leadership experience in communications, marketing, external partnerships, and/or modern inclusion strategy within complex, matrixed global organization.
  • Modern Inclusion Mindset: Passionate about evolving inclusion beyond legacy, compliance-driven HR definitions into an innovative, scalable practice that drives competitive advantage, creativity, and systemic change.
  • Partnership & Sponsorship: Track record shaping partnership or sponsorship strategy and recommending where budget should go.
  • Advertising & Agency Fluency: Familiarity with major cultural and industry moments (e.g., Cannes Lions, Advertising Week, CES), client marketing expectations.
  • Confident Ambassador: Natural connector, with experience working across various organizational levels and functions.
  • Strategic & Structured: Brings clarity to competing requests, sets criteria, and makes clear recommendations to senior leaders.
  • Collaborative Leader: Demonstrates high emotional intelligence and an inclusive, collaborative leadership style; proven track record of mentoring and elevating direct reports while influencing cross-functional peers across multiple geographies.

Who you are:

You're open: We are inclusive and collaborative; we encourage the free exchange of ideas; we respect and celebrate diverse views. We are open-minded: to new ideas, new partnerships, new ways of working.

You're optimistic: We believe in the power of creativity, technology and talent to create brighter futures or our people, our clients and our communities. We approach all that we do with conviction: to try the new and to seek the unexpected.

You're extraordinary: We are stronger together: through collaboration we achieve the amazing. We are creative leaders and pioneers of our industry; we provide extraordinary every day.

 

What we'll give you:

Passionate, inspired people – We aim to create a culture in which people can do extraordinary work

Scale and opportunity – We offer the opportunity to create, influence and complete projects at a scale that is unparalleled in the industry.

Challenging and stimulating work – Unique work and the opportunity to join a group of creative problem solvers. Are you up for the challenge?

job.title: IAM Engineer - SSO
job.description:
WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. 

We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. 
 
We work with the world's most valuable brands and have global reach across 100+ markets, with deep local expertise.
 
Our people are the key to our success. We're committed to fostering a culture of creativity, belonging and continuous learning, attracting and developing the brightest talent, and providing exciting career opportunities that help our people grow. 
 
For more information, visit WPP.com.
 

Why we're hiring:

The Senior Identity and Access security Engineer is responsible for governing who, and what, can access DTS systems, data, APIs, tools, workflows and AI-enabled capabilities.

This is a hands-on governance and control role, reporting into the SVP Security and Compliance. The role ensures that access across DTS is appropriate, auditable, reviewed, least-privileged and aligned with security, privacy, compliance and client commitments.

The scope covers traditional human access, external users, privileged access, service accounts, machine identities, API keys, tokens, dataset access, and the emerging governance of AI agents and agentic workflows.

The role will work closely with Architecture, Security, Product, Engineering, Infrastructure, Privacy, Legal/DPO, TechOps, Enterprise Technology and the ISMS and Risk Officer to ensure DTS has a clear and controlled model for access across platforms such as WPP Open, Choreograph, InfoSum, Open Intelligence, Resolve and related DTS capabilities.

 

What you'll be doing:

1. Identity and access governance framework

Define and maintain the access governance framework for DTS.

This includes:

  • Defining access governance standards, processes and control expectations.
  • Establishing how access should be requested, approved, provisioned, reviewed, revoked and evidenced.
  • Ensuring access governance covers internal users, external users, clients, partners, vendors, service accounts, machine identities and AI agents.
  • Aligning identity and access governance with DTS architecture, security, privacy, compliance and data governance requirements.
  • Ensuring access governance is practical for product and engineering teams to implement.

 

2. Access reviews and recertification

Own the process for regular access reviews and recertification across DTS.

This includes:

  • Defining the scope, frequency and evidence requirements for access reviews.
  • Coordinating access reviews for critical DTS systems, production environments, privileged roles, sensitive datasets, client-facing platforms and administrative tools.
  • Ensuring access review outcomes are tracked, remediated and evidenced.
  • Identifying stale, excessive, orphaned or poorly owned access.
  • Escalating overdue, high-risk or unresolved access issues through the appropriate governance channels.

 

3. Privileged access governance

Ensure privileged access across DTS is properly controlled, justified and auditable.

This includes:

  • Reviewing access to production systems, cloud environments, security tools, databases, CI/CD tooling, administrative consoles and sensitive platforms.
  • Supporting least-privilege, just-in-time and time-bound access models where appropriate.
  • Working with Cloud and Platform Security and Infrastructure to improve privileged access controls.
  • Ensuring privileged access risks are visible in the DTS risk register where required.

 

4. External user, client and partner access governance

Govern access for external users, clients, agencies, partners and vendors.

This includes:

  • Defining standards for external user onboarding, approval, permissions, expiry and offboarding.
  • Ensuring external access has a clear business owner and justification.
  • Supporting access governance across client workspaces, agency environments, partner integrations and shared collaboration areas.
  • Working with Product and Engineering to ensure tenant, workspace and client-level isolation is appropriately governed.
  • Tracking risks related to stale accounts, vendor access, partner permissions and external user overprivilege.

 

5. Service account, machine identity and API access governance

Govern non-human access across DTS systems and platforms.

This includes:

  • Defining standards for service accounts, machine identities, automation users, API keys, tokens, secrets and integration credentials.
  • Ensuring non-human access has clear ownership, purpose, scope, rotation, expiry and auditability.
  • Working with Product, Engineering, Cloud Security and Infrastructure to reduce unmanaged credential risk.
  • Ensuring service accounts and machine identities are included in access reviews.
  • Supporting stronger governance of API access, token issuance, credential lifecycle and integration permissions.

 

6. AI and agentic access governance

Define and oversee the governance model for AI agents and agentic workflows across DTS.

This includes:

  • Defining how AI agents are identified, permissioned, monitored, reviewed and revoked.
  • Ensuring agents have clear ownership, scoped permissions and auditable actions.
  • Defining which agent actions require human approval or additional control.
  • Governing agent access to APIs, tools, datasets, workflows, client environments and production capabilities.
  • Ensuring agents act within delegated authority and cannot exceed the permissions of the user, system or business process they represent.
  • Working with Product, Architecture and Security to ensure agentic workflows are designed with clear action boundaries.
  • Working with the Product, Application and Offensive Security Lead to test whether agent permissions and action boundaries can be bypassed.
  • Working with Privacy Engineering to ensure AI access models support permitted use, minimisation and data protection requirements.

7. Data access governance

Govern access to sensitive, client, partner and WPP-owned data across DTS.

This includes:

  • Defining standards for dataset access approval, review, revocation and evidence.
  • Supporting data classification from an access-control and security-governance perspective.
  • Ensuring access to sensitive data is role-based, purpose-based, least-privileged and auditable.
  • Supporting controls for cross-client, cross-market, cross-agency and partner data access.
  • Ensuring data access governance supports InfoSum, Open Intelligence, Resolve, WPP Open and other DTS data collaboration use cases.
  • Working with Privacy Engineering on data minimisation, permitted use, retention and privacy-by-design requirements.
  • Ensuring data access risks are surfaced through the DTS risk process.

 

8. Governance of access to tools, workflows and actions

Ensure access governance extends beyond systems and datasets into tools, workflows and actions.

This includes:

  • Defining governance for access to operational tools, workflow automation, orchestration systems, AI tools and administrative actions.
  • Ensuring high-risk actions are subject to appropriate approval, logging and monitoring.
  • Supporting segregation of duties across sensitive workflows.
  • Ensuring automated workflows and agents have clearly scoped authority.
  • Working with Security Operations to ensure high-risk access and actions are visible in monitoring and detection processes.

 

9. Auditability, evidence and reporting

Maintain clear evidence of access governance and support audit and assurance requirements.

This includes:

  • Producing access governance evidence for SOC 2, ISO 27001, client assurance, internal audit and risk reviews.
  • Working with the ISMS and Risk Officer to ensure access controls, reviews, exceptions and remediation actions are documented.
  • Reporting on access review completion, high-risk access, overdue actions and access control gaps.
  • Supporting client and audit questions related to identity, access, privileged roles, service accounts, AI agents and data access.
  • Ensuring access governance is repeatable, measurable and auditable.

 

Who you'll be working with:

The Senior Identity and Access Security Engineer will be accountable for:

  • DTS identity and access governance standards.
  • Regular access reviews and recertification.
  • Privileged access governance.
  • External user, client, partner and vendor access governance.
  • Service account, machine identity, API key and token governance.
  • AI agent identity, permission and action governance.
  • Dataset and sensitive data access governance.
  • Governance of access to tools, workflows and high-risk actions.
  • Access governance evidence for audit, compliance and client assurance.
  • Escalation of material access risks into the DTS risk process.

 

What you'll need:

The successful candidate will have:

  • Experience in identity governance, access management, IAM, security governance, GRC, data access control or platform security.
  • Strong understanding of least privilege, role-based access control, attribute-based access control, access reviews, privileged access and segregation of duties.
  • Experience governing access across SaaS platforms, cloud environments, APIs, data platforms or enterprise technology estates.
  • Knowledge of identity platforms such as Okta, Auth0, Keycloak, Azure AD / Entra ID or similar.
  • Understanding of service accounts, machine identities, API keys, tokens, secrets and non-human access governance.
  • Understanding of AI agents, agentic workflows, delegated authority and tool-access governance would be highly valuable.
  • Understanding of data classification, dataset access governance, privacy-by-design and audit requirements.
  • Ability to work across security, architecture, product, engineering, infrastructure, legal, privacy and compliance teams.
  • Strong organisational skills and ability to coordinate reviews, evidence, remediation and reporting.
  • Ability to translate complex access issues into clear risks, controls and practical actions.

 

Leadership expectations

The Senior Identity and Access Security Engineer is expected to:

  • Be structured, disciplined and pragmatic.
  • Bring clarity to complex access and permission models.
  • Challenge excessive, unclear or poorly governed access.
  • Work constructively with product and engineering teams to design workable controls.
  • Avoid creating unnecessary bureaucracy while ensuring access is properly governed.
  • Treat human, machine and agent access as part of the same control landscape.
  • Escalate material access risks clearly and early.
  • Support DTS in building a secure, auditable and scalable access governance model.

 

Success measures

Success in the role will be measured by:

  • DTS having clear identity, access and data access governance standards.
  • Regular access reviews completed on schedule with evidence.
  • Reduction in stale, excessive, orphaned or poorly owned access.
  • Stronger governance of privileged access and production access.
  • Clear ownership and review of service accounts, machine identities, API keys and tokens.
  • Defined governance for AI agent identities, permissions and actions.
  • Improved auditability of access to data, APIs, tools, workflows and production systems.
  • Better alignment between identity, security, privacy, architecture, product and engineering teams.
  • Material access risks being visible through the DTS risk register and Risk Review Board.
  • Increased confidence that DTS can answer: who or what has access to what, why, and when was it last reviewed?

job.description:
WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. 

We unite cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, world-class creativity, next-generation production, transformative enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel in a single company – powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform, WPP Open, to help our clients navigate change, capture opportunity and deliver transformational growth. 
 
We work with the world's most valuable brands and have global reach across 100+ markets, with deep local expertise.
 
Our people are the key to our success. We're committed to fostering a culture of creativity, belonging and continuous learning, attracting and developing the brightest talent, and providing exciting career opportunities that help our people grow. 
 
For more information, visit WPP.com.
 

 

Title: Lead Software Engineer

Level: Lead Engineer, Data & Technology Solutions

Location: Copenhagen

Reporting to: Director of Engineering

About Open Intelligence:

We are the Activation arm of WPP Open Intelligence. Our team builds the foundational data infrastructure and high-performance edge services that power WPP’s position in the market. With approximately one-third of all global media spend flowing through WPP, our platform operates at the core of this massive network-deeply integrated and adopted by the largest supply-side partners in the AdTech industry. Operating at our scale presents unique engineering challenges. Our edge services currently handle over 60,000 classification requests per second, while our contextual classification pipelines process 10,000 requests per second. With operations spanning the US, UK, and ongoing expansion into EMEA and APAC, our infrastructure continuously interacts with up to 98% of the population in our active markets. We are an engineering-led team focused on building robust, scalable, and highly reliable systems.

 

WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR

We are looking for a Lead Software Engineer who thrives on owning backend systems end to end — architecture, delivery, and the people who build them. You care more about sound software design, reliable APIs, and clear ownership than about any single framework or language.

You are comfortable setting technical direction for a squad, mentoring engineers, and turning product roadmap into shippable, versioned contracts. Hands-on when it matters, you design and operate services, partner integrations, and orchestration components in production — authentication, retries, idempotency, rate limiting, and the operational discipline that keeps live systems healthy. You are likely highly proficient in a backend language such as Python, Go, or Java/Kotlin, and experienced with cloud platforms, containers/Kubernetes, CI/CD, and production observability. Interest in infrastructure as code (e.g. Terraform), durable workflows, and AI coding assistants is a plus when it helps the team ship faster without lowering the quality bar.

Beyond the technical craft, you are a strong communicator who can explain trade-offs to engineers, Product, and non-technical stakeholders, and align sibling teams on interfaces. You take ownership of reliability and technical debt for the systems your squad runs, escalate blockers early with clear options, and are motivated by growing both the platform and the engineers who build it.

 

WHY ARE WE HIRING We are at a critical inflection point in our growth and need to scale our engineering team to tackle an expanding set of complex challenges. As the digital ecosystem evolves, we are actively developing and releasing a new catalog of privacy-preserving data products. These solutions are designed to scale advanced targeting capabilities while remaining uncompromising on our promise to protect user privacy.

To support this product evolution, our infrastructure is undergoing massive global expansion. By the end of this year, we will be fully operational across the rest of the EMEA and APAC regions. Concurrently, we are deepening our integrations to support even more of the largest supply-side partners in the AdTech industry. We are hiring because we need strong engineering talent to help us architect for this next order of magnitude in scale-ensuring our systems remain resilient, performant, and compliant as our global footprint and feature set rapidly expand.

 

WHAT YOU WILL DO:

· Lead an engineering squad: set technical direction, prioritize delivery, run design and code reviews, and grow engineers through mentoring and clear ownership.

· Own the architecture and health of activation and orchestration services — API, databases, partner gateways, internal integrations, MCP and agentic integrations.

· Partner with Product and sibling teams to turn roadmap phases into shippable, versioned contracts — not ad hoc

integrations.

· Drive API integration engineering: authentication, rate limiting, idempotency, retries, partial-update patterns, and runbooks as partner APIs evolve.

· Establish and uphold production standards — CI/CD, testing, observability, auditability, and safe release practices.

· Keep an end-to-end overview of how data flow through activation — what is live, what is in progress, and where dependencies or technical debt block the next phase.

· Contribute hands-on where it matters: critical paths, new gateways, framework foundations (e.g. tool registry, workflow runtime, guardrails hooks).

· Identify and address technical debt deliberately; balance speed with reliability for systems that support live campaigns.

· Share knowledge in design reviews, stand-ups, and cross-team forums; escalate blockers early with clear options.

· Stay curious about agentic orchestration, durable workflows, and AI coding assistants to improve how the team designs and ships software.

 

WHAT YOU WILL NEED

· Strong communication — you explain trade-offs to engineers, product, and non-technical stakeholders and align multiple teams on interfaces.

· 6+ years in software engineering with 2+ years leading engineers or owning a significant technical area (team lead, staff, or equivalent).

· Proven delivery of backend and API-centric systems in production — services, integrations, or platforms at meaningful scale.

· Solid experience building and operating REST/HTTP APIs and event- or workflow-driven systems (durable state, async jobs, or orchestration).

· Comfort owning third-party integrations — auth, errors, versioning, operational monitoring, and partner-driven change.

· Strong proficiency in at least one backend language (e.g. Python, Go, or Java/Kotlin) and sound software design (patterns, testing, code review).

· Experience with CI/CD, Git, and testing — unit, integration, and boundary/contract tests where APIs matter.

· Experience with cloud platforms (GCP, AWS, or Azure) and deploying services with containers and Kubernetes.

· Familiarity with infrastructure as code (e.g. Terraform) and production observability (metrics, logs, tracing).

· A track record of technical debt and reliability ownership — incidents, postmortems, and systemic fixes, not one-off firefighting.

· Interest in leveraging AI coding assistants and prompt engineering to improve team productivity without lowering the production bar.

 

NICE TO HAVE

· Experience leading delivery of orchestration, workflow, or agentic systems (tool registries, policy/guardrails, human-in-the-loop flows).

· Full-stack exposure — internal UIs or ops tools (e.g. change logs, escalations) backed by the same APIs you own.

· Familiarity with AdTech / MarTech — SSPs, DSPs, deals, audiences, or campaign activation terminology.

· Experience in a monorepo or large shared codebase with many integration surfaces.

· Awareness of data privacy and safe handling of sensitive data in distributed deployments.

· Prior work on audit trails or decision logs for high-trust or automated systems.

If you are ready to be at the forefront of the AdTech industry, shaping its future, and driving success for both our clients, we encourage you to apply and join our team.
